Paccaṃsenāti paṭilabhitabbena aṃsena, attano attano laddhabbakoṭṭhāsānurūpenāti attho. Saṃvibhajissāmāti dassāma. Sampādessāmāti sampādayissāma.

'And we shall know what has been done as done, and what has not been done as not done' means we shall know thus: 'It is proper to give this and do that for those who come after having worked the whole day, for those who come after having worked half a day, and for those sitting at home without work.' And regarding 'the strength and weakness of the sick': for if, when they are ill, one does not make their illness comfortable by giving them medicine, food, and so on, they may think: 'When we are well, these people make us do what they want. When we are sick, they do not even acknowledge our existence.' Thus, disaffected, they later fail to perform their duties, or do them badly. Therefore, it shows that you should train thus: 'Knowing their strength and weakness, we shall know what is to be given and what is to be done.' 'Khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyañcassa' means hard food and soft food for the people of the household. 'Paccaṃsena' means by the share to be received; that is, each according to their rightful portion. 'Saṃvibhajissāma' means we shall distribute. 'Sampādessāma' means we shall provide.

Adhuttīti [M 3.0020] purisadhuttasurādhuttatāvasena adhuttiyo. Athenīti atheniyo acoriyo. Asoṇḍīti surāsoṇḍatādivasena asoṇḍiyo.

'Adhuttī' means not being profligate, by way of profligacy with men and profligacy with liquor. 'Athenī' means not being a thief, not being a robber. 'Asoṇḍī' means not being a drunkard, by way of being a drunkard with liquor and so on.

Evaṃ suttantaṃ niṭṭhapetvā idāni gāthāhi kūṭaṃ gaṇhanto yo naṃ bharati sabbadātiādimāha. Tattha bharatīti posati paṭijaggati. Sabbakāmaharanti sabbakāmadadaṃ. Sotthīti suitthī. Evaṃ vattatīti ettakaṃ vattaṃ pūretvā vattati. Manāpā nāma te devāti nimmānaratī devā. Te hi icchiticchitaṃ [P 3.0249] rūpaṃ māpetvā abhiramaṇato nimmānaratīti ca manāpāti ca vuccantīti.

Having thus concluded the discourse, now taking the pinnacle with verses, he spoke the words beginning with 'yo naṃ bharati sabbadā'. Therein, 'bharati' means nourishes and looks after. 'Sabbakāmaharaṃ' means the giver of all sense-pleasures. 'Sotthi' means a good woman. 'She conducts herself thus' means she conducts herself having fulfilled this much duty. 'Manāpā nāma te devā' means the Nimmānaratī devas. For they, because they delight in creating whatever form they wish, are called both Nimmānaratī and Manāpā.

4. Sīhasenāpatisuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse to Sīha the General

34. Catutthe [V 3.0020] sandiṭṭhikanti sāmaṃ passitabbakaṃ. Dāyakoti dānasūro. Na so saddhāmattakeneva tiṭṭhati, pariccajitumpi sakkotīti attho. Dānapatīti yaṃ dānaṃ deti, tassa pati hutvā deti, na dāso, na sahāyo. Yo hi attanā madhuraṃ bhuñjati, paresaṃ amadhuraṃ deti, so dānasaṅkhātassa deyyadhammassa dāso hutvā deti. Yo yaṃ attanā bhuñjati, tadeva deti, so sahāyo hutvā deti. Yo pana attanā yena kenaci yāpeti, paresaṃ madhuraṃ deti, so pati jeṭṭhako sāmī hutvā deti. Tādisaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “dānapatī”ti.

34. In the fourth, 'sandiṭṭhikaṃ' means to be seen by oneself. 'Dāyako' means one who is heroic in giving. The meaning is that he does not stand on faith alone, but is also able to relinquish. 'Dānapati' means that when he gives a gift, he gives as its master, not as a servant, nor as a companion. For one who eats sweet food himself but gives others unsavory food gives as a servant of the gift-object, which is called a gift. One who gives the same as what he himself eats gives as a companion. But one who sustains himself on whatever is available, yet gives others sweet food, gives as a master, a senior, a lord. It is with reference to such a one that it was said, 'dānapati'.

Amaṅkubhūtoti na nittejabhūto. Visāradoti ñāṇasomanassappatto. Sahabyataṃ gatāti sahabhāvaṃ ekībhāvaṃ gatā. Katāvakāsāti yena kammena tattha avakāso hoti, tassa katattā katāvakāsā. Taṃ pana yasmā kusalameva hoti, tasmā katakusalāti vuttaṃ. Modareti modanti pamodanti. Asitassāti anissitassa tathāgatassa. Tādinoti tādilakkhaṇaṃ pattassa.

'Amaṅkubhūto' means not having become lackluster. 'Visārado' means one who has attained knowledge and gladness. 'Sahabyataṃ gatā' means having attained companionship, having attained unity. 'Katāvakāsā' means that because the action by which there is an opportunity there has been done, they have made an opportunity. And since that is solely wholesome, therefore it is said 'katakusalā' (having done what is skillful). 'Modanti' means they rejoice, they rejoice exceedingly. 'Asitassa' means of the unattached one, the Tathāgata. 'Tādino' means of one who has attained such a characteristic.

5. Dānānisaṃsasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse on the Benefits of Giving

35. Pañcame gihidhammā anapagato hotīti akhaṇḍapañcasīlo hoti. Sataṃ dhammaṃ anukkamanti sappurisānaṃ mahāpurisānaṃ dhammaṃ anukkamanto[M 3.0021]. Santo [P 3.0250] naṃ bhajantīti sappurisā buddhapaccekabuddhatathāgatasāvakā etaṃ bhajanti.

35. In the fifth discourse, 'he has not departed from the household life' (gihidhammā anapagato hoti) means he possesses the five precepts unbroken. 'He follows the Dhamma of the good' (sataṃ dhammaṃ anukkamanti) means he follows the Dhamma of the virtuous and the great ones. 'The virtuous associate with him' (santo naṃ bhajanti) means the virtuous ones—Buddhas, Paccekabuddhas, and disciples of the Tathāgata—associate with him.

6. Kāladānasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Discourse on Timely Giving

36. Chaṭṭhe kāladānānīti yuttadānāni, pattadānāni anucchavikadānānīti attho. Navasassānīti aggasassāni. Navaphalānīti ārāmato paṭhamuppannāni aggaphalāni. Paṭhamaṃ sīlavantesu patiṭṭhāpetīti paṭhamaṃ sīlavantānaṃ datvā pacchā attanā paribhuñjati. Vadaññūti bhāsitaññū. Kālena dinnanti yuttappattakālena dinnaṃ. Anumodantīti ekamante ṭhitā anumodanti. Veyyāvaccanti kāyena veyyāvaṭikakammaṃ karonti. Appaṭivānacittoti anukkaṇṭhitacitto. Yattha dinnaṃ mahapphalanti yasmiṃ ṭhāne dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti, tattha dadeyya.

36. In the sixth discourse, 'timely gifts' (kāladānāni) means gifts that are suitable, appropriate, and fitting—this is the meaning. 'New crops' (navasassāni) means the first crops. 'New fruits' (navaphalāni) means the first and choicest fruits produced from the monastery park. 'First establishes it among the virtuous' (paṭhamaṃ sīlavantesu patiṭṭhāpeti) means first giving to the virtuous and then consuming it oneself. 'Generous' (vadaññū) means one who understands what is said. 'Given at the right time' (kālena dinnaṃ) means given at a suitable and appropriate time. 'They rejoice' (anumodanti) means they stand to one side and rejoice. 'Service' (veyyāvaccaṃ) means they perform helpful actions with the body. 'With a mind without reluctance' (appaṭivānacitto) means a mind without regret. 'Where a gift bears great fruit' (yattha dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ) means one should give in that place where a gift has great result.

7. Bhojanasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Discourse on Food

37. Sattame [V 3.0021] āyuṃ detīti āyudānaṃ deti. Vaṇṇanti sarīravaṇṇaṃ. Sukhanti kāyikacetasikasukhaṃ. Balanti sarīrathāmaṃ. Paṭibhānanti yuttamuttappaṭibhānaṃ.

37. In the seventh discourse, 'one gives life' (āyuṃ deti) means one gives the gift of life. 'Beauty' (vaṇṇaṃ) means bodily beauty. 'Happiness' (sukhaṃ) means bodily and mental happiness. 'Strength' (balaṃ) means bodily stamina. 'Eloquence' (paṭibhānaṃ) means apt and ready eloquence.

8. Saddhasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Discourse on Faith

38. Aṭṭhame anukampantīti anuggaṇhanti. Khandhimāva mahādumoti khandhasampanno mahārukkho viya. Manorame āyataneti ramaṇīye samosaraṇaṭṭhāne. Chāyaṃ chāyatthikā yantīti chāyāya atthikāva chāyaṃ upagacchanti. Nivātavuttinti nīcavuttiṃ. Atthaddhanti kodhamānathaddhatāya rahitaṃ. Soratanti soraccena sucisīlena samannāgataṃ. Sakhilanti sammodakaṃ.

38. In the eighth discourse, 'they have compassion' (anukampanti) means they support. 'Like a great tree with a trunk' (khandhimāva mahādumo) means like a great tree endowed with a trunk. 'In a delightful place' (manorame āyatane) means in a pleasing gathering place. 'Those seeking shade go to the shade' (chāyaṃ chāyatthikā yanti) means those desiring shade approach the shade. 'Of humble conduct' (nivātavuttiṃ) means of lowly conduct. 'Not obstinate' (atthaddhaṃ) means free from the obstinacy of anger and pride. 'Gentle' (sorataṃ) means endowed with gentleness and pure virtue. 'Friendly' (sakhilaṃ) means amiable.

9. Puttasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Discourse on Sons

39. Navame bhato vā no bharissatīti amhehi thaññapāyanahatthapādavaḍḍhanādīhi bhato paṭijaggito amhe mahallakakāle [P 3.0251] hatthapādadhovana-nhāpanayāgubhattadānādīhi bharissati. Kiccaṃ vā no karissatīti attano kammaṃ ṭhapetvā amhākaṃ rājakulādīsu uppannaṃ kiccaṃ gantvā karissati[M 3.0022]. Kulavaṃso ciraṃ ṭhassatīti amhākaṃ santakaṃ khettavatthuhiraññasuvaṇṇādiṃ avināsetvā rakkhante putte kulavaṃso ciraṃ ṭhassati, amhehi vā pavattitāni salākabhattādīni anupacchinditvā pavattessati, evampi no kulavaṃso ciraṃ ṭhassati. Dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjissatīti kulavaṃsānurūpāya paṭipattiyā attānaṃ dāyajjārahaṃ karonto amhākaṃ santakaṃ dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjissati. Dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassatīti pattidānaṃ katvā tatiyadivasato paṭṭhāya dānaṃ anuppadassati.

39. In the ninth discourse, 'having been supported, he will support us' (bhato vā no bharissati) means: he who has been nourished and cared for by us with milk-feeding, helping his hands and feet to grow, and so on, will in our old age support us by washing our hands and feet, bathing, giving gruel and food, and so on. 'Or he will do our work for us' (kiccaṃ vā no karissati) means: setting aside his own work, he will go and perform the tasks that arise for us in the royal court and elsewhere. 'The family lineage will last long' (kulavaṃso ciraṃ ṭhassati) means: when sons protect our property—fields, land, gold, silver, and so on—without destroying it, the family lineage will last long; or, he will continue the ticketed food offerings and other alms we have established without cutting them off, and in this way too our family lineage will last long. 'He will take up the inheritance' (dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjissati) means: by conducting himself in a manner befitting the family lineage, making himself worthy of the inheritance, he will take up our property which is the inheritance. 'He will give an offering on our behalf' (dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassati) means: having made a transfer of merit, from the third day onwards, he will give offerings.

Santo sappurisāti imasmiṃ ṭhāne mātāpitūsu sammā paṭipattiyā santo sappurisāti veditabbā. Pubbe katamanussaranti mātāpitūhi paṭhamataraṃ kataguṇaṃ anussarantā. Ovādakārīti mātāpitūhi dinnassa ovādassa kattā. Bhataposīti yehi bhato, tesaṃ posako. Pasaṃsiyoti diṭṭheva dhamme mahājanena pasaṃsitabbo hoti.

Here, 'good and true men' (santo sappurisā) should be understood as good people who are tranquil through right conduct towards their parents. 'Remembering what was done before' (pubbe katamanussaranti) means recalling the kindness done first by their parents. 'One who follows advice' (ovādakārī) is one who carries out the advice given by parents. 'One who supports those who nourished him' (bhataposī) means he is a supporter of those by whom he was nourished. 'Praiseworthy' (pasaṃsiyo) means he is to be praised by the populace in this very life.

10. Mahāsālaputtasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Discourse to the Son of a Wealthy Brahmin

40. Dasame [V 3.0022] mahāsālāti mahārukkhā. Sākhāpattapalāsena vaḍḍhantīti khuddakasākhāhi ca pattasaṅkhātena ca palāsena vaḍḍhanti. Araññasminti agāmake padese. Brahāvaneti mahāvane aṭaviyaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

40. In the tenth discourse, 'great sāl trees' (mahāsālā) means great trees. 'They grow with branches, leaves, and foliage' (sākhāpattapalāsena vaḍḍhanti) means they grow with small branches and with foliage which is designated as leaves. 'In the wilderness' (araññasmiṃ) means in a place without a village. 'In a great forest' (brahāvaṇe) means in a large forest, a wild tract. The rest is clear in meaning throughout.

Sumanavaggo catuttho.

The Sumanā Chapter, the Fourth.

5. Muṇḍarājavaggo

5. The Chapter on King Muṇḍa

1. Ādiyasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Ādiya Sutta

41. Pañcamassa [P 3.0252] paṭhame bhogānaṃ ādiyāti bhogānaṃ ādātabbakāraṇāni. Uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehīti uṭṭhānasaṅkhātena vīriyena adhigatehi. Bāhābalaparicitehīti bāhubalena sañcitehi. Sedāvakkhittehīti sedaṃ avakkhipetvā uppāditehi. Dhammikehīti dhammayuttehi. Dhammaladdhehīti dasakusalakammaṃ akopetvā laddhehi. Pīṇetīti pīṇitaṃ [M 3.0023] thūlaṃ karoti. Sesamettha catukkanipāte vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

41. In the first discourse of the fifth chapter, 'benefits of wealth' (bhogānaṃ ādiya) means the reasons for acquiring wealth. 'Acquired through initiative and energy' (uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi) means acquired through energy which is called initiative. 'Accumulated by the strength of one’s arms' (bāhābalaparicitehi) means amassed by the power of one’s arms. 'Earned by the sweat of one's brow' (sedāvakkhittehi) means produced by causing sweat to fall. 'Righteous' (dhammikehi) means connected with the Dhamma. 'Righteously gained' (dhammaladdhehi) means obtained without violating the ten wholesome courses of action. 'Nourishes' (pīṇeti) means makes plump and substantial. The rest here should be understood in the same way as explained in the Book of the Fours. The second discourse is clear in meaning.

3. Iṭṭhasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Iṭṭha Sutta

43. Tatiye āyusaṃvattanikā paṭipadāti dānasīlādikā puññapaṭipadā. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Atthābhisamayāti atthassa abhisamāgamena, atthappaṭilābhenāti vuttaṃ hoti.

43. In the third discourse, 'the practice conducive to longevity' (āyusaṃvattanikā paṭipadā) means the meritorious practice of generosity, virtue, and so on. This same method applies to the remaining terms as well. 'Realization of the goal' (atthābhisamaya) means the attainment of the goal, that is, the acquisition of the goal.

4. Manāpadāyīsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Discourse on the Giver of What is Pleasing

44. Catutthe [V 3.0023] uggoti guṇehi uggatattā evaṃladdhanāmo. Sālapupphakaṃ khādanīyanti catumadhurayojitena sālipiṭṭhena kataṃ sālapupphasadisaṃ khādanīyaṃ. Tañhi paññāyamānavaṇṭapattakesaraṃ katvā jīrakādisambhārayutte sappimhi pacitvā sappiṃ vinivattetvā kolumbe pūretvā gandhavāsaṃ gāhāpetvā pidahitvā lañchetvā ṭhapitaṃ [P 3.0253] hoti. Taṃ so yāguṃ pivitvā nisinnassa bhagavato antarabhatte dātukāmo evamāha. Paṭiggahesi bhagavāti desanāmattametaṃ, upāsako pana taṃ bhagavato ca pañcannañca bhikkhusatānaṃ adāsi. Yathā ca taṃ, evaṃ sūkaramaṃsādīnipi. Tattha sampannakolakanti sampannabadaraṃ. Sūkaramaṃsanti madhurarasehi badarehi saddhiṃ jīrakādisambhārehi yojetvā pakkaṃ ekasaṃvaccharikasūkaramaṃsaṃ. Nibbattatelakanti vinivattitatelaṃ. Nāliyasākanti sālipiṭṭhena saddhiṃ madditvā jīrakādisaṃyutte sappimhi pacitvā catumadhurena yojetvā vāsaṃ gāhāpetvā ṭhapitaṃ nāliyasākaṃ. Netaṃ bhagavato kappatīti ettha akappiyaṃ upādāya kappiyampi na kappatīti vuttaṃ, seṭṭhi pana sabbampi taṃ āharāpetvā rāsiṃ katvā yaṃ yaṃ akappiyaṃ, taṃ taṃ antarāpaṇaṃ pahiṇitvā kappiyaṃ upabhogaparibhogabhaṇḍaṃ adāsi. Candanaphalakaṃ nātimahantaṃ dīghato aḍḍhateyyaratanaṃ, tiriyaṃ diyaḍḍharatanaṃ, sāravarabhaṇḍattā pana mahagghaṃ ahosi. Bhagavā taṃ paṭiggahetvā khaṇḍākhaṇḍikaṃ chedāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ añjanapisanatthāya dāpesi.

44. In the fourth sutta, “Ugga” (uggo) was so named because he was elevated by virtues. “Sālapupphakaṃ khādanīyaṃ” refers to an edible item made from rice flour mixed with the four sweets, resembling a sal flower. It is prepared by shaping it to have a visible stalk, petals, and filaments, cooked in ghee with spices like cumin, then having the ghee removed, filled into containers, scented with perfumes, covered, sealed, and stored. Wishing to offer it to the Blessed One during the mealtime, after he had drunk the gruel and was seated, he spoke thus. “The Blessed One accepted it” (paṭiggahesi bhagavā) is merely a teaching statement; the lay follower, however, offered it to the Blessed One and the five hundred monks. And just as that was prepared, so too were the pork and other items. Therein, “sampannakolakaṃ” means fully ripe jujube fruit. “Sūkaramaṃsaṃ” refers to one-year-old pork cooked with sweet jujube fruits and spices like cumin. “Nibbattatelakaṃ” means with the oil removed. “Nāliyasākaṃ” is a dish of nāliya greens made by mashing them with rice flour, cooking it in ghee mixed with spices like cumin, combining it with the four sweets, having it scented, and storing it. “This is not suitable for the Blessed One” (netaṃ bhagavato kappati)—here, it is said that on account of what is unsuitable, even what is suitable is not suitable. The merchant, however, had all of it brought, made a heap, sent whatever was unsuitable to the market, and offered the suitable goods for use and enjoyment. The sandalwood plank was not very large—two and a half cubits in length, one and a half cubits in width—but being an excellent heartwood item, it was very valuable. The Blessed One accepted it, had it cut into small pieces, and had it given to the monks for the purpose of grinding eye-ointment.

Ujjubhūtesūti [M 3.0024] kāyavācācittehi ujukesu. Chandasāti pemena. Cattantiādīsu pariccāgavasena cattaṃ. Muttacāgatāya muttaṃ. Anapekkhacittatāya cittena na uggahitanti anuggahītaṃ. Khettūpameti [P 3.0254] viruhanaṭṭhena khettasadise.

“Ujjubhūtesu” means upright in body, speech, and mind. “Chandasā” means with affection. In “cattanti” and so on, “cattaṃ” means given up by way of relinquishment. “Muttaṃ” is said on account of open-handed generosity. “Anuggahītaṃ” means not grasped by the mind due to a mind free from longing. “Khettūpama” means like a field in the sense of being a place of growth.

Aññataraṃ manomayanti suddhāvāsesu ekaṃ jhānamanena nibbattaṃ devakāyaṃ. Yathādhippāyoti yathājjhāsayo. Iminā kiṃ pucchati? Tassa kira manussakāle arahattatthāya ajjhāsayo ahosi, taṃ pucchāmīti pucchati. Devaputtopi arahattaṃ pattatāya taggha me bhagavā yathādhippāyoti āha. Yattha yatthūpapajjatīti tīsu vā kulasampattīsu chasu vā kāmasaggesu yattha yattha uppajjati, tattha tattha dīghāyu yasavā hotīti. Pañcamaṃ catukkanipāte vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Chaṭṭhasattamāni uttānatthāneva.

“Aññataraṃ manomayaṃ” refers to a mind-made divine body produced by jhāna-mind in one of the Pure Abodes. “Yathādhippāyo” means according to his inclination. What does he ask by this? It is said that in his human life, he had an inclination for the sake of arahantship; “I ask about that,” he asks. The devaputta, having attained arahantship, says, “Indeed, Blessed One, it is according to my inclination.” “Wherever he is reborn” (yattha yatthūpapajjati) means whether in the three kinds of family prosperity or in the six desire-realm heavens, wherever he is born, there he is long-lived and glorious. The fifth sutta should be understood in the same way as explained in the Catukkanipāta. The sixth and seventh suttas are clear in meaning.

8. Alabbhanīyaṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Alabbhanīyaṭhāna Sutta

48. Aṭṭhame [V 3.0024] alabbhanīyānīti aladdhabbāni, na sakkā labhituṃ. Ṭhānānīti kāraṇāni. Jarādhammaṃ mā jīrīti yaṃ mayhaṃ jarāsabhāvaṃ, taṃ mā jīratu. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Nacchādeyyāti na rucceyya. Abbuhīti nīhari.

48. In the eighth sutta, “alabbhanīyāni” means unobtainable; it is not possible to obtain them. “Ṭhānāni” means reasons. “Jarādhammaṃ mā jīri” means: whatever nature of aging is mine, may that not age. In the remaining phrases also, this is the method. “Nacchādeyya” means it would not be pleasing. “Abbuhī” means he removed.

Yatoti yasmiṃ kāle. Āpadāsūti upaddavesu. Na vedhatīti na kampati nānusocati. Atthavinicchayaññūti kāraṇatthavinicchaye kusalo. Purāṇanti nibbikāratāya porāṇakameva. Jappenāti vaṇṇabhaṇanena. Mantenāti mahānubhāvamantaparivattanena. Subhāsitenāti subhāsitakathanena. Anuppadānenāti satassa vā sahassassa vā dānena. Paveṇiyā [P 3.0255] vāti kulavaṃsena vā, “idaṃ amhākaṃ paveṇiyā āciṇṇaṃ, idaṃ anāciṇṇa”nti evaṃ paveṇikathanenāti attho. Yathā yathā yattha labhetha atthanti etesu jappādīsu yena yena yattha yattha ṭhāne jarādhammādīnaṃ ajīraṇatādiatthaṃ labheyya. Tathā tathā tattha parakkameyyāti tena tena tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne parakkamaṃ kareyya. Kammaṃ daḷhanti vaṭṭagāmikammaṃ mayā thiraṃ katvā āyūhitaṃ, svāhaṃ idāni kinti karomīti evaṃ paccavekkhitvā adhivāseyyāti.

“Yato” means at which time. “Āpadāsu” means in calamities. “Na vedhati” means he does not tremble, he does not grieve. “Atthavinicchayaññū” means skilled in the determination of cause and effect. “Purāṇaṃ” means, due to its unalterable nature, it is simply of the past. “Jappena” means by speaking of praise. “Mantena” means by reciting a mantra of great power. “Subhāsitena” means by speaking well-spoken words. “Anuppadānena” means by the giving of a hundred or a thousand. “Paveṇiyā vā” means or by lineage; the meaning is by stating the lineage thus: ‘This is a practice of our lineage; this is not a practice of our lineage.’ “Yathā yathā yattha labhetha atthaṃ” means: among these means such as chanting, by whatever means and in whatever place one might obtain the benefit of not aging, etc., for that which has the nature of aging. “Tathā tathā tattha parakkameyya” means: by that means, in that place, one should make an effort. “Kammaṃ daḷhaṃ” means: ‘The kamma leading to the round of existence has been firmly established and undertaken by me; what shall I do now?’—having reflected thus, one should endure.

9. Kosalasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Kosala Sutta

49. Navame [M 3.0025] upakaṇṇaketi kaṇṇamūle. Dummanoti duṭṭhumano. Pattakkhandhoti patitakkhandho. Pajjhāyantoti cintayanto. Appaṭibhānoti nippaṭibhāno hutvā. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

49. In the ninth sutta, “upakaṇṇake” means at the root of the ear. “Dummano” means having a distressed mind. “Pattakkhandho” means having drooping shoulders. “Pajjhāyanto” means brooding. “Appaṭibhāno” means being without ready wit. The rest is just as stated below.

10. Nāradasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Nārada Sutta

50. Dasame ajjhomucchitoti adhiomucchito gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā gahaṇasabhāvāya atirekamucchāya taṇhāya samannāgato. Mahaccā rājānubhāvenāti mahatā rājānubhāvena, aṭṭhārasahi senīhi parivārito mahatiyā rājiddhiyā pāyāsīti attho. Tagghāti ekaṃsatthe nipāto[V 3.0025], ekaṃseneva sokasallaharaṇoti attho. Iti rājā imaṃ ovādaṃ sutvā tasmiṃ ṭhito dhammena samena rajjaṃ kāretvā saggaparāyaṇo ahosi.

50. In the tenth sutta, “ajjhomucchito” means being extremely infatuated, having swallowed, having brought to completion, he is endowed with excessive, infatuated craving which has the nature of grasping. “Mahaccā rājānubhāvena” means with great royal power; the meaning is that, surrounded by eighteen armies, he went with great royal splendor. “Taggha” is a particle in the sense of ‘certainly’; the meaning is: it certainly removes the dart of sorrow. Thus the king, having heard this instruction and being established in it, ruled the kingdom righteously and justly and was bound for the heavenly world.

Muṇḍarājavaggo pañcamo.

The Muṇḍarāja Chapter, the fifth.

Paṭhamapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Fifty is finished.

2. Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ

2. The Second Fifty

(6) 1. Nīvaraṇavaggo

(6) 1. The Chapter on the Hindrances

1. Āvaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Āvaraṇa Sutta

51. Dutiyassa [M 3.0026][V 3.0026][P 3.0256] paṭhame āvaraṇavasena āvaraṇā. Nīvaraṇavasena nīvaraṇā. Ceto ajjhāruhantīti cetaso ajjhāruhā. Vipassanāpaññañca maggapaññañca uppattinivāraṇaṭṭhena dubbalaṃ karontīti paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā. Yā vā etehi saddhiṃ vokiṇṇā paññā uppajjati, taṃ dubbalaṃ karontītipi paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā. Abalāyāti pañcanīvaraṇapariyonaddhattā apagatabalāya. Uttari vā manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesanti dasakusalakammapathasaṅkhātā manussadhammā uttari ariyabhāvaṃ kātuṃ samatthaṃ ñāṇadassanavisesaṃ. Hārahārinīti haritabbaṃ harituṃ samatthā. Naṅgalamukhānīti mātikāmukhāni. Tāni hi naṅgalasarikkhakattā naṅgalehi ca khatattā naṅgalamukhānīti vuccanti.

51. In the first sutta of the second fifty: 'Āvaraṇā' (obstructions) are so called in the sense of obstructing. 'Nīvaraṇā' (hindrances) are so called in the sense of completely preventing. They ascend, overwhelming the mind, thus they are called 'overwhelmings of the mind.' They make weak both insight-wisdom and path-wisdom by preventing their arising; thus they are called 'weakeners of wisdom.' Or, because the wisdom that arises mixed with these is made weak by them, they are also called 'weakeners of wisdom.' 'Abalāya' means: to one whose strength is gone because of being enmeshed by the five hindrances. 'Uttari vā manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ' means: a special knowledge and vision capable of producing the state of a noble one, which is beyond the human qualities known as the ten wholesome courses of action. 'Hārahārinī' means: capable of carrying away what is to be carried away. 'Naṅgalamukhāni' means: the mouths of canals. For indeed, they are called 'naṅgalamukhāni' (plow-mouths) because they are similar to plows and because they are made by plows.

Evameva khoti ettha sotaṃ viya vipassanāñāṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, ubhato naṅgalamukhānaṃ vivaraṇakālo viya chasu dvāresu saṃvarassa vissaṭṭhakālo, majjhenadiyā rukkhapāde koṭṭetvā palālatiṇamattikāhi āvaraṇe kate udakassa vikkhittavisaṭabyādiṇṇakālo viya pañcahi nīvaraṇehi pariyonaddhakālo, evaṃ āvaraṇe kate vihatavegassa udakassa tiṇapalālādīni [P 3.0257] parikaḍḍhitvā samuddaṃ pāpuṇituṃ asamatthakālo viya vipassanāñāṇena sabbākusale viddhaṃsetvā nibbānasāgaraṃ pāpuṇituṃ asamatthakālo veditabbo. Sukkapakkhe vuttavipallāsena yojanā kātabbā. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ. Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

Herein, in the passage 'Evameva kho,' insight-knowledge should be regarded as like a stream. The time of releasing restraint at the six doors should be regarded as like the time of opening the plow-mouths on both sides. The time of being enmeshed by the five hindrances should be regarded as like the time when the water is scattered, dispersed, and spread all around, after an obstruction has been made in the middle of the river with straw, grass, and clods of earth by driving in tree stumps. When such an obstruction is made, it should be known that the time of being unable to reach the ocean of Nibbāna by destroying all unwholesome states with insight-knowledge is like the time when the water, its force spent, is unable to reach the ocean by dragging along grass, straw, and so on. In the case of the bright side, the application should be made with the opposite of what has been said. In this sutta, the round of existence and that which is free from the round are taught. The second sutta has a clear meaning.

3. Padhāniyaṅgasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on the Factors of Striving

53. Tatiye [V 3.0027] padhāniyaṅgānīti padhānaṃ vuccati padahanabhāvo, padhānamassa atthīti padhāniyo, padhāniyassa bhikkhuno aṅgānīti padhāniyaṅgāni. Saddhoti saddhāya samannāgato. Saddhā panesā āgamasaddhā adhigamasaddhā okappanasaddhā pasādasaddhāti catubbidhā. Tattha sabbaññubodhisattānaṃ saddhā, abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya āgatattā āgamasaddhā nāma. Ariyasāvakānaṃ [M 3.0027] paṭivedhena adhigatattā adhigamasaddhā nāma. Buddho dhammo saṅghoti vutte acalabhāvena okappanaṃ okappanasaddhā nāma. Pasāduppatti pasādasaddhā nāma. Idha okappanasaddhā adhippetā. Bodhinti catumaggañāṇaṃ. Taṃ suppaṭividdhaṃ tathāgatenāti saddahati. Desanāsīsameva cetaṃ, iminā pana aṅgena tīsupi ratanesu saddhā adhippetā. Yassa hi buddhādīsu pasādo balavā, tassa padhānavīriyaṃ ijjhati.

53. In the third sutta, regarding 'padhāniyaṅgāni' (the factors of striving): The state of exertion is called 'striving.' One who has striving is a 'striver.' The factors of a striving monk are the 'factors of striving.' 'Saddho' means: endowed with faith. Furthermore, this faith is of four kinds: faith from lineage, faith from attainment, faith of conviction, and faith of confidence. Therein, the faith of Omniscient Bodhisattas, because it has come down since their aspiration, is called 'faith from lineage.' The faith of noble disciples, because it is attained through penetration, is called 'faith from attainment.' When it is said, 'The Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha,' the settling down with an unshakeable state is called 'faith of conviction.' The arising of confidence is 'faith of confidence.' Here, 'faith of conviction' is intended. 'Bodhiṃ' means: the knowledge of the four paths. He has faith thus: 'It has been well penetrated by the Tathāgata.' This is indeed the head of the teaching, but in fact, by this factor, faith in the Three Jewels is intended. Indeed, for one whose confidence in the Buddha and so on is strong, their energy for striving succeeds.

Appābādhoti arogo. Appātaṅkoti niddukkho. Samavepākiniyāti samavipākiniyā. Gahaṇiyāti kammajatejodhātuyā. Nātisītāya nāccuṇhāyāti atisītalaggahaṇiko hi sītabhīruko hoti, accuṇhaggahaṇiko uṇhabhīruko, tesaṃ padhānaṃ na ijjhati, majjhimaggahaṇikassa ijjhati. Tenāha – majjhimāya padhānakkhamāyāti. Yathābhūtaṃ [P 3.0258] attānaṃ āvikattāti yathābhūtaṃ attano aguṇaṃ pakāsetā. Udayatthagāminiyāti udayañca atthañca gantuṃ paricchindituṃ samatthāya. Etena paññāsalakkhaṇapariggāhakaṃ udayabbayañāṇaṃ vuttaṃ. Ariyāyāti parisuddhāya. Nibbedhikāyāti anibbiddhapubbe lobhakkhandhādayo nibbijjhituṃ samatthāya. Sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyāti tadaṅgavasena kilesānaṃ pahīnattā yaṃ dukkhaṃ khīyati, tassa dukkhassa khayagāminiyā. Iti sabbehipi imehi padehi vipassanāpaññāva kathitā. Duppaññassa hi padhānaṃ na ijjhati.

'Appābādho' means: free from illness. 'Appātaṅko' means: free from suffering. 'Samavepākiniyā' means: with even digestion. 'Gahaṇiyā' means: with the fire element born of kamma. Regarding 'nātisītāya nāccuṇhāyā' (not too cold, not too hot): one with an excessively cold digestive fire is fearful of cold, and one with an excessively hot digestive fire is fearful of heat. For them, striving does not succeed; it succeeds for one with a medium digestive fire. Therefore, He said: 'majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya' (medium and suitable for striving). 'Yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikattā' means: one who shows one's own faults as they really are. 'Udayatthagāminiyā' means: capable of knowing and defining both arising and passing away. By this, the knowledge of arising and passing away, which comprehends the fifty characteristics, is stated. 'Ariyāya' means: purified. 'Nibbedhikāyā' means: capable of piercing the aggregates of greed, etc., which have not been pierced before. 'Sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā' means: leading to the destruction of that suffering which is destroyed because of the abandoning of defilements by way of substitution of opposites. Thus, by all these terms, only insight-wisdom is taught. Indeed, for a person without wisdom, striving does not succeed.

4. Samayasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Samaya Discourse

54. Catutthe padhānāyāti vīriyakaraṇatthāya. Na sukaraṃ uñchena paggahena yāpetunti na sakkā hoti pattaṃ gahetvā uñchācariyāya yāpetuṃ. Imasmimpi sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭameva kathitaṃ.

54. In the fourth sutta, 'padhānāya' means for the purpose of making effort. 'Na sukaraṃ uñchena paggahena yāpetuṃ' means: it is not possible to sustain oneself by the practice of gleaning, having taken a bowl. In this discourse too, only the cycle and that which is free from the cycle are taught.

5. Mātāputtasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Mātāputta Discourse

55. Pañcame [V 3.0028] pariyādāya tiṭṭhatīti pariyādiyitvā gahetvā khepetvā tiṭṭhati. Ugghātitāti uddhumātā.

55. In the fifth sutta, 'pariyādāya tiṭṭhati' means: having completely taken, seized, and exhausted, it remains. 'Ugghātitā' means a bloated corpse.

Asihatthenāti sīsacchedanatthāya asiṃ ādāya āgatenāpi. Pisācenāti khādituṃ āgatayakkhenāpi. Āsīdeti ghaṭṭeyya. Mañjunāti mudukena. Kāmoghavuḷhānanti kāmoghena vuḷhānaṃ kaḍḍhitānaṃ. Kālaṃ [P 3.0259] gati bhavābhavanti [M 3.0028] vaṭṭakālaṃ gatiñca punappunabbhave ca. Purakkhatāti purecārikā purato gatāyeva. Ye ca kāme pariññāyāti ye paṇḍitā duvidhepi kāme tīhi pariññāhi parijānitvā. Caranti akutobhayāti khīṇāsavānaṃ kutoci bhayaṃ nāma natthi, tasmā te akutobhayā hutvā caranti. Pāraṅgatāti pāraṃ vuccati nibbānaṃ, taṃ upagatā, sacchikatvā ṭhitāti attho. Āsavakkhayanti arahattaṃ. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭameva kathetvā gāthāsu vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ.

'Asihatthena' means even by an enemy who has come having taken a sword to cut off the head. 'Pisācena' means even by a yakkha who has come to devour. 'Āsīdeti' means would strike. 'Mañjunā' means by a soft one. 'Kāmoghavuḷhānaṃ' means of those swept away, dragged by the flood of sensuality. 'Kālaṃ gati bhavābhavaṃ' means the time of the cycle, the destination, and repeated existence. 'Purakkhatā' means they are forerunners, having gone before. 'Ye ca kāme pariññāya' means: those wise ones who, having fully known the two kinds of sensual pleasures with the three kinds of full understanding... 'Caranti akutobhayā' means: for the destroyers of taints, there is no such thing as fear from any cause; therefore, having become fearless, they go about. 'Pāraṅgatā': here, 'pāraṃ' (the beyond) is said to be Nibbāna; the meaning is that they are established, having approached and realized it. 'Āsavakkhayaṃ' means Arahantship. In this sutta, having taught only the cycle, in the verses, the cycle and that which is free from the cycle are taught.

6. Upajjhāyasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Upajjhāya Sutta

56. Chaṭṭhe madhurakajātoti sañjātagarubhāvo. Disā ca me na pakkhāyantīti catasso disā ca anudisā ca mayhaṃ na upaṭṭhahantīti vadati. Dhammā ca maṃ nappaṭibhantīti samathavipassanādhammāpi me na upaṭṭhahanti. Anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṃ carāmīti ukkaṇṭhito hutvā brahmacariyavāsaṃ vasāmi. Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti tassa kathaṃ sutvā “buddhaveneyyapuggalo aya”nti taṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavato ārocetuṃ upasaṅkami. Avipassakassa kusalānaṃ dhammānanti kusaladhamme avipassantassa, anesantassa agavesantassāti attho. Bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānanti satipaṭṭhānādīnaṃ sattatiṃsadhammānaṃ.

56. In the sixth sutta, `madhurakajāto` means a state of heaviness has arisen. `Disā ca me na pakkhāyanti` means he says: ‘The four cardinal directions and the intermediate directions do not appear to me.’ `Dhammā ca maṃ nappaṭibhanti` means: even the dhammas of serenity and insight do not arise for me. `Anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṃ carāmi` means: being dissatisfied, I live the holy life. `Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami` means: having heard his speech, thinking, ‘This is a person to be trained by the Buddha,’ he approached to inform the Blessed One of that reason. `Avipassakassa kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ` means: of one who does not see wholesome dhammas, who does not seek, who does not search; this is the meaning. `Bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ` means: of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, beginning with the foundations of mindfulness.

7. Abhiṇhapaccavekkhitabbaṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Sutta on Themes for Frequent Contemplation

57. Sattame jarādhammomhīti jarāsabhāvo amhi. Jaraṃ anatītoti jaraṃ anatikkanto, antojarāya eva carāmi. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Kammassakotiādīsu [P 3.0260] kammaṃ mayhaṃ sakaṃ [V 3.0029] attano santakanti kammassako amhi. Kammassa dāyādoti kammadāyādo, kammaṃ mayhaṃ dāyajjaṃ santakanti attho. Kammaṃ mayhaṃ yoni kāraṇanti kammayoni. Kammaṃ mayhaṃ bandhūti kammabandhu, kammañātakoti attho. Kammaṃ mayhaṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ patiṭṭhāti kammapaṭisaraṇo. Tassa dāyādo bhavissāmīti tassa kammassa dāyādo tena dinnaphalapaṭiggāhako bhavissāmīti attho. Yobbanamadoti yobbanaṃ ārabbha uppannamado. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Maggo sañjāyatīti lokuttaramaggo sañjāyati. Saṃyojanāni sabbaso pahīyantīti dasa saṃyojanāni sabbaso pahīyanti. Anusayā byantīhontīti satta anusayā vigatantā paricchinnā parivaṭumā [M 3.0029] honti. Evamettha heṭṭhā pañcasu ṭhānesu vipassanā kathitā, imesu pañcasu lokuttaramaggo.

57. In the seventh sutta, 'I am subject to aging' (jarādhammomhi) means 'I am of the nature of aging'. 'Not beyond aging' (jaraṃ anatīto) means 'I have not transcended aging; I move only within aging'. The same principle applies to the remaining terms. In 'owner of my kamma' (kammassako), etc., 'kamma is my own possession, belonging to myself'—thus, 'I am the owner of my kamma'. 'Heir to kamma' (kammadāyādo) means 'kamma is my inheritance, my property'—this is the meaning. 'Kamma is my origin' (kammayoni) means 'kamma is my cause'. 'Kamma is my relative' (kammabandhu) means 'kamma is my kin'—this is the meaning. 'Kamma is my refuge' (kammapaṭisaraṇo) means 'kamma is my support'. 'I will be the heir to that' (tassa dāyādo bhavissāmi) means 'I will be the heir of that kamma, the receiver of the fruit given by it'—this is the meaning. 'Intoxication with youth' (yobbanamado) means 'the intoxication arising in dependence on youth'. The same principle applies to the remaining terms. 'The path arises' (maggo sañjāyati) means 'the supramundane path arises'. 'The fetters are entirely abandoned' (saṃyojanāni sabbaso pahīyanti) means 'the ten fetters are entirely abandoned'. 'The underlying tendencies are brought to an end' (anusayā byantīhonti) means 'the seven underlying tendencies are terminated and cut off'. Thus, in the five earlier instances, insight was taught; in these five, the supramundane path was taught.

Idāni gāthāhi kūṭaṃ gaṇhanto byādhidhammātiādimāha. Tattha ñatvā dhammaṃ nirūpadhinti upadhirahitaṃ arahattamaggaṃ ñatvā. Sabbe made abhibhosmīti sabbe ime tayopi made adhibhaviṃ, atikkamma ṭhitosmīti attho. Nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khematoti pabbajjaṃ khemato disvā. Tassa me ahu ussāho, nibbānaṃ abhipassatoti tassa mayhaṃ nibbānaṃ abhipassantassa vāyāmo ahosi. Anivatti bhavissāmīti pabbajjato anivattiko bhavissāmi, brahmacariyavāsato [P 3.0261] anivattiko, sabbaññutaññāṇato anivattiko bhavissāmi. Brahmacariyaparāyaṇoti maggabrahmacariyaparāyaṇo. Iminā lokuttaro aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo kathitoti.

Now, taking up the pinnacle with verses, he speaks of 'subject to disease' (byādhidhammā), and so on. There, 'knowing the Dhamma as free from clinging' (ñatvā dhammaṃ nirūpadhiṃ) means knowing the path of Arahantship, which is devoid of clinging. 'I have overcome all intoxications' (sabbe made abhibhosmi) means 'I have overcome all these three intoxications; I stand having transcended them'—this is the meaning. 'Seeing renunciation as safety' (nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhu khemato) means having seen the going forth as secure. 'Then arose in me effort, beholding Nibbāna' (tassa me ahu ussāho, nibbānaṃ abhipassato) means 'for me, who was beholding Nibbāna, effort arose'. 'I shall not turn back' (anivatti bhavissāmi) means 'I shall not turn back from the going forth; I shall not turn back from living the holy life; I shall not turn back from the knowledge of omniscience'. 'Devoted to the holy life' (brahmacariyaparāyaṇo) means 'devoted to the holy life of the path'. By this, the supramundane Eightfold Path is taught.

8. Licchavikumārakasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Sutta to the Licchavi Youths

58. Aṭṭhame sajjāni dhanūnīti sajiyāni āropitadhanūni. Addasūti addasaṃsu. Bhavissanti vajjīti vaḍḍhissanti vajjirājāno. Apānubhāti avaḍḍhinissitā mānathaddhā. Pacchāliyaṃ khipantīti pacchato gantvā piṭṭhiṃ pādena paharanti. Raṭṭhikassātiādīsu raṭṭhaṃ bhuñjatīti raṭṭhiko. Pitarā dattaṃ sāpateyyaṃ bhuñjatīti pettaniko. Senāya pati jeṭṭhakoti senāpatiko. Gāmagāmaṇikassāti gāmānaṃ gāmaṇikassa, gāmasāmikassāti attho. Pūgagāmaṇikassāti gaṇajeṭṭhakassa. Kulesūti tesu tesu kulesu. Paccekādhipaccaṃ kārentīti paccekaṃ jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānaṃ kārenti. Kalyāṇena manasā anukampantīti sundarena cittena anuggaṇhanti. Khettakammantasāmantasabyohāreti ye ca attano khettakammantānaṃ sāmantā anantarakkhettasāmino, te ca rajjudaṇḍehi bhūmippamāṇaggāhake sabbohāre ca. Balipaṭiggāhikā [V 3.0030][P 3.0262] devatāti kulappaveṇiyā āgatā ārakkhadevatā. Sakkarotīti tā devatā aggayāgubhattādīhi sakkaroti.

58. In the eighth sutta, 'bows ready' (sajjāni dhanūni) means prepared, strung bows. 'They saw' (addasūti) means they saw. 'The Vajjis will prosper' (bhavissanti vajjī) means the Vajji kings will increase. 'Not prospering' (apānubhāti) means they are dependent on non-prosperity and are stiff with conceit. 'Kicking from behind' (pacchāliyaṃ khipanti) means going behind and striking the back with the foot. In 'to the provincial governor' (raṭṭhikassa), etc., 'one who enjoys the country' is a provincial governor (raṭṭhika). 'Enjoying the inheritance given by his father' is a paternal heir (pettanika). 'Leader of the army, the eldest' is a general (senāpatika). 'To the village headman' (gāmagāmaṇikassa) means to the leader of villages, to the lord of the village; this is the meaning. 'To the guild leader' (pūgagāmaṇikassa) means to the chief of a guild. 'In families' (kulesu) means in those various families. 'They exercise individual authority' (paccekādhipaccaṃ kārenti) means they establish individual positions of seniority. 'With a benevolent mind, they show compassion' (kalyāṇena manasā anukampanti) means they support them with a good mind. This refers to the owners of fields adjacent to one's own fields and agricultural work, those who take land measurements with ropes and rods, and the judicial officers. 'Deities who receive offerings' (balipaṭiggāhikā devatā) means protective deities who have come down through the family lineage. 'He honors' (sakkaroti) means he honors those deities with the first portion of rice gruel and cooked rice, and so on.

Kiccakaroti uppannānaṃ kiccānaṃ kārako. Ye cassa anujīvinoti ye ca etaṃ upanissāya jīvanti. Ubhinnañceva atthāyāti ubhinnampi hitatthāya paṭipanno hotīti attho. Pubbapetānanti paralokagatānaṃ. Diṭṭhe dhamme ca jīvatanti ye ca diṭṭhe dhamme [M 3.0030] jīvanti. Iti padadvayenāpi atītapaccuppanne ñātayo dasseti. Vittisañjananoti tuṭṭhijanano. Gharamāvasanti gharāvāsaṃ vasanto. Pujjo hoti pasaṃsiyoti pūjetabbo ca pasaṃsitabbo ca hotīti.

'One who performs duties' (kiccākaro) means one who performs arisen tasks. 'And those who depend on him' (ye cassa anujīvino) means those who live depending on him. 'For the benefit of both' (ubhinnañceva atthāya) means he is one who practices for the welfare of both—this is the meaning. 'For the departed ancestors' (pubbapetānaṃ) means for those who have gone to the other world. 'And for those living in the present' (diṭṭhe dhamme ca jīvanti) means those who are living in the present existence. Thus, with this pair of terms, he indicates relatives of both the past and present. 'Generating delight' (vittisañjanano) means a generator of contentment. 'Living at home' (gharamāvasanto) means living the household life. 'He is worthy of honor and praise' (pujjo hoti pasaṃsiyo) means he is to be honored and praised.

9-10. Vuḍḍhapabbajitasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

9-10. Commentary on the Two Suttas on the Elderly Gone Forth

59-60. Navame nipuṇoti saṇho sukhumakāraṇaññū. Ākappasampannoti samaṇākappena sampanno. Dasame padakkhiṇaggāhīti dinnovādaṃ padakkhiṇato gaṇhanto. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

In the ninth, `nipuṇo` means subtle, able to know subtle causes. `Ākappasampanno` means endowed with the demeanor of a contemplative. In the tenth, `padakkhiṇaggāhī` means one who is able to accept the given instruction in a supreme manner. The rest is clear throughout.

Nīvaraṇavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on the Hindrances.

(7) 2. Saññāvaggo

(7) 2. The Chapter on Perceptions

1-2. Saññāsuttadvayavaṇṇanā

1-2. Commentary on the Two Suttas on Perceptions

61-62. Dutiyassa paṭhame mahapphalāti vipākaphalena mahapphalā. Vipākānisaṃseneva mahānisaṃsā. Amatogadhāti nibbānapatiṭṭhā. Sabbaloke [P 3.0263] anabhiratisaññāti sabbasmiṃ tedhātusannivese loke ukkaṇṭhitassa uppajjanakasaññā. Dutiyaṃ uttānatthameva.

In the first of the second chapter, `mahapphalā` means of great fruit by way of resultant fruit. `Mahānisaṃsā` means of great benefit only by way of resultant benefit. `Amatogadhā` means having Nibbāna as its foundation. `Sabbaloke anabhiratisaññā` means the perception of non-delight that arises in one who is discontented with the entire world, the aggregation of the three realms. The second is clear in meaning.

3-4. Vaḍḍhasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

3-4. Commentary on the Two Suttas to Vaḍḍha

63-64. Tatiye [V 3.0031] varādāyīti uttamassa varassa ādāyako. Sesamettha catutthe ca uttānatthamevāti.

In the third, `varādāyī` means the receiver of the supreme, praiseworthy benefit. The rest, here and in the fourth, is clear in meaning.

5. Sākacchasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse on Discussion

65. Pañcame alaṃsākacchoti sākacchāya yutto. Āgataṃ pañhanti pucchitaṃ pañhaṃ. Byākattā hotīti vissajjitā hoti.

65. In the fifth, `alaṃsākaccho` means fit for discussion. `Āgataṃ pañhaṃ` means the question that has been asked. `Byākattā hoti` means one is able to answer.

6. Sājīvasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on Livelihood

66. Chaṭṭhe [M 3.0031] alaṃsājīvoti sājīvāya yutto. Sājīvoti pañhapucchanañceva pañhavissajjanañca. Sabbepi hi sabrahmacārino pañhaṃ upajīvanti, tenetaṃ pañhapucchanavissajjanaṃ samānājīvatāya sājīvoti vuttaṃ. Kataṃ pañhanti abhisaṅkhataṃ pañhaṃ.

66. In the sixth, `alaṃsājīvo` means fit for livelihood. `Sājīvo` refers to both the asking of questions and the answering of questions. Indeed, all fellow practitioners live by means of questions; therefore, because it is a common livelihood, this asking and answering of questions is called `sājīvo`. `Kataṃ pañhaṃ` means a contrived question.

7-10. Paṭhamaiddhipādasuttādivaṇṇanā

7-10. Commentary on the First Discourse on the Bases of Spiritual Power, and so forth

67-70. Sattame ussoḷhīti adhimattavīriyaṃ. Aṭṭhame attano bodhimaṇḍe paṭividdhe āgamanaiddhipāde kathetvā upari attanova cha abhiññā kathesīti. Navamadasamesu vipassanā kathitā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

In the seventh, `ussoḷhī` means exceeding effort. In the eighth, having taught the causal bases of spiritual power that were penetrated at his own Bodhi-maṇḍa, he then taught his own six superknowledges. In the ninth and tenth suttas, insight was taught. The rest is clear throughout.

Saññāvaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Perceptions is finished.

(8) 3. Yodhājīvavaggo

(8) 3. The Chapter on the Warrior

1. Paṭhamacetovimuttiphalasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Discourse on the Fruit of the Mind's Liberation

71. Tatiyassa [V 3.0032] paṭhame yato kho, bhikkhaveti heṭṭhā vuttanayena vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pattassa bhikkhuno idāni vaṇṇabhaṇanatthaṃ idaṃ āraddhaṃ. Tattha [P 3.0264] yato khoti yadā kho. Ukkhittapalighoti avijjāpalighaṃ ukkhipitvā apanetvā ṭhito. Saṃkiṇṇaparikhoti saṃsāraparikhaṃ saṃkiritvā vināsetvā ṭhito. Abbūḷhesikoti taṇhāsaṅkhātaṃ esikāthambhaṃ abbuyha luñcitvā ṭhito. Niraggaḷoti nīvaraṇakavāṭaṃ ugghāṭetvā ṭhito. Pannaddhajo pannabhāroti mānaddhajañca khandhābhisaṅkhārakilesabhārañca pātetvā otāretvā ṭhito. Visaṃyuttoti vaṭṭena visaṃyutto. Sesaṃ pāḷinayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ettāvatā bhagavatā maggena kilese khepetvā nirodhasayanavaragatassa nibbānārammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ appetvā viharato khīṇāsavassa kālo dassito.

71. In the first of the third chapter, this discourse beginning 'Yato kho, bhikkhave...' was undertaken for the purpose of extolling a bhikkhu who has attained Arahantship by developing insight according to the method stated previously. Therein, `yato kho` means 'when indeed.' `Ukkhittapaligho` means one who stands having lifted up and removed the cross-bar of ignorance. `Saṃkiṇṇaparikho` means one who stands having scattered and destroyed the moat of saṃsāra. `Abbūḷhesiko` means one who stands having pulled out the door-post known as craving. `Niraggaḷo` means one who stands having opened the door of the hindrances. `Pannaddhajo pannabhāro` means one who stands having laid down the banner of conceit and lowered the burden of the aggregates, formations, and defilements. `Visaṃyutto` means one who is disjoined from the round of existence. The rest should be understood according to the Pāḷi itself. By this much, the Blessed One has shown the state of a destroyer of cankers who, having exhausted the defilements by means of the path, abides having entered the fruition-attainment that has Nibbāna as its object, and has reached the supreme bed of cessation.

Yathā hi dve nagarāni ekaṃ coranagaraṃ ekaṃ khemanagaraṃ. Atha ekassa mahāyodhassa evaṃ bhaveyya – “yāvimaṃ coranagaraṃ tiṭṭhati, tāva khemanagaraṃ bhayato [M 3.0032] na muccati, coranagaraṃ anagaraṃ karissāmī”ti sannāhaṃ katvā khaggaṃ gahetvā coranagaraṃ upasaṅkamitvā nagaradvāre ussāpite esikāthambhe khaggena chinditvā saddhiṃ dvārabāhāhi kavāṭaṃ bhinditvā palighaṃ ukkhipitvā pākāraṃ bhinditvā parikhaṃ vikiritvā nagarasobhatthāya ussite dhaje pātetvā nagaraṃ agginā jhāpetvā khemanagaraṃ pavisitvā pāsādaṃ āruyha ñātigaṇaparivuto surasabhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya. Evaṃ coranagaraṃ viya sakkāyo, khemanagaraṃ viya nibbānaṃ, mahāyodho viya yogāvacaro. Tassevaṃ hoti – “yāva sakkāyavaṭṭaṃ vaṭṭati, tāva dvattiṃsakammakāraṇāaṭṭhanavutirogapañcavīsatimahābhayehi [P 3.0265] parimuccanaṃ natthī”ti. So mahāyodho sannāhaṃ viya sīlasannāhaṃ katvā paññākhaggaṃ gahetvā khaggena esikāthambhe viya arahattamaggena taṇhesikaṃ luñcitvā, so yodho sadvārabāhakaṃ nagarakavāṭaṃ viya pañcorambhāgiyasaṃyojanaaggaḷaṃ ugghāṭetvā, so yodho palighaṃ viya avijjāpalighaṃ ukkhipitvā, so yodho pākāraṃ bhindanto parikhaṃ viya kammābhisaṅkhāraṃ bhindanto jātisaṃsāraparikhaṃ vikiritvā, so yodho nagaraṃ sobhatthāya [V 3.0033] ussāpitaddhaje viya mānaddhaje pātetvā sakkāyanagaraṃ jhāpetvā, so yodho khemanagare uparipāsāde subhojanaṃ viya kilesaparinibbānanagaraṃ pavisitvā amataṃ nirodhārammaṇaṃ phalasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavamāno kālaṃ vītināmeti.

For it is as if there were two cities: one a city of thieves, the other a city of safety. Then a great warrior might think: 'As long as this city of thieves stands, the city of safety is not free from danger. I will make this city of thieves a non-city!' Having donned his armor and taken up his sword, he would approach the city of thieves. At the city gate, he would cut down the erected door-posts with his sword, break down the door-leaf together with the door-posts, lift up the cross-bar, breach the city wall, scatter the moat, fell the banners raised for the city's splendor, burn the city with fire, enter the city of safety, ascend to a palace and, surrounded by his host of kinsmen, enjoy a delicious meal. So too, the personality-group is like the city of thieves, Nibbāna is like the city of safety, and the yogī is like the great warrior. It occurs to him: 'As long as the round of the personality-group turns, there is no release from the thirty-two kinds of afflictions, the ninety-eight diseases, and the twenty-five great fears.' That yogī, like the great warrior donning his armor, dons the armor of virtue. Taking up the sword of wisdom, just as the warrior pulls out the door-posts with his sword, he pulls out the door-post of craving with the path to Arahantship. Just as that warrior unbolts the city door-leaf together with its door-posts, he unbolts the bolt of the five lower fetters. Just as that warrior lifts up the cross-bar, he lifts up the cross-bar of ignorance. Just as that warrior, breaching the city wall, shatters the moat, he, shattering the karmic formations, scatters the moat of birth and saṃsāra. Just as that warrior fells the banners raised for the city's splendor, he fells the banners of conceit. Having burned the city of the personality-group, just as that warrior enters the city of safety and enjoys a fine meal in a palace, he enters the city of Nibbāna, the quenching of defilements, and passes his time experiencing the bliss of fruition-attainment, which has the deathless cessation as its object.

2. Dutiyacetovimuttiphalasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Fruit of the Liberation of Mind

72. Dutiye aniccasaññāti khandhapañcakaṃ hutvā abhāvākārena aniccanti uppajjanakasaññā. Anicce dukkhasaññāti yadaniccaṃ, taṃ paṭipīḷanākārena dukkhanti uppajjanakasaññā. Dukkhe anattasaññāti yaṃ dukkhaṃ, taṃ avasavattanākārena anattāti uppajjanakasaññā. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva. Imesu pana dvīsupi suttesu vipassanāphalaṃ nāma kathitanti.

72. In the second discourse: 'Perception of impermanence' is the perception that arises thus: 'The pentad of aggregates, having come to be, is impermanent by way of its non-existence.' 'Perception of suffering in the impermanent' is the perception that arises thus: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering by way of oppression.' 'Perception of not-self in suffering' is the perception that arises thus: 'Whatever is suffering, that is not-self by way of its uncontrollability.' The remainder is of the same method as stated previously. However, in both these discourses, what is called the fruit of insight is taught.

3. Paṭhamadhammavihārīsuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the First Discourse on Dhamma-Abiding

73. Tatiye divasaṃ atināmetīti divasaṃ atikkāmeti. Riñcati paṭisallānanti ekībhāvaṃ vissajjeti. Desetīti katheti pakāseti. Dhammapaññattiyāti [M 3.0033] dhammassa paññāpanāya. Dhammaṃ [P 3.0266] pariyāpuṇātīti navaṅgavasena catusaccadhammaṃ pariyāpuṇāti vaḷañjeti katheti. Na riñcati paṭisallānanti ekībhāvaṃ na vissajjeti. Anuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathanti niyakajjhatte cittasamādhiṃ āsevati bhāveti, samathakammaṭṭhāne yuttappayutto hoti.

73. In the third discourse: 'He passes the day' means he causes the day to pass. 'He abandons seclusion' means he gives up solitude. 'He teaches' means he speaks and makes it clear. 'By means of the Dhamma-designation' means for the purpose of making the Dhamma known. 'He masters the Dhamma' means he masters, makes use of, and speaks on the Dhamma of the Four Truths by way of the ninefold scriptures. 'He does not abandon seclusion' means he does not give up solitude. 'He applies himself to internal serenity of mind' means he resorts to and develops concentration of mind in his own person; he is diligently engaged in the meditation subject of serenity.

Hitesināti hitaṃ esantena. Anukampakenāti anukampamānena. Anukampaṃ upādāyāti anukampaṃ cittena pariggahetvā, paṭiccātipi vuttaṃ hoti. Kataṃ vo taṃ mayāti taṃ mayā ime pañca puggale desentena tumhākaṃ kataṃ. Ettakameva hi anukampakassa satthu kiccaṃ yadidaṃ aviparītadhammadesanā, ito paraṃ pana paṭipatti nāma sāvakānaṃ kiccaṃ. Tenāha – etāni bhikkhu rukkhamūlāni…pe… amhākaṃ anusāsanīti. Tattha ca rukkhamūlānīti iminā rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ dasseti. Suññāgārānīti iminā janavivittaṭṭhānaṃ. Ubhayenāpi ca yogānurūpaṃ senāsanamācikkhati, dāyajjaṃ niyyāteti. Jhāyathāti ārammaṇūpanijjhānena aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇāni, lakkhaṇūpanijjhānena ca aniccādito khandhāyatanādīni upanijjhāyatha, samathañca [V 3.0034] vipassanañca vaḍḍhethāti vuttaṃ hoti. Mā pamādatthāti mā pamajjittha. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthāti ye hi pubbe daharakāle ārogyakāle sattasappāyādisampattikāle satthu sammukhībhāvakāle ca yonisomanasikāravirahitā rattindivaṃ maṅkulabhattā hutvā seyyasukhamiddhasukhamanuyuttā pamajjanti, te pacchā jarākāle rogakāle maraṇakāle vipattikāle [P 3.0267] satthu parinibbānakāle ca taṃ pubbe pamādavihāraṃ anussarantā sappaṭisandhikālakiriyañca bhāriyaṃ sampassamānā vippaṭisārino honti. Tumhe pana tādisā mā ahuvatthāti etamatthaṃ dassento āha – “mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvatthā”ti. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanīti ayaṃ amhākaṃ santikā “jhāyatha mā pamādatthā”ti tumhākaṃ anusāsanī, ovādoti vuttaṃ hoti.

‘By one who seeks what is beneficial’ means by one who seeks the good. ‘By a compassionate one’ means by one who is compassionate. ‘Out of compassion’ means having encompassed compassion with the mind, based on it; this is also what is meant. ‘That has been done for you by me’ means: that task has been done for you by me while teaching these five individuals. For this much is the duty of a compassionate Teacher: the teaching of the Dhamma without distortion. Beyond this, however, what is called practice is the duty of the disciples. Therefore, he said: 'These, monks, are the roots of trees… this is our instruction.' Therein, by 'the roots of trees' he indicates a lodging at the foot of a tree. By 'empty dwellings' he indicates a place secluded from people. And by both, he points out a lodging suitable for the meditative endeavor and bestows it as an inheritance. 'Meditate' means: 'Contemplate closely the thirty-eight objects by means of object-scrutiny, and the aggregates, sense-bases, and so on, beginning with impermanence, by means of characteristic-scrutiny; develop both serenity and insight.' This is what is meant. 'Do not be heedless' means do not be negligent. 'Do not be remorseful later' [means this]: For those who formerly, in their youth, in times of health, in times of favorable circumstances, and in the presence of the Teacher, being devoid of wise attention, having become food for bedbugs day and night, are heedless, devoted to the pleasure of lying down and the pleasure of drowsiness; they later, in old age, in times of sickness, at the time of death, in times of misfortune, and after the Teacher's final Nibbāna, remembering that former heedless abiding and seeing the burdensome death that entails rebirth-linking, become remorseful. But you should not be like that. Showing this meaning, he said: 'Do not be remorseful later.' 'This is our instruction to you' means: this, from us to you, 'Meditate, do not be heedless,' is our instruction, our exhortation. This is what is meant.

4. Dutiyadhammavihārīsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Exposition of the Second Discourse on Dwellers in the Dhamma

74. Catutthe uttari cassa paññāya atthaṃ nappajānātīti tato pariyattito uttari tassa dhammassa sahavipassanāya maggapaññāya atthaṃ nappajānāti[M 3.0034], cattāri saccāni na passati nappaṭivijjhatīti attho. Sesavāresupi eseva nayo. Evametesu dvīsupi suttesu bahussutabhikkhu vipassanākammiko sotāpanno sakadāgāmī anāgāmī khīṇāsavoti cha janā dhammavihārino nāmāti veditabbā.

74. In the fourth case, the phrase 'he does not understand the meaning beyond that by wisdom' means that he does not understand the meaning of that Dhamma, which is beyond mere learning, with the wisdom of the path accompanied by insight; that is to say, he does not see or penetrate the Four Noble Truths. The same method applies in the remaining cases as well. Thus, in these two discourses, six types of persons are to be known as dwellers in the Dhamma: the learned monk, the monk devoted to insight practice, the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, and the arahant.

5. Paṭhamayodhājīvasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Exposition of the First Discourse on the Warrior

75. Pañcame yodhājīvāti yuddhūpajīvino. Rajagganti hatthiassādīnaṃ pādappahārabhinnāya bhūmiyā uggataṃ rajakkhandhaṃ. Na santhambhatīti santhambhitvā ṭhātuṃ na sakkoti. Sahati rajagganti rajakkhandhaṃ disvāpi adhivāseti. Dhajagganti hatthiassadīnaṃ piṭṭhesu vā rathesu vā ussāpitānaṃ dhajānaṃ aggaṃ. Ussāraṇanti hatthiassarathānañceva balakāyassa ca uccāsaddamahāsaddaṃ. Sampahāreti samāgate appamattakepi pahāre. Haññatīti vihaññati vighātaṃ āpajjati. Byāpajjatīti vipattiṃ āpajjati, pakatibhāvaṃ jahati. Sahati sampahāranti dve tayo pahāre patvāpi sahati adhivāseti. Tameva [P 3.0268] saṅgāmasīsanti taṃyeva jayakkhandhāvāraṭṭhānaṃ. Ajjhāvasatīti sattāhamattaṃ abhibhavitvā āvasati. Kiṃ kāraṇā[V 3.0035]? Laddhapahārānaṃ pahārajagganatthañceva katakammānaṃ visesaṃ ñatvā ṭhānantaradānatthañca issariyasukhānubhavanatthañca.

75. In the fifth section, 'yodhājīvā' means 'those who live by warfare' (yuddhūpajīvino). 'Rajagga' refers to the elevated mass of dust that has risen from the ground broken by the trampling of elephants, horses, and so forth. 'Na santhambhati' means 'he is not able to stand firm.' 'Sahati rajagga' means 'he endures even having seen the mass of dust.' 'Dhajagga' refers to the tops of banners raised on the backs of elephants, horses, or chariots. 'Ussāraṇa' means the loud, tumultuous noise of elephants, horses, chariots, and the army. 'Sampahāra' refers to blows, even minor ones, that are encountered. 'Haññati' means 'he is distressed' (vihaññati) and 'falls into affliction' (vighātaṃ āpajjati). 'Byāpajjati' means 'he falls into misfortune' (vipattiṃ āpajjati) and 'abandons his natural state' (pakatibhāvaṃ jahati). 'Sahati sampahāra' means 'he endures, even having received two or three blows.' 'Tameva saṅgāmasīsaṃ' refers to that very place of the victorious encampment. 'Ajjhāvasati' means 'he dwells there for about a week after conquering.' For what reason? For the nursing of the blows of those who have received them, for allocating positions after recognizing the special deeds of those who have performed them, and for experiencing the pleasure of sovereignty.

Idāni yasmā satthu yodhājīvehi kiccaṃ natthi, imasmiṃ pana sāsane tathārūpe pañca puggale dassetuṃ idaṃ opammaṃ ābhataṃ. Tasmā te puggale dassento evameva khotiādimāha. Tattha saṃsīdatīti micchāvitakkasmiṃ saṃsīdati anuppavisati. Na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretunti brahmacariyavāsaṃ anupacchijjamānaṃ gopetuṃ na sakkoti. Sikkhādubbalyaṃ āvikatvāti sikkhāya dubbalabhāvaṃ pakāsetvā. Kimassa rajaggasminti kiṃ tassa puggalassa rajaggaṃ nāmāti vadati. Abhirūpāti abhirūpavatī. Dassanīyāti dassanayoggā. Pāsādikāti dassaneneva cittappasādāvahā. Paramāyāti uttamāya. Vaṇṇapokkharatāyāti sarīravaṇṇena ceva aṅgasaṇṭhānena ca. Ūhasatīti avahasati. Ullapatīti katheti. Ujjhagghatīti [M 3.0035] pāṇiṃ paharitvā mahāhasitaṃ hasati. Uppaṇḍetīti uppaṇḍanakathaṃ katheti. Abhinisīdatīti abhibhavitvā santike vā ekāsane vā nisīdati. Dutiyapadepi [P 3.0269] eseva nayo. Ajjhottharatīti avattharati. Viniveṭhetvā vinimocetvāti gahitaṭṭhānato tassā hatthaṃ vinibbeṭhetvā ceva mocetvā ca. Sesamettha uttānatthamevāti. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ.

Now, because the Teacher has no need for warriors, this simile has been brought forth in this teaching to illustrate five such individuals. Therefore, while pointing out those individuals, he says, 'evameva kho,' and so forth. Here, 'saṃsīdati' means he sinks into and enters wrong thoughts. 'Na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ' means he cannot maintain the holy life without interruption and protect it. 'Sikkhādubbalyaṃ āvikatvā' means having revealed his weakness in the training. 'Kimassa rajaggasminti' means 'What is that person’s 'mound of dust'?' he asks. 'Abhirūpā' means beautiful. 'Dassanīyā' means worthy of being seen. 'Pāsādikā' means inspiring confidence by mere sight. 'Paramāyā' means supreme. 'Vaṇṇapokkharatāya' means excellence in complexion and bodily form. 'Ūhasati' means he mocks. 'Ullapati' means he speaks. 'Ujjhagghati' means he laughs loudly, clapping his hands. 'Uppaṇḍeti' means he engages in teasing talk. 'Abhinisīdati' means he overpowers and sits nearby or on the same seat. The same method applies to the second phrase as well. 'Ajjhottharati' means he overwhelms. 'Viniveṭhetvā vinimocetvā' means untwisting and releasing her hand from its grasped position. The rest here is of clear meaning. In this discourse, the cycle of existence and liberation has been spoken.

6. Dutiyayodhājīvasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Professional Soldier

76. Chaṭṭhe asicammaṃ gahetvāti asiñca cammañca gahetvā. Dhanukalāpaṃ sannayhitvāti dhanuñca sarakalāpañca sannayhitvā. Viyūḷhanti yuddhasannivesavesena ṭhitaṃ. Saṅgāmaṃ otaratīti mahāyuddhaṃ otarati. Ussahati vāyamatīti ussāhañca vāyāmañca karoti. Hanantīti ghātenti. Pariyāpādentīti pariyāpādayanti. Upalikkhantīti vijjhanti. Apanentīti sakasenaṃ gahetvā gacchanti. Apanetvā ñātakānaṃ nentīti sakasenaṃ netvā tato ñātakānaṃ santikaṃ nenti. Nīyamānoti attano gehaṃ vā sesañātisantikaṃ vā niyyamāno. Upaṭṭhahanti paricarantīti pahārasodhanavaṇakappanādīni karontā jagganti gopayanti.

76. In the sixth sutta, 'asicammaṃ gahetvā' means taking up a sword and a shield. 'Dhanukalāpaṃ sannayhitvā' means slinging on a bow and a quiver. 'Viyūḷhaṃ' means standing arrayed by way of battle formation. 'Saṅgāmaṃ otarati' means he descends into the great battle. 'Ussahati vāyamati' means he makes an effort and strives. 'Hananti' means they slay. 'Pariyāpādenti' means they bring his life to an end. 'Upalikkhanti' means they pierce. 'Apanenti' means they take him and go to their own army. 'Having led him away, they lead him to his relatives' means having led him to their own army, from there they lead him to the presence of his relatives. 'Nīyamāno' means being led to his own home or to the presence of other relatives. 'Upaṭṭhahanti paricaranti' means while doing things such as cleaning the strike-wound and dressing the injury, they watch over and protect him.

Arakkhiteneva kāyenāti arakkhitena kāyadvārena. Arakkhitāya vācāyāti arakkhitena vacīdvārena. Arakkhitena cittenāti arakkhitena manodvārena. Anupaṭṭhitāya satiyāti satiṃ supaṭṭhitaṃ [V 3.0036] akatvā. Asaṃvutehi [P 3.0270] indriyehīti manacchaṭṭhehi indriyehi apihitehi agopitehi. Rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃsetīti rāgo uppajjamānova samathavipassanācittaṃ dhaṃseti, dūre khipati. Rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgaparetoti ahaṃ, āvuso, rāgena ratto, rāgena anugato.

'With an unguarded body' means with an unguarded body-door. 'With unguarded speech' means with an unguarded speech-door. 'With an unguarded mind' means with an unguarded mind-door. 'With unestablished mindfulness' means not having made mindfulness well-established. 'With unrestrained faculties' means with the faculties that have the mind-faculty as the sixth, being unclosed and unprotected. 'Lust assails the mind' means that lust, on arising, destroys the mind of serenity and insight; it casts it far away. 'Friend, I am assailed by lust, overcome by lust' means, 'Friend, I am impassioned by lust, I am pursued by lust.'

Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamātiādīsu aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā appassādaṭṭhena. Maṃsapesūpamā bahusādhāraṇaṭṭhena. Tiṇukkūpamā anudahanaṭṭhena. Aṅgārakāsūpamā mahābhitāpaṭṭhena. Supinakūpamā ittarapaccupaṭṭhānaṭṭhena. Yācitakūpamā tāvakālikaṭṭhena. Rukkhaphalūpamā sabbaṅgapaccaṅgapalibhañjanaṭṭhena. Asisūnūpamā adhikuṭṭanaṭṭhena. Sattisūlūpamā vinivijjhanaṭṭhena. Sappasirūpamā sāsaṅkasappaṭibhayaṭṭhena[M 3.0036]. Ussahissāmīti ussāhaṃ karissāmi. Dhārayissāmīti samaṇabhāvaṃ dhārayissāmi. Abhiramissāmīti abhiratiṃ uppādessāmi na ukkaṇṭhissāmi. Sesamettha uttānatthameva. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitanti.

In the similes of the skeleton, etc.: the simile of the skeleton is because of the meaning of being without gratification; the simile of the piece of flesh is because of the meaning of being common to many; the simile of the grass torch is because of the meaning of burning; the simile of the heap of embers is because of the meaning of causing great heat; the simile of a dream is because of the meaning of appearing for a moment; the simile of a borrowed object is because of the meaning of being temporary; the simile of the tree’s fruit is because of the meaning of destroying all major and minor limbs; the simile of the butcher's block is because of the meaning of being a place for chopping; the simile of the spear-point is because of the meaning of piercing through; the simile of the snake’s head is because of the meaning of being accompanied by disgust and frightful danger. 'I will make an effort' means I will strive. 'I will bear' means I will bear the state of a renunciant. 'I will delight' means I will cause delight to arise and will not be discontented. The rest here has a clear meaning. In this sutta, the round of existence and the turning away from it has been taught. Thus ends the sixth sutta.

7. Paṭhamaanāgatabhayasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the First Discourse on Future Dangers

77. Sattame āraññakenāti araññavāsinā. Appattassāti asampattassa jhānavipassanāmaggaphalappabhedassa visesassa pattiyā. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. So mamassa antarāyoti so mama jīvitantarāyo ca brahmacariyantarāyo ca, puthujjanakālakiriyaṃ karontassa saggantarāyo ca maggantarāyo ca bhaveyya. Handāti vavassaggatthe nipāto. Vīriyaṃ ārabhāmīti duvidhampi vīriyaṃ karomi. Satthakāti [P 3.0271] satthaṃ viya sandhibandhanacchedakavātā. Vāḷehīti kakkhaḷehi. Māṇavehīti corehi. Katakammehi vā akatakammehi vāti ettha corikaṃ katvā nikkhantā katakammā nāma, corikaṃ kātuṃ gacchantā akatakammā nāma. Tattha katakammā kammassa nipphannattā sattānaṃ galalohitaṃ gahetvā devatānaṃ baliṃ karonti, akatakammā “evaṃ no kammaṃ nipphajjissatī”ti paṭhamataraṃ karonti. Idaṃ sandhāya te maṃ jīvitā voropeyyunti vuttaṃ. Vāḷā amanussāti kakkhaḷā duṭṭhā yakkhādayo amanussā.

77. In the seventh sutta, 'by a forest dweller' means by one who lives in the forest. 'For one who has not attained' means for the attainment of the special state, which has the distinctions of jhāna, insight, path, and fruition, that has not been reached. This same method applies to the remaining phrases. 'That would be an obstacle for me' means: 'That would be an obstacle to my life and an obstacle to the holy life; for one who dies as an ordinary person, it would be an obstacle to heaven and an obstacle to the path.' The particle 'handa' ('come now') occurs in the sense of resolve. 'I will arouse energy' means I will undertake both kinds of energy. 'Like a weapon' means winds that, like a weapon, sever the joints and ligaments. 'By savage ones' means by harsh ones. 'By young men' means by thieves. 'Whether they have committed the deed or not committed the deed': herein, thieves who have left after committing theft are called 'those who have committed the deed'; thieves who are going to commit theft are called 'those who have not committed the deed.' Among them, those who have committed the deed, because their deed is accomplished, take the throat-blood of beings and make an offering to the deities. Those who have not committed the deed, thinking, 'Thus our deed will be accomplished,' first make an offering to the deities. With reference to this, it was said: 'they would deprive me of life.' 'Savage non-humans' means harsh, malevolent non-humans such as yakkhas and so on.

8. Dutiyaanāgatabhayasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Second Discourse on Future Dangers

78. Aṭṭhame purā maṃ so dhammo āgacchatīti yāva so dhammo maṃ na upagacchati, tāva [V 3.0037] ahaṃ puretarameva vīriyaṃ ārabhāmīti attho. Khīrodakībhūtāti khīrodakaṃ viya bhūtā ekībhāvaṃ upagatā. Piyacakkhūhīti mettacakkhūhi.

78. In the eighth sutta, the meaning of 'before that state comes to me' is: 'As long as that state of old age does not approach me, so long will I arouse energy beforehand.' 'Having become like milk and water' means having become like milk mixed with water, having attained a state of oneness. 'With affectionate eyes' means with eyes of loving-kindness.

9. Tatiyaanāgatabhayasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Third Discourse on Future Dangers

79. Navame dhammasandosā vinayasandosoti dhammasandosena vinayasandoso hoti. Kathaṃ pana dhammasmiṃ dussante vinayo dussati nāma? Samathavipassanādhammesu gabbhaṃ aggaṇhantesu pañcavidho vinayo na hoti[M 3.0037], evaṃ dhamme dussante vinayo dussati. Dussīlassa pana saṃvaravinayo nāma na hoti, tasmiṃ asati samathavipassanā gabbhaṃ na gaṇhāti. Evaṃ vinayasandosenapi dhammasandoso veditabbo. Abhidhammakathanti sīlādiuttamadhammakathaṃ. Vedallakathanti vedapaṭisaṃyuttaṃ ñāṇamissakakathaṃ. Kaṇhadhammaṃ okkamamānāti randhagavesitāya upārambhapariyesanavasena [P 3.0272] kāḷakadhammaṃ okkamamānā. Apica duṭṭhacittena puggalaṃ ghaṭṭentāpi taṃ kaṇhadhammaṃ attano dahantāpi lābhasakkāratthaṃ kathentāpi kaṇhadhammaṃ okkamantiyeva.

79. In the ninth sutta, 'from the corruption of the Dhamma, the corruption of the Vinaya' means that through the corruption of the Dhamma, the corruption of the Vinaya occurs. How, then, when the Dhamma is corrupted, is the Vinaya said to be corrupted? When they do not grasp the profound core of the Dhamma of serenity and insight, the five-fold Vinaya does not exist; thus, when the Dhamma is corrupted, the Vinaya is corrupted. Furthermore, for an immoral person, there is no Vinaya of restraint. When that is absent, serenity and insight do not grasp the profound core. Thus, the corruption of the Dhamma should also be understood as being due to the corruption of the Vinaya. 'Talk on the higher Dhamma' means talk on the excellent Dhamma, such as virtue and so on. 'Talk in the question-and-answer format (vedalla)' means talk connected with the attainment of knowledge, mixed with wisdom. 'Descending into the dark state' means descending into the dark state by way of seeking faults. Moreover, monks who oppress a person with a malevolent mind, or who place that dark, unwholesome state in themselves, or who speak for the sake of gain and honor, are indeed descending into the dark state.

Gambhīrāti pāḷigambhīrā. Gambhīratthāti atthagambhīrā. Lokuttarāti lokuttaradhammadīpakā. Suññatāpaṭisaṃyuttāti khandhadhātuāyatanapaccayākārapaṭisaṃyuttā. Na aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhapessantīti jānanatthāya cittaṃ na ṭhapessanti. Uggahetabbaṃ pariyāpuṇitabbanti uggahetabbe ca vaḷañjetabbe ca. Kavitāti silokādibandhanavasena kavīhi katā. Kāveyyāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Bāhirakāti sāsanato bahiddhā ṭhitā. Sāvakabhāsitāti bāhirasāvakehi bhāsitā. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayattā suviññeyyattā ca uttānatthameva.

'Profound' means profound in terms of the Pali text. 'Profound in meaning' means profound in terms of the meaning. 'Supramundane' means they illuminate the supramundane Dhamma. 'Connected with emptiness' means connected with the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and dependent origination. 'They will not apply the mind to final knowledge' means they will not establish the mind for the purpose of knowing. 'To be learned and mastered' means that which should be learned and that which should be practiced. 'Composed by poets' means composed by poets by way of constructing verses and so on. 'Poetic works' is a synonym for that very term. 'External' means those who stand outside the Dispensation. 'Spoken by disciples' means spoken by the disciples of external sectarians. The rest here, because the method has been stated previously and it is easy to understand, is plain in meaning.

10. Catutthaanāgatabhayasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Fourth Discourse on Future Dangers

80. Dasame kalyāṇakāmāti sundarakāmā. Rasaggānīti uttamarasāni. Saṃsaṭṭhā viharissantīti pañcavidhena saṃsaggena saṃsaṭṭhā viharissanti. Sannidhikāraparibhoganti sannidhikatassa paribhogaṃ. Oḷārikampi nimittanti ettha pathaviṃ khaṇantopi khaṇāhīti āṇāpentopi pathaviyaṃ oḷārikaṃ nimittaṃ karoti nāma. Tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ chindantopi chindāti āṇāpentopi haritagge [P 3.0273] oḷārikaṃ nimittaṃ karoti nāma. Ājīvatthāya paṇṇanivāpaādīni [V 3.0038] gāhāpento phalāni ocinante vā ocināpentena vattabbameva natthi. Imesu catūsu suttesu satthārā sāsane vuddhiparihāni kathitāti.

80. In the tenth discourse, 'desiring what is fine' means desiring what is beautiful. 'The finest tastes' means the supreme tastes. 'They will live associated' means they will live associated by five kinds of association. 'Enjoying what has been stored' means the enjoyment of what has been stored. Regarding 'also a gross sign': here, one who digs the earth, or orders someone to dig, is said to make a gross sign on the earth. One who cuts grass, sticks, branches, or leaves, or orders someone to cut, is said to make a gross sign on green growth. For the sake of livelihood, there is nothing at all to be said of one who causes leaves for fodder and so on to be taken, or of one who picks fruits or causes them to be picked. In these four discourses, the Teacher has spoken of growth and decline in the Dispensation.

Yodhājīvavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Warriors.

(9) 4. Theravaggo

(9) 4. The Chapter on the Elders

1. Rajanīyasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sutta on What is Alluring

81. Catutthassa [M 3.0038] paṭhame rajanīyesūti rāgassa paccayesu ārammaṇesu. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

81. In the first sutta of the fourth chapter, 'in what is alluring' means in objects that are conditions for lust. In the remaining instances as well, this is the method.

2. Vītarāgasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Sutta on One Free from Passion

82. Dutiye makkhīti guṇamakkhako. Paḷāsīti yugaggāhalakkhaṇena paḷāsena samannāgato.

82. In the second sutta, 'one who is denigrating' means one who disparages good qualities. 'One who is spiteful' means one endowed with spite, which is characterized by partisanship.

3. Kuhakasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sutta on the Deceiver

83. Tatiye kuhakoti tīhi kuhanavatthūhi samannāgato. Lapakoti lābhasannissitāya lapanāya samannāgato. Nemittikoti nimittakiriyakārako. Nippesikoti nippesanakatāya samannāgato. Lābhena ca lābhaṃ nijigīsitāti lābhena lābhagavesako. Sukkapakkho vuttavipallāsavasena veditabbo. Catutthaṃ uttānameva.

83. In the third sutta, 'a deceiver' means one endowed with the three bases of deception. 'A flatterer' means one endowed with flattery dependent on gain. 'A sign-maker' means one who makes signs. 'A coercer' means one endowed with coercive speech. 'And seeking to gain much by means of gain' means one who seeks gain by means of gain. The wholesome side should be understood by way of the opposite of what has been stated. The fourth sutta is self-evident.

5. Akkhamasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Sutta on the Intolerant

85. Pañcame [V 3.0039] akkhamo hoti rūpānanti rūpārammaṇānaṃ anadhivāsako hoti, tadārammaṇehi rāgādīhi abhibhuyyati. Eseva nayo sabbattha.

85. In the fifth sutta, 'he is intolerant of forms' means he is unable to endure visual-form objects, being overwhelmed by lust and other defilements related to them. This is the method in all instances.

6. Paṭisambhidāppattasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sutta on One Who Has Attained the Analytical Knowledges

86. Chaṭṭhe [P 3.0274] atthapaṭisambhidāppattoti pañcasu atthesu pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ patto. Dhammapaṭisambhidāppattoti catubbidhe dhamme pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ patto. Niruttipaṭisambhidāppattoti dhammaniruttīsu pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ patto. Paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāppattoti tesu tīsu ñāṇesu pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ patto. So pana tāni tīṇi ñāṇāneva jānāti, na tesaṃ kiccaṃ karoti. Uccāvacānīti mahantakhuddakāni. Kiṃkaraṇīyānīti iti kattabbāni.

86. In the sixth sutta, 'one who has attained the analytical knowledge of meaning' means one who has attained the knowledge that has penetrated the distinctions in the five kinds of meanings. 'One who has attained the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma' means one who has attained the knowledge that has penetrated the distinctions in the fourfold Dhamma. 'One who has attained the analytical knowledge of language' means one who has attained the knowledge that has penetrated the distinctions in the linguistic expressions of the Dhamma. 'One who has attained the analytical knowledge of perspicuity' means one who has attained the knowledge that has penetrated the distinctions in those three knowledges. However, he only knows those three knowledges; he does not perform their function. 'High and low' means great and small. 'What is to be done' means 'things to be performed thus'.

7. Sīlavantasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Sīlavanta Sutta

87. Sattamaṃ [M 3.0039] uttānatthameva. Sīlaṃ panettha khīṇāsavasīlameva, bāhusaccampi khīṇāsavabāhusaccameva, vācāpi khīṇāsavassa kalyāṇavācāva, jhānānipi kiriyajjhānāneva kathitānīti veditabbāni.

87. The seventh is self-explanatory. It should be understood that herein, the virtue spoken of is only the virtue of one whose taints are destroyed, the extensive learning is only the extensive learning of one whose taints are destroyed, the speech is also only the good speech of one whose taints are destroyed, and the jhānas spoken of are only functional jhānas.

8. Therasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Thera Sutta
