88. Aṭṭhame theroti thirabhāvappatto. Rattaññūti pabbajitadivasato paṭṭhāya atikkantānaṃ bahūnaṃ rattīnaṃ ñātā. Ñātoti paññāto pākaṭo. Yasassīti yasanissito. Micchādiṭṭhikoti ayāthāvadiṭṭhiko. Saddhammā vuṭṭhāpetvāti dasakusalakammapathadhammato vuṭṭhāpetvā. Asaddhamme patiṭṭhāpetīti akusalakammapathesu patiṭṭhāpeti.

88. In the eighth, 'thera' means one who has attained a state of stability. 'Rattaññū' means one who knows the many nights that have passed since the day of ordination. 'Ñāta' means well-known and manifest. 'Yasassī' means one who is attended by a retinue. 'Micchādiṭṭhika' means one who has a distorted view. 'Having caused to rise up from the true Dhamma' means having caused to rise up from the Dhamma of the ten wholesome paths of action. 'Establishes in the false Dhamma' means establishes in the unwholesome paths of action.

9. Paṭhamasekhasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the First Sekha Sutta

89. Navame [V 3.0040] sekhassāti sikkhakassa sakaraṇīyassa. Parihānāyāti upariguṇehi parihānatthāya. Kammārāmatāti navakamme ramanakabhāvo. Bhassārāmatāti [P 3.0275] ālāpasallāpe ramanakabhāvo. Niddārāmatāti niddāyane ramanakabhāvo. Saṅgaṇikārāmatāti gaṇasaṅgaṇikāya ramanakabhāvo. Yathāvimuttaṃ cittaṃ na paccavekkhatīti yathā yaṃ cittaṃ vimuttaṃ, ye ca dosā pahīnā, guṇā ca paṭiladdhā, te paccavekkhitvā upariguṇapaṭilābhāya vāyāmaṃ na karotīti attho. Iti imasmiṃ sutte sattannaṃ sekhānaṃ upariguṇehi parihānikāraṇañca vuddhikāraṇañca kathitaṃ. Yañca nāma sekhassa parihānakāraṇaṃ, taṃ puthujjanassa paṭhamameva hotīti.

89. In the ninth, 'of a trainee' means of one who trains, who has a duty to perform. 'For decline' means for the purpose of decline from higher qualities. 'Delight in work' means the state of delighting in new work. 'Delight in talk' means the state of delighting in initiating talk and conversation. 'Delight in sleep' means the state of delighting in sleeping. 'Delight in company' means the state of delighting in association with a group. 'Does not review the mind as it is liberated' means that one does not reflect on from which faults the mind has been liberated, which faults have been abandoned, and which qualities attained, and thus does not strive for the attainment of higher qualities. Thus, in this sutta, the cause for decline from and the cause for growth in higher qualities for the seven kinds of trainees are taught. And whatever is a cause of decline for a trainee, that is a cause of decline for an ordinary person from the very beginning.

10. Dutiyasekhasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Second Sekha Sutta

90. Dasame viyattoti byatto cheko. Kiṃkaraṇīyesūti iti kattabbesu. Cetosamathanti samādhikammaṭṭhānaṃ. Ananulomikenāti sāsanassa ananucchavikena. Atikālenāti atipātova. Atidivāti divā vuccati majjhanhiko, taṃ atikkamitvā. Ābhisallekhikāti ativiya kilesasallekhikā. Cetovivaraṇasappāyāti cittavivaraṇasaṅkhātānaṃ samathavipassanānaṃ sappāyā. Appicchakathāti appicchā hothāti [M 3.0040] kathanakathā. Santuṭṭhikathāti catūhi paccayehi santuṭṭhā hothāti kathanakathā. Pavivekakathāti tīhi vivekehi vivittā hothāti kathanakathā. Asaṃsaggakathāti pañcavidhena saṃsaggena asaṃsaṭṭhā hothāti kathanakathā. Vīriyārambhakathāti duvidhaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhathāti kathanakathā. Sīlakathādīsu sīlaṃ ārabbha kathā sīlakathā. Samādhiṃ ārabbha, paññaṃ ārabbha, pañcavidhaṃ [P 3.0276] vimuttiṃ ārabbha, ekūnavīsatipaccavekkhaṇasaṅkhātaṃ vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ ārabbha kathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā. Na nikāmalābhītiādīsu na icchiticchitalābhī, dukkhalābhī na vipulalābhīti attho. Sesaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

90. In the tenth, 'skilled' means intelligent and clever. 'In what should be done' means in what ought to be done. 'Calm of mind' means the meditation subject of concentration. 'Unsuitably' means unfitting for the teaching. 'At the wrong time' means too early. 'Too late in the day' means having passed midday, for 'day' refers to midday. 'Exceedingly effacing' means exceedingly effacing of defilements. 'Conducive to opening the mind' means conducive to tranquility and insight, which are called 'the opening of the mind'. 'Talk on fewness of wishes' is talk advising, “Be of few wishes.” 'Talk on contentment' is talk advising, “Be content with the four requisites.” 'Talk on seclusion' is talk advising, “Be secluded by the three kinds of seclusion.” 'Talk on non-association' is talk advising, “Do not associate by the five kinds of association.” 'Talk on arousing energy' is talk advising, “Arouse the two kinds of energy.” Regarding 'talk on virtue' and so on: talk concerning virtue is 'talk on virtue'; talk concerning concentration is 'talk on concentration'; talk concerning wisdom is 'talk on wisdom'; talk concerning the fivefold liberation is 'talk on liberation'; and talk concerning the knowledge and vision of liberation, which is known as the nineteenfold reviewing, is 'talk on the knowledge and vision of liberation'. In the words beginning with 'not obtaining at will', the meaning is: not obtaining whenever desired, not obtaining without difficulty, and not obtaining abundantly. The rest has a clear meaning.

Theravaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on the Elders.

(10) 5. Kakudhavaggo

(10) 5. The Kakudha Chapter

1-2. Sampadāsuttadvayavaṇṇanā

1–2. Commentary on the Two Discourses on Accomplishment

91-92. Pañcamassa [V 3.0041] paṭhame pañca sampadā missikā kathitā. Dutiye purimā catasso missikā, pañcamī lokikāva.

91–92. In the first sutta of the fifth chapter, five accomplishments are taught as mixed. In the second, the first four are taught as mixed, while the fifth is taught as only worldly.

3. Byākaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on Declarations.

93. Tatiye aññābyākaraṇānīti arahattabyākaraṇāni. Mandattāti mandabhāvena aññāṇena. Momūhattāti atimūḷhabhāvena. Aññaṃ byākarotīti arahattaṃ pattosmīti katheti. Icchāpakatoti icchāya abhibhūto. Adhimānenāti adhigatamānena. Sammadevāti hetunā nayena kāraṇeneva.

93. In the third sutta, 'declarations of final knowledge' means declarations of the fruit of Arahantship. 'Due to dullness' means due to a dull state, due to ignorance. 'Due to delusion' means due to a state of extreme delusion. 'Declares final knowledge' means one says, “I have attained the fruit of Arahantship.” 'Overcome by desire' means being overwhelmed by base desire. 'Due to conceit' means by the conceit of having attained. 'Rightly' means by reason, by method, by cause itself.

4-5. Phāsuvihārasuttādivaṇṇanā

4–5. Commentary on the Discourses on Comfortable Abiding, etc.

94-95. Catutthe phāsuvihārāti sukhavihārā. Pañcame akuppanti arahattaṃ.

94–95. In the fourth sutta, 'comfortable abidings' means pleasant abidings. In the fifth, 'the unshakable' means the fruit of Arahantship.

6. Sutadharasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on One Who Bears the Teachings.

96. Chaṭṭhe [M 3.0041] appaṭṭhoti appasamārambho. Appakiccoti appakaraṇīyo. Subharoti sukhena bharitabbo suposo. Susantosoti tīhi santosehi suṭṭhu santoso. Jīvitaparikkhāresūti jīvitasambhāresu. Appāhāroti mandāhāro. Anodarikattanti na odarikabhāvaṃ amahagghasabhāvaṃ anuyutto. Appamiddhoti [P 3.0277] na bahuniddo. Sattamaṭṭhamāni uttānatthāni.

96. In the sixth sutta, 'appaṭṭho' means having little undertaking. 'Appakicco' means having few duties to perform. 'Subharo' means easily supported, well supported. 'Susantoso' means well content with the three kinds of contentment. 'Jīvitaparikkhāresu' means in the supports of life. 'Appāhāro' means having little food. 'Anodarikattaṃ' means being devoted to not filling the belly, to not being a big eater. 'Appamiddho' means not sleeping much. The seventh and eighth suttas have a clear meaning.

9. Sīhasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Discourse on the Lion.

99. Navame [V 3.0042] sakkaccaññeva deti no asakkaccanti anavaññāya avirajjhitvāva deti, no avaññāya virajjhitvā. Mā me yoggapatho nassāti mayā katayoggapatho mayhaṃ mā nassatu, “eko sīho uṭṭhāya biḷāraṃ paharanto virajjhitvā paharī”ti evaṃ vattāro mā hontūti attho. Annabhāranesādānanti ettha annaṃ vuccati yavabhattaṃ, taṃ bhāro etesanti annabhārā. Yācakānaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ. Nesādā vuccanti sākuṇikā. Iti sabbapacchimāya koṭiyā etesaṃ yācakanesādānampi sakkaccameva deseti.

99. In the ninth sutta, 'sakkaccaññeva deti no asakkaccaṃ' means: one gives without contempt and without failing, not with contempt and having failed. 'Mā me yoggapatho nassā' means: ‘May the path of endeavor made by me not be lost to me.’ The meaning is: let there not be those who say, ‘A lion, rising up to strike a cat, struck having failed.’ Regarding 'annabhāranesādānaṃ': here, 'anna' is said to be barley-meal; those for whom that is a burden are 'annabhārā'. This is a name for beggars. 'Nesādā' are said to be fowlers. Thus, at the very last extreme, he teaches even these beggar-fowlers with respect.

10. Kakudhatherasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Discourse about the Elder Kakudha.

100. Dasame attabhāvapaṭilābhoti sarīrapaṭilābho. Dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakkhettānīti ettha māgadhikaṃ gāmakkhettaṃ atthi khuddakaṃ, atthi majjhimaṃ, atthi mahantaṃ. Khuddakaṃ gāmakkhettaṃ ito cattālīsaṃ usabhāni, ito cattālīsanti gāvutaṃ hoti, majjhimaṃ ito gāvutaṃ, ito gāvutanti aḍḍhayojanaṃ hoti, mahantaṃ ito diyaḍḍhagāvutaṃ, ito diyaḍḍhagāvutanti tigāvutaṃ hoti. Tesu khuddakena gāmakkhettena tīṇi, khuddakena ca majjhimena ca dve gāmakkhettāni tassa attabhāvo. Tigāvutañhissa sarīraṃ. Pariharissāmīti paṭijaggissāmi gopayissāmi. Rakkhassetanti rakkhassu etaṃ. Moghapurisoti tucchapuriso. Nāssassāti na [M 3.0042] etassa bhaveyya. Samudācareyyāmāti [P 3.0278] katheyyāma. Sammannatīti sammānaṃ karoti. Yaṃ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatīti yaṃ esa karissati, esova tena kammena pākaṭo bhavissati. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

100. In the tenth sutta, 'attabhāvapaṭilābho' means the acquisition of a body. Regarding 'dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakkhettāni' ('two or three Magadhan village fields'): here, a Magadhan village field can be small, medium, or large. A small village field is forty usabhas from the center in one direction and forty in the other, making a gāvuta. A medium one is a gāvuta from the center in one direction and a gāvuta in the other, making half a yojana. A large one is one and a half gāvutas from the center in one direction and one and a half in the other, making three gāvutas. Among these, his individual existence is the size of three small village fields, or two village fields (a small and a medium one). Indeed, his body is three gāvutas. 'Pariharissāmi' means ‘I will look after it,’ ‘I will protect it.’ 'Rakkhassetaṃ' is to be divided as 'rakkhassu etaṃ' (‘protect this’). 'Moghapuriso' means a worthless man. 'Nāssassā' means ‘may it not be for him.’ 'Samudācareyyāma' means ‘should we speak?’ 'Sammannati' means one pays respect. 'Yaṃ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī' means: whatever this one does, by that very deed he will become manifest. The rest has a clear meaning everywhere.

Kakudhavaggo pañcamo.

The Kakudha Chapter, the Fifth.

Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Fifty is Concluded.

3. Tatiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ

3. The Third Fifty

(11) 1. Phāsuvihāravaggo

(11) 1. The Chapter on Pleasant Living

1. Sārajjasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sārajja Sutta

101. Tatiyassa [M 3.0043][V 3.0043] paṭhame vesārajjakaraṇāti visāradabhāvāvahā. Sārajjaṃ hotīti domanassaṃ hoti.

101. In the first sutta of the third chapter, 'vesārajjakaraṇā' means bringing about fearlessness. 'Sārajjaṃ hoti' means sorrow arises.

2. Ussaṅkitasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Ussaṅkita Sutta

102. Dutiye ussaṅkitaparisaṅkitoti ussaṅkito ca parisaṅkito ca. Api akuppadhammopīti api akuppadhammo khīṇāsavo samānopi parehi pāpabhikkhūhi ussaṅkitaparisaṅkito hotīti attho. Vesiyāgocarotiādīsu vesiyā vuccanti rūpūpajīviniyo, tā gocaro assāti vesiyāgocaro, tāsaṃ gehaṃ abhiṇhagamanoti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Tattha pana vidhavāti matapatikā. Thullakumārikāti mahallikakumārikāyo.

102. In the second sutta, 'ussaṅkitaparisaṅkito' means both suspected and distrusted. 'Api akuppadhammopīti' means that even an Arahant, one who is of an unshakeable nature whose taints are destroyed, may be suspected and distrusted by others as a wicked monk—this is the meaning. Regarding 'frequenting courtesans' and so forth: 'vesiyā' are called women who live by their beauty; 'vesiyāgocaro' means that they are his resort, meaning frequently going to their houses. The same applies to other cases. Here, 'vidhavā' means a woman whose husband has died. 'Thullakumārikā' means older unmarried girls.

3. Mahācorasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Great Robber Sutta

103. Tatiye ito bhogena paṭisantharissāmīti ito mama sāpateyyato bhogaṃ gahetvā tena paṭisanthāraṃ karissāmi, tassa ca mama ca antaraṃ pidahissāmīti attho. Gahaṇānīti [P 3.0279] parasantakānaṃ bhaṇḍānaṃ gahaṇāni. Guyhamantāti guhitabbamantā. Antaggāhikāyāti sassataṃ vā ucchedaṃ vā gahetvā ṭhitāya. Sesamettha uttānatthameva. Catutthe sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

103. In the third sutta, 'I will treat him with hospitality from here through wealth' means: 'I will take wealth from my own property and with that I will provide hospitality, and I will close the gap between him and me'—this is the meaning. 'Gahaṇāni' means the takings of goods belonging to others. 'Guyhamantā' means secret counsel. 'Antaggāhikāya' means a view clinging to eternalism or annihilationism. The rest here is straightforward in meaning. In the fourth sutta, everything is in accordance with the method already stated.

5. Phāsuvihārasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse on Comfortable Dwelling

105. Pañcame mettaṃ kāyakammanti mettacittena pavattitaṃ kāyakammaṃ. Āvi ceva raho cāti [V 3.0044] sammukhe ceva parammukhe ca. Itaresupi eseva nayo. Yāni tāni sīlānītiādi catupārisuddhisīlavasena vuttaṃ. Samādhisaṃvattanikānīti [M 3.0044] maggasamādhiphalasamādhinibbattakāni. Sīlasāmaññagatoti samānasīlataṃ gato, ekasadisasīlo hutvāti attho. Takkarassāti yo naṃ karoti, tassa. Iti imasmiṃ sutte sīlaṃ missakaṃ kathitaṃ, diṭṭhi vipassanāsammādiṭṭhīti.

105. In the fifth sutta, 'bodily action of loving-kindness' means bodily action performed with a mind of loving-kindness. 'Both openly and privately' means both in the presence of others and in their absence. The same method applies to the others. 'Those virtues, etc.' refers to what was stated in terms of the fourfold purity of virtue. 'Leading to concentration' means productive of path-concentration and fruition-concentration. 'Endowed with the common virtues' means having attained similar virtue, having virtue of the same kind—this is the meaning. 'For the one who does so' refers to the one who performs it. Thus, in this sutta, virtue is taught, and 'view' is the right view that is insight.

6. Ānandasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Ānanda Sutta

106. Chaṭṭhe no ca paraṃ adhisīle sampavattā hotīti paraṃ sīlabhāvena na garahati na upavadati. Attānupekkhīti attanova katākataṃ jānanavasena attānaṃ anupekkhitā. No parānupekkhīti parassa katākatesu abyāvaṭo. Apaññātoti apākaṭo appapuñño. Apaññātakenāti apaññātabhāvena apākaṭatāya mandapuññatāya. No paritassatīti paritāsaṃ nāpajjati. Iti imasmiṃ sutte khīṇāsavova kathito.

106. In the sixth sutta, 'and does not act with regard to another's higher virtue' means one does not criticize or disparage others on account of their virtue. 'Self-reflective' means being reflective of oneself by knowing one's own actions and omissions. 'Not reflecting on others' means not being concerned with the actions and omissions of others. 'Unrecognized' means unknown, of little merit. 'By being unrecognized' means due to being unknown and of little merit. 'Not agitated' means not experiencing agitation. Thus, in this sutta, it is the one whose taints are destroyed who is spoken of.

7-8. Sīlasuttādivaṇṇanā

7-8. Commentary on the Sīla Sutta, etc.

107-108. Sattame sīlasamādhipaññā missikā kathitā, vimutti arahattaphalaṃ[P 3.0280], vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ lokiyameva. Aṭṭhamepi eseva nayo. Paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ panettha asekhassa pavattattā asekhanti vuttaṃ.

In the seventh discourse, virtue, concentration, and wisdom are spoken of as mixed. Liberation is the fruit of arahantship; the knowledge and vision of liberation is reviewing knowledge, which is only mundane. In the eighth as well, this is the method. Herein, reviewing knowledge is called 'of the non-trainee' because it occurs in a non-trainee.

9-10. Cātuddisasuttādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Cātuddisa Sutta, etc.

109-110. Navame cātuddisoti catūsu disāsu appaṭihatacāro. Imasmimpi sutte khīṇāsavova kathito. Dasame alanti yutto. Idhāpi khīṇāsavova kathito.

In the ninth discourse, 'one of the four directions' means one who has unimpeded movement in the four directions. In this discourse too, only one whose taints are destroyed is spoken of. In the tenth discourse, 'enough' means suitable. Here too, only one whose taints are destroyed is spoken of.

Phāsuvihāravaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter: The Section on Comfortable Abodes.

(12) 2. Andhakavindavaggo

The Andhakavinda Chapter

1. Kulūpakasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Kulūpaka Sutta.

111. Dutiyassa [V 3.0045] paṭhame asanthavavissāsīti attanā saddhiṃ santhavaṃ akarontesu vissāsaṃ anāpajjantesuyeva vissāsaṃ karoti. Anissaravikappīti [M 3.0045] anissarova samāno “imaṃ detha, imaṃ gaṇhathā”ti issaro viya vikappeti. Vissaṭṭhupasevīti vissaṭṭhāni bhinnakulāni ghaṭanatthāya upasevati. Upakaṇṇakajappīti kaṇṇamūle mantaṃ gaṇhāti. Sukkapakkho vuttavipariyāyena veditabbo.

111. In the first discourse of the second chapter, 'one who trusts without intimacy' means one places trust only in those who do not form intimacy with oneself, in those who do not become familiar. 'One who arranges things without being a master' means, though not a master, one arranges things as if a master, saying, “Give this, take this.” 'One who associates with the dispersed' means one associates with broken families for the sake of uniting them. 'One who whispers in the ear' means one takes counsel near the ear. The bright side should be understood as the opposite of what was stated.

2. Pacchāsamaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Pacchāsamaṇa Sutta.

112. Dutiye pattapariyāpannaṃ na gaṇhātīti upajjhāye nivattitvā ṭhite attano tucchapattaṃ datvā tassa pattaṃ na gaṇhāti, tato vā dīyamānaṃ na gaṇhāti. Na nivāretīti idaṃ vacanaṃ āpattivītikkamavacanaṃ nāmāti [P 3.0281] na jānāti. Ñatvā vāpi, “bhante, evarūpaṃ nāma vattuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti na nivāreti. Kathaṃ opātetīti tassa kathaṃ bhinditvā attano kathaṃ paveseti. Jaḷoti jaḍo. Eḷamūgoti paggharitakheḷamukho. Tatiyaṃ uttānameva.

112. In the second discourse, 'does not accept what has come into the bowl' means that when the preceptor has returned and is standing, one gives one's own empty bowl and does not take his bowl, or does not take the almsfood being given from it. 'Does not prevent' means one does not know that such an utterance is called an utterance that causes transgression of an offense. Or, even knowing, one does not prevent him by saying, 'Venerable sir, it is not proper to say such a thing.' 'Interrupts the talk' means one breaks his speech and inserts one's own speech. 'Dull' means stupid. 'Slobbering' means having a mouth from which saliva drips. The third discourse is self-evident.

4. Andhakavindasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Andhakavinda Sutta.

114. Catutthe sīlavā hothāti sīlavantā hotha. Ārakkhasatinoti dvārarakkhikāya satiyā samannāgatā. Nipakkasatinoti dvārarakkhanakeneva ñāṇena samannāgatassatino. Satārakkhena cetasā samannāgatāti satārakkhena cittena samannāgatā. Appabhassāti appakathā. Sammādiṭṭhikāti kammassakatajjhāna-vipassanāmagga-phalavasena pañcavidhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgatā. Apica paccavekkhaṇañāṇampi sammādiṭṭhiyevāti veditabbā.

114. In the fourth discourse, 'be virtuous' means 'be possessed of virtue.' 'Those with guarding mindfulness' means those endowed with mindfulness that guards the doors. 'Those with prudent mindfulness' means those endowed with the very knowledge that guards the doors. 'Endowed with a mind guarded by mindfulness' means endowed with a mind that has the guard of mindfulness. 'Of few words' means having little talk. 'Those with right view' means those endowed with the fivefold right view, that is, by way of right view of kamma as one's own, of jhāna, of insight, of the path, and of the fruit. Moreover, it should be understood that reviewing knowledge is also indeed right view.

5. Maccharinīsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Maccharinī Sutta.

115. Pañcame [V 3.0046] āvāsamaccharinīti āvāsaṃ maccharāyati, tattha aññesaṃ vāsaṃ na sahati. Kulamaccharinīti upaṭṭhākakulaṃ maccharāyati, aññesaṃ tattha upasaṅkamanaṃ na sahati. Lābhamaccharinīti lābhaṃ maccharāyati, aññesaṃ taṃ uppajjantaṃ na sahati. Vaṇṇamaccharinīti guṇaṃ maccharāyati, aññesaṃ guṇakathaṃ na sahati. Dhammamaccharinīti [P 3.0282] pariyattidhammaṃ maccharāyati, aññesaṃ dātuṃ na icchati.

115. In the fifth discourse, 'miserly with dwellings' means she is miserly with a monastery and cannot bear others living there. 'Miserly with families' means she is miserly with a supporter family and cannot bear others visiting them. 'Miserly with gains' means she is miserly with gains and cannot bear them arising for others. 'Miserly with praise' means she is miserly with her good qualities and cannot bear talk of others' good qualities. 'Miserly with the Dhamma' means she is miserly with the Dhamma of learning and does not wish to give it to others.

6-7. Vaṇṇanāsuttādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourses beginning with the Vaṇṇanā Sutta.

116-117. Chaṭṭhe [M 3.0046] saddhādeyyaṃ vinipātetīti parehi saddhāya dinnapiṇḍapātato aggaṃ aggahetvā parassa deti. Sattame issukinīti issāya samannāgatā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

In the sixth discourse, 'she destroys faith-given offerings' means that without taking the first portion from almsfood given in faith by others, she gives it to another. In the seventh discourse, 'envious' means endowed with envy. The rest is clear in all instances.

Andhakavindavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter: The Andhakavinda.

(13) 3. Gilānavaggo

The Chapter on the Sick.

4. Dutiyaupaṭṭhākasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Second Upaṭṭhāka Sutta.

124. Tatiyassa catutthe nappaṭibaloti kāyabalena ca ñāṇabalena ca asamannāgato. Āmisantaroti āmisahetuko cīvarādīni paccāsīsamāno.

124. In the fourth discourse of the third chapter, 'incapable' means not endowed with physical strength and the strength of knowledge. 'Motivated by material gain' means having material gain as a motive, expecting robes and other requisites.

5-6. Anāyussāsuttadvayavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Pair of Discourses on What Is Not Conducive to Long Life.

125-126. Pañcame [V 3.0047] anāyussāti āyupacchedanā, na āyuvaḍḍhanā. Chaṭṭhepi eseva nayo.

In the fifth discourse, 'not conducive to long life' means they are causes for the cutting off of life, not for the increase of life. In the sixth discourse also, this is the method.

7. Vapakāsasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Vapakāsa Sutta.

127. Sattame nālaṃ saṅghamhā vapakāsitunti saṅghato nikkhamitvā ekako vasituṃ na yutto. Kāmañcesa saṅghamajjhepi vasituṃ ayuttova asaṅghasobhanatāya, ovādānusāsanippaṭibaddhattā pana nippariyāyeneva saṅghamhā vapakāsituṃ na yutto. Alaṃ saṅghamhā vapakāsitunti cātuddisattā saṅghamhā nikkhamma ekako vasituṃ yutto, saṅghasobhanatāya pana saṅghepi vasituṃ yuttoyeva. Aṭṭhamaṃ uttānatthameva.

127. In the seventh discourse, 'not fit to withdraw from the Sangha' means it is not proper to leave the Sangha and live alone. Although it is indeed improper for him to live in the midst of the Sangha because he does not adorn the Sangha, yet because he is bound to receive admonition and instruction, it is absolutely not proper to withdraw from the Sangha. 'Fit to withdraw from the Sangha' means that because he is one of the four directions, it is proper to leave the Sangha and live alone; however, because he is an adornment to the Sangha, it is also proper to live within the Sangha. The eighth discourse is clear in meaning.

9. Parikuppasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Parikuppa Sutta.

129. Navame āpāyikāti apāyagāmino. Nerayikāti nirayagāmino. Parikuppāti [P 3.0283] parikuppanasabhāvā purāṇavaṇasadisā. Atekicchāti akattabbaparikammā. Dasamaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

129. In the ninth discourse, 'destined for the plane of misery' means those who are heading to the woeful states. 'Destined for hell' means those who are heading to hell. 'Irrevocably ruined' means having a nature that is ruined, like an old wound. 'Incurable' means one for whom a remedy cannot be undertaken. The tenth discourse is clear in meaning.

Gilānavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter: On the Sick.

(14) 4. Rājavaggo

The Chapter on Kings.

1. Paṭhamacakkānuvattanasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Discourse on the Rolling Onward of the Wheel.

131. Catutthassa [M 3.0047] paṭhame dhammenāti dasakusaladhammena. Cakkanti āṇācakkaṃ. Atthaññūti rajjatthaṃ jānāti. Dhammaññūti paveṇidhammaṃ jānāti. Mattaññūti daṇḍe vā balamhi vā pamāṇaṃ jānāti. Kālaññūti rajjasukhānubhavanakālaṃ, vinicchayakaraṇakālaṃ, janapadacārikākālañca [V 3.0048] jānāti. Parisaññūti ayaṃ parisā khattiyaparisā, ayaṃ brāhmaṇavessasuddasamaṇaparisāti jānāti.

131. In the first discourse of the fourth chapter, 'by Dhamma' means by the ten wholesome principles. 'Wheel' means the wheel of command. 'Knower of what is beneficial' means one who knows what is for the good of the kingdom. 'Knower of the Dhamma' means one who knows the traditional law. 'Knower of measure' means one who knows the measure in punishment or in force. 'Knower of time' means one who knows the time for experiencing the bliss of kingship, the time for making judgments, and the time for touring the country. 'Knower of assemblies' means one who knows: 'This is an assembly of nobles, this is an assembly of brahmins, merchants, commoners, or ascetics.'

Tathāgatavāre atthaññūti pañca atthe jānāti. Dhammaññūti cattāro dhamme jānāti. Mattaññūti catūsu paccayesu paṭiggahaṇaparibhogamattaṃ jānāti. Kālaññūti ayaṃ kālo paṭisallīnassa, ayaṃ samāpattiyā, ayaṃ dhammadesanāya, ayaṃ janapadacārikāyāti evaṃ kālaṃ jānāti. Parisaññūti ayaṃ parisā khattiyaparisā…pe… ayaṃ samaṇaparisāti jānāti. Anuttaranti navahi lokuttaradhammehi anuttaraṃ. Dhammacakkanti seṭṭhacakkaṃ.

In the section on the Tathāgata, 'knower of what is beneficial' means one who knows the five benefits. 'Knower of the Dhamma' means one who knows the four truths. 'Knower of measure' means one who knows the measure in receiving and using the four requisites. 'Knower of time' means one who knows the time thus: 'This is the time for seclusion, this for attainment, this for teaching the Dhamma, this for wandering in the country.' 'Knower of assemblies' means one who knows: 'This is an assembly of nobles... this is an assembly of ascetics.' 'Unsurpassed' means unsurpassed by the nine supramundane dhammas. 'The Wheel of Dhamma' means the excellent wheel.

2. Dutiyacakkānuvattanasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Discourse on the Rolling Onward of the Wheel

132. Dutiye pitarā pavattitaṃ cakkanti cakkavattimhi pabbajite vā kālakate vā cakkaratanaṃ sattāhamattaṃ ṭhatvā antaradhāyati, kathamesa taṃ anuppavatteti nāma? Pitu paveṇiyaṃ [P 3.0284] ṭhatvā cakkavattivattaṃ pūretvā cakkavattirajjaṃ kārentopi pitarā pavattitameva anuppavatteti nāma.

132. In the second sutta, regarding 'the wheel set in motion by the father': when a wheel-turning monarch has gone forth or passed away, the wheel-treasure, having remained for just seven days, disappears. How then is it said that one causes it to roll onward? By standing in the father's tradition, fulfilling the duties of a wheel-turning monarch, and ruling the kingdom as a wheel-turning monarch, one is said to cause to roll onward that very wheel which was set in motion by the father.

3. Dhammarājāsuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Dhammarāja Sutta

133. Tatiyaṃ tikanipāte vuttanayameva. Sevitabbāsevitabbe panettha pacchimapadadvayameva viseso. Tattha sammāājīvo sevitabbo, micchāājīvo na sevitabbo. Sappāyo gāmanigamo sevitabbo, asappāyo na sevitabbo.

133. The third sutta has the same method as that stated in the Tikanipāta. Here, the distinction is only in the last two pairs of terms concerning what should be resorted to and what should not be resorted to. Therein, right livelihood is to be pursued, and wrong livelihood is not to be pursued. A suitable village or town is to be frequented; an unsuitable one is not to be frequented.

4. Yassaṃdisaṃsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Yassaṃdisaṃ Sutta

134. Catutthe [M 3.0048] ubhatoti dvīhipi pakkhehi. Mātito ca pitito cāti yassa hi mātā khattiyā, mātumātā khattiyā, tassāpi mātā khattiyā. Pitā khattiyo, pitupitā khattiyo, tassapi pitā khattiyo. So ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca. Saṃsuddhagahaṇikoti saṃsuddhāya mātukucchiyā samannāgato. “Samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā”ti ettha pana [V 3.0049] kammajatejodhātu gahaṇīti vuccati. Yāva sattamā pitāmahayugāti ettha pitupitā pitāmaho, pitāmahassa yugaṃ pitāmahayugaṃ. Yuganti āyuppamāṇaṃ vuccati. Abhilāpamattameva cetaṃ, atthato pana pitāmahoyeva pitāmahayugaṃ. Tato uddhaṃ sabbepi pubbapurisā pitāmahaggahaṇeneva gahitā. Evaṃ yāva sattamo puriso, tāva saṃsuddhagahaṇiko, atha vā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādenāti dasseti. Akkhittoti “apanetha etaṃ, kiṃ iminā”ti evaṃ akkhitto anavakkhitto. Anupakkuṭṭhoti na upakkuṭṭho na akkosaṃ vā nindaṃ vā pattapubbo. Kena [P 3.0285] kāraṇenāti? Jātivādena, “itipi hīnajātiko eso”ti evarūpena vacanenāti attho.

134. In the fourth sutta, 'from both sides' means from both parties. 'From the mother's side and from the father's side' means that his mother is of noble birth, his maternal grandmother is of noble birth, and her mother is also of noble birth. His father is of noble birth, his paternal grandfather is of noble birth, and his father is also of noble birth. Thus, he is well-born from both sides, from his mother's and his father's. 'Of pure conception' means endowed with a pure mother's womb. In the phrase 'with a womb of even ripening,' the kamma-born fire element is called 'gahaṇī' (womb). In the phrase 'up to the seventh paternal-grandfather-generation,' the father's father is the 'pitāmaha' (paternal grandfather), and the generation of the paternal grandfather is the 'pitāmahayuga.' 'Yuga' (generation) refers to the lifespan. This is just a figure of speech; in terms of meaning, the paternal grandfather himself is the 'paternal-grandfather-generation.' Above that, all male ancestors are included by the term 'paternal grandfather.' Thus, up to the seventh man, he is of pure conception. Alternatively, it shows that he is 'not cast off, not reviled, by speech concerning birth.' 'Not cast off' means not cast off or rejected thus: 'Remove this person! What is the use of him?' 'Not reviled' means not reviled; he has never before been subject to abuse or blame. For what reason? By speech concerning birth; that is, by speech of such a kind as, 'This person is of low birth'—this is the meaning.

Aḍḍhotiādīsu yo koci attano santakena vibhavena aḍḍho hoti. Idha pana na kevalaṃ aḍḍhoyeva, mahaddhano mahatā aparimāṇasaṅkhena dhanena samannāgatoti attho. Pañcakāmaguṇavasena mahantā uḷārā bhogā assāti mahābhogo. Paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāroti koso vuccati bhaṇḍāgāraṃ, nidahitvā ṭhapitena dhanena paripuṇṇakoso, dhaññena ca paripuṇṇakoṭṭhāgāroti attho. Atha vā catubbidho koso hatthī assā rathā raṭṭhanti, tividhaṃ koṭṭhāgāraṃ dhanakoṭṭhāgāraṃ dhaññakoṭṭhāgāraṃ vatthakoṭṭhāgāranti. Taṃ sabbampi paripuṇṇamassāti paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro. Assavāyāti kassaci bahumpi dhanaṃ dentassa senā na suṇāti, sā anassavā nāma hoti. Kassaci adentassāpi suṇātiyeva, ayaṃ assavā nāma. Ovādapaṭikarāyāti “idaṃ vo kattabba, idaṃ na kattabba”nti dinnaovādakarāya. Paṇḍitoti paṇḍiccena samannāgato. Byattoti paññāveyyattiyena yutto. Medhāvīti ṭhānuppattikapaññāya [M 3.0049] samannāgato. Paṭibaloti samattho. Atthe cintetunti vaḍḍhiatthe cintetuṃ. So hi paccuppannaatthavaseneva “atītepi evaṃ ahesuṃ, anāgatepi evaṃ bhavissantī”ti cinteti. Vijitāvīnanti vijitavijayānaṃ, mahantena vā vijayena samannāgatānaṃ. Vimuttacittānanti pañcahi vimuttīhi vimuttamānasānaṃ.

In terms such as 'aḍḍho' (wealthy), anyone is wealthy with their own possessions. But here, it is not merely being wealthy, but 'mahaddhano' (greatly wealthy), meaning endowed with great and immeasurably vast wealth. He is 'mahābhogo' (of great enjoyments) because he has great and magnificent enjoyments by way of the five strands of sensual pleasure. 'Paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro' (with full treasury and storehouses): a treasury is called a 'kosa'; his treasury is full with wealth that has been stored away, and his storehouse ('koṭṭhāgāra') is full with grain—this is the meaning. Alternatively, the 'kosa' is fourfold: elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry; and the 'koṭṭhāgāra' is threefold: a storehouse for wealth, a storehouse for grain, and a storehouse for cloth. All of these are full for him, thus he is 'paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro.' 'Assavā' (influential): for a certain king, even when giving much wealth, the army does not listen; that army is called 'anassavā' (uninfluential). For another, even without giving, the army listens; this one is called 'assavā.' 'Ovādapaṭikarā' (acting on advice) means acting on the given instruction: 'This should be done by you; this should not be done by you.' 'Paṇḍito' (wise) means endowed with wisdom. 'Byatto' (competent) means possessed of keen intelligence. 'Medhāvī' (intelligent) means endowed with situational intelligence. 'Paṭibalo' (capable) means able. 'To consider what is beneficial' means to ponder matters of progress. Indeed, based on the present benefit, he thinks: 'Thus it was in the past, and thus it will be in the future.' 'Vijitāvīnaṃ' (of the victorious) means of those who have conquered their enemies, or of those endowed with a great victory. 'Vimuttacittānaṃ' (of those with liberated minds) means of those whose minds are liberated by the five kinds of liberation.

5-6. Patthanāsuttadvayavaṇṇanā

5-6. Commentary on the Two Discourses on Aspiration

135-136. Pañcame [P 3.0286] negamajānapadassāti nigamavāsino ca raṭṭhavāsino ca janassa. Hatthismintiādīhi hatthiassarathatharudhanulekhamuddāgaṇanādīni soḷasa mahāsippāni dassitāni. Anavayoti [V 3.0050] samattho paripuṇṇo. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Chaṭṭhe oparajjanti uparājabhāvaṃ.

In the fifth sutta, 'of the town and country folk' means of the people dwelling in market towns and in the country. By 'regarding the elephant,' and so on, the sixteen great arts—such as the art of the elephant, the art of the horse, the art of the chariot, the art of the bow, the art of writing, the art of counting on the fingers, the art of calculation, and so on—are shown. 'Without deficiency' means capable, complete. The rest here should be understood according to the method stated below. In the sixth sutta, 'they appoint as viceroy' means the state of being a viceroy.

7. Appaṃsupatisuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Appaṃsupati Sutta

137. Sattame purisādhippāyāti assaddhammavasena purise uppannādhippāyā purisajjhāsayā. Ādānādhippāyoti idāni gahetuṃ sakkhissāmi, idāni sakkhissāmīti evaṃ gahaṇādhippāyo. Visaṃyogādhippāyoti idāni nibbānaṃ pāpuṇissāmi, idāni pāpuṇissāmīti evaṃ nibbānajjhāsayo.

137. In the seventh sutta, 'having a man as one's aim' means: having an intention that has arisen towards a man by way of ignoble practice; having an inclination for a man. 'Having taking as one's aim' means: having the intention to steal, thinking, 'Now I will be able to take it.' 'Having disengagement as one's aim' means: having an inclination for Nibbāna, thinking, 'Now I will reach Nibbāna.'

8. Bhattādakasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Bhattādaka Sutta

138. Aṭṭhame bhattādakoti bhattakkhādako, bahubhattabhuñjoti attho. Okāsapharaṇoti okāsaṃ pharitvā aññesaṃ sambādhaṃ katvā ṭhānena okāsapharaṇo. Tattha tattha laṇḍaṃ sāreti pātetīti laṇḍasāraṇo. Ettakā hatthīti gaṇanakāle salākaṃ gaṇhātīti salākaggāhī. Nisīdanasayanavasena mañcapīṭhaṃ maddatīti mañcapīṭhamaddano. Bhikkhugaṇanakāle salākaṃ gaṇhātīti salākaggāhī.

138. In the eighth sutta, 'a food-eater' means a food-devourer; the meaning is one who consumes much food. 'One who pervades space' means one who pervades space by standing, having made it constricted for others. 'One who drops dung' is so called because one causes dung to fall here and there. 'A ticket-taker' is so called because at the time of counting, thinking, 'There are this many elephants,' one takes a ticket. 'One who crushes couches and chairs' is so called because one wears down a couch and chair by way of sitting and lying down. 'A ticket-taker' is so called because at the time of counting monks, one takes a ticket.

9. Akkhamasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Akkhama Sutta

139. Navame hatthikāyanti hatthighaṭaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Saṅgāme avacarantīti saṅgāmāvacarā. Ekissā [P 3.0287] vā tiṇodakadattiyā vimānitoti [M 3.0050] ekadivasaṃ ekena tiṇodakadānena vimānito, ekadivasamattaṃ aladdhatiṇodakoti attho. Ito parampi eseva nayo. Na sakkoti cittaṃ samādahitunti ārammaṇe cittaṃ sammā ṭhapetuṃ na sakkoti. Sesamettha uttānameva. Imasmiṃ pana sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitanti veditabbaṃ.

139. In the ninth, 'a body of elephants' means a group of elephants. This is the method in the remaining terms as well. 'They roam in battle,' therefore they are 'battle-roamers.' 'Dishonored by a single offering of grass and water' means: dishonored by a single giving of grass and water on one day; the meaning is not receiving grass and water for just one day. From here on, this is the method. 'One is not able to concentrate the mind' means: one is not able to place the mind well on an object. The rest here has a plain meaning. It should be known that in this sutta, the round of existence and that which is contrary to the round are taught.

10. Sotasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Sota Sutta

140. Dasame [V 3.0051] duruttānanti na suṭṭhu vuttānaṃ dosavasena pavattitānaṃ pharusavacanānaṃ. Durāgatānanti dukkhuppādanākārena sotadvāraṃ āgatānaṃ. Vacanapathānanti vacanānaṃ. Dukkhānanti dukkhamānaṃ. Tibbānanti bahalānaṃ tāpanasabhāvānaṃ vā. Kharānanti pharusānaṃ. Kaṭukānanti tikhiṇānaṃ. Asātānanti amadhurānaṃ. Amanāpānanti manaṃ appāyituṃ vaḍḍhetuṃ asamatthānaṃ. Pāṇaharānanti jīvitaharānaṃ. Yā sā disāti sabbasaṅkhārasamathādivasena dissati apadissatīti nibbānaṃ disāti veditabbaṃ. Yasmā pana taṃ āgamma sabbe saṅkhārā samathaṃ gacchanti, tasmā sabbasaṅkhārasamathoti vuttaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Imasmiṃ pana sutte sīlasamādhipaññā missikā kathitāti.

140. In the tenth, 'of ill-spoken words' means of harsh words that are not well-spoken, that are produced by way of aversion. 'Of those that have come badly' means of those that have come to the ear-door in a manner that produces suffering. 'Of paths of speech' means of words. 'Of painful things' means of those that are hard to endure. 'Of intense things' means of those that are thick, or of those that have a tormenting nature. 'Of harsh things' means of those that are rough. 'Of bitter things' means of those that are sharp. 'Of disagreeable things' means of those that are not sweet. 'Of unlovely things' means of those unable to please or cause the mind to grow. 'Of life-taking things' means of those that take away life. 'That direction' should be known as Nibbāna, which is pointed out by way of the stilling of all conditioned things, and so on. And because, having reached it, all conditioned things go to stillness, therefore it is called 'the stilling of all conditioned things.' The rest is plain everywhere. Furthermore, in this sutta, virtue, concentration, and wisdom are taught as mixed.

Rājavaggo catuttho.

The Royal Chapter, the Fourth.

(15) 5. Tikaṇḍakīvaggo

(15) 5. The Tikaṇḍakī Chapter

1. Avajānātisuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Avajānāti Sutta

141. Pañcamassa [P 3.0288] paṭhame saṃvāsenāti ekatovāsena. Ādeyyamukhoti ādiyanamukho, gahaṇamukhoti attho. Tamenaṃ datvā avajānātīti “ayaṃ dinnaṃ paṭiggahetumeva jānātī”ti evaṃ avamaññati. Tamenaṃ saṃvāsena avajānātīti appamattake kismiñcideva kujjhitvā “jānāmahaṃ tayā katakammaṃ, ettakaṃ addhānaṃ ahaṃ kiṃ karonto vasiṃ, nanu tuyhameva katākataṃ vīmaṃsanto”tiādīni vattā hoti. Atha itaro “addhā koci mayhaṃ doso bhavissatī”ti kiñci paṭippharituṃ na sakkoti. Taṃ khippaññeva adhimuccitā hotīti taṃ vaṇṇaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ vā sīghameva [M 3.0051] saddahati. Saddahanaṭṭhena hi ādānena esa ādiyanamukhoti vutto. Ādheyyamukhoti pāḷiyā [V 3.0052] pana ṭhapitamukhoti attho. Magge khaṭaāvāṭo viya āgatāgataṃ udakaṃ vaṇṇaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ vā saddahanavasena sampaṭicchituṃ ṭhapitamukhoti vuttaṃ hoti.

141. In the first of the fifth chapter, saṃvāsena means by living together. Ādeyyamukho means one with a receptive countenance; the meaning is one with a countenance for grasping. 'Having given to him, he despises him' means he thinks contemptuously thus, 'This one only knows how to receive what is given.' 'He despises him through association' means that, having become angry over some trivial matter, he is one who says such things as, 'I know the deed done by you! For all this time that I have lived here, what was I doing? Was I not just investigating what you have done repeatedly?' and so on. Then the other, thinking, 'Surely, there must be some fault of mine,' is unable to say anything in response. 'He is quickly convinced of it' means he quickly believes that praise or blame. For by taking with the nature of belief, he is called ādiyanamukho (one with a receptive countenance). As for the Pāḷi term ādheyyamukho, the meaning is ṭhapitamukho (one with a fixed countenance). Just as a pit dug by the road has a 'countenance' set to receive whatever water comes, so too, it is said that he has a countenance set to receive praise or blame through the power of belief.

Ittarasaddhoti parittakasaddho. Kusalākusale dhamme na jānātītiādīsu kusale dhamme “ime kusalā”ti na jānāti, akusale dhamme “ime akusalā”ti na jānāti. Tathā sāvajje sadosadhamme “ime sāvajjā”ti, anavajje ca niddosadhamme “ime anavajjā”ti, hīne hīnāti, paṇīte paṇītāti. Kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgeti “ime kaṇhā sukke paṭibāhetvā ṭhitattā sappaṭibhāgā nāma, ime ca sukkā kaṇhe paṭibāhitvā ṭhitattā sappaṭibhāgā”ti na jānāti.

Ittarasaddho means one of little faith. Regarding 'he does not know skillful and unskillful dhammas,' and so on: he does not know of skillful dhammas, 'These are skillful'; he does not know of unskillful dhammas, 'These are unskillful.' Similarly, of blameworthy dhammas which are with fault, 'These are blameworthy'; and of blameless dhammas which are without fault, 'These are blameless'; of inferior dhammas, 'These are inferior'; of superior dhammas, 'These are superior.' Regarding 'dark and white with their counterparts,' he does not know, 'These dark dhammas, because they stand having obstructed the white, are called counterparts; and these white dhammas, because they stand having obstructed the dark, are called counterparts.'

2. Ārabhatisuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Ārabhati Sutta

142. Dutiye [P 3.0289] ārabhati ca vippaṭisārī ca hotīti āpattivītikkamanavasena ārabhati ceva, tappaccayā ca vippaṭisārī hoti. Cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttinti arahattasamādhiñceva arahattaphalañāṇañca. Nappajānātīti anadhigatattā na jānāti. Ārabhati na vippaṭisārī hotīti āpattiṃ āpajjati, vuṭṭhitattā pana na vippaṭisārī hoti. Nārabhati vippaṭisārī hotīti sakiṃ āpattiṃ āpajjitvā tato vuṭṭhāya pacchā kiñcāpi nāpajjati, vippaṭisāraṃ pana vinodetuṃ na sakkoti. Nārabhati na vippaṭisārī hotīti na ceva āpattiṃ āpajjati, na ca vippaṭisārī hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ…pe… nirujjhantīti arahattaṃ pana appatto hoti. Pañcamanayena khīṇāsavo kathito.

142. In the second sutta, 'he both initiates and is remorseful' means he initiates by way of transgressing an offense, and because of that, he is remorseful. 'Liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom' refers to the concentration of arahantship and the knowledge of the fruit of arahantship. 'He does not know' means he does not know because of not having attained it. 'He initiates but is not remorseful' means he falls into an offense, but because he has emerged from it, he is not remorseful. 'He does not initiate but is remorseful' means that having once fallen into an offense and having emerged from it, although he does not fall into it again later, he is unable to dispel the remorse. 'He neither initiates nor is remorseful' means he neither falls into an offense, nor is he remorseful. 'And that liberation of mind… cease' means he has not attained arahantship. By the fifth method, the one with destroyed taints is spoken of.

Ārambhajāti āpattivītikkamasambhavā. Vippaṭisārajāti vippaṭisārato jātā. Pavaḍḍhantīti punappunaṃ uppajjanena vaḍḍhanti. Ārambhaje āsave pahāyāti vītikkamasambhave āsave āpattidesanāya vā āpattivuṭṭhānena vā pajahitvā. Paṭivinodetvāti suddhante ṭhitabhāvapaccavekkhaṇena nīharitvā. Cittaṃ paññañca bhāvetūti vipassanācittañca taṃsampayuttaṃ paññañca bhāvetu. Sesaṃ iminā upāyeneva veditabbanti.

Ārambhajā (born of initiation) means born from the occurrence of transgression. Vippaṭisārajā (born of remorse) means born from remorse. 'They increase' means they grow through repeated arising. 'Having abandoned the taints born of initiation' means having abandoned the taints born from transgression either by confessing the offense or by emerging from the offense. 'Having dispelled' means having removed them by reflecting on the state of being established in the culmination of purity. 'He should develop mind and wisdom' means he should develop the insight-mind and the wisdom associated with it. The rest should be understood by this same method.

3. Sārandadasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sārandada Sutta

143. Tatiye [V 3.0053][M 3.0052] kāmādhimuttānanti vatthukāmakilesakāmesu adhimuttānaṃ. Dhammānudhammappaṭipannoti navalokuttaradhammatthāya [P 3.0290] sahasīlakaṃ pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno paṭipattipūrako puggalo dullabho lokasmiṃ.

143. In the third, 'intent on sensual pleasures' means those intent on sensual objects and sensual defilements. 'Practicing in accordance with the Dhamma' means a person who has undertaken the preliminary practice by means of concentration and insight for the sake of the nine supramundane Dhammas; such a person who fulfills the practice is rare in the world.

4. Tikaṇḍakīsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Tikaṇḍakī Sutta

144. Catutthe appaṭikūleti appaṭikūlārammaṇe. Paṭikūlasaññīti paṭikūlanti evaṃsaññī. Esa nayo sabbattha. Kathaṃ panāyaṃ evaṃ viharatīti? Iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ pana asubhāya vā pharati, aniccato vā upasaṃharati. Evaṃ tāva appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī viharati. Aniṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ mettāya vā pharati, dhātuto vā upasaṃharati. Evaṃ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī viharati. Ubhayasmiṃ pana purimanayassa ca pacchimanayassa ca vasena tatiyacatutthavārā vuttā, chaḷaṅgupekkhāvasena pañcamo. Chaḷaṅgupekkhā cesā khīṇāsavassa upekkhāsadisā, na pana khīṇāsavupekkhā. Tattha upekkhako vihareyyāti majjhattabhāve ṭhito vihareyya. Kvacanīti kismiñci ārammaṇe. Katthacīti kismiñci padese. Kiñcanati koci appamattakopi. Iti imasmiṃ sutte pañcasu ṭhānesu vipassanāva kathitā. Taṃ āraddhavipassako bhikkhu kātuṃ sakkoti, ñāṇavā paññuttaro bahussutasamaṇopi kātuṃ sakkoti. Sotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmino kātuṃ sakkontiyeva, khīṇāsave vattabbameva natthīti. Pañcamaṃ uttānameva.

144. In the fourth [discourse], 'not repulsive' means a non-repulsive object. 'Perceiving it as repulsive' means one perceives it thus: 'It is repulsive.' This method should be understood in all instances. But how does one dwell in this way? This is the question. Regarding a desirable object, one either pervades it as foul or considers it as impermanent. Thus, one dwells perceiving the non-repulsive as repulsive. Regarding an undesirable object, one either pervades it with loving-kindness or considers it in terms of elements. Thus, one dwells perceiving the repulsive as non-repulsive. In both cases, the third and fourth instances are stated by means of the former and latter methods, and the fifth by means of the six-factored equanimity. This six-factored equanimity is similar to the equanimity of an Arahant, but it is not the equanimity of an Arahant. Therein, 'one should dwell equanimously' means one should dwell established in a state of neutrality. 'Kvacani' means in any object. 'Katthaci' means in any place. 'Kiñcana' means any, even a little. Thus, in this sutta, insight is taught in five instances. A monk who has undertaken insight practice can accomplish this; a wise, supremely intelligent, learned ascetic can also accomplish this. Stream-enterers, once-returners, and non-returners can certainly accomplish this; for an Arahant, there is nothing to be said. The fifth is self-evident.

6. Mittasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Mitta Sutta

146. Chaṭṭhe kammantaṃ kāretīti khettādikammantaṃ kāreti. Adhikaraṇaṃ ādiyatīti cattāri adhikaraṇāni ādiyati. Pāmokkhesu bhikkhūsūti disāpāmokkhesu bhikkhūsu. Paṭiviruddho [P 3.0291] hotīti paccanīkaggāhitāya viruddho hoti. Anavatthacārikanti anavatthānacārikaṃ.

6. In the sixth [discourse], 'he makes someone else do the work' means he has others do work, such as in the fields. 'He takes up disputes' means he takes up the four disputes. 'Among leading monks' means among monks who are leaders in the regions. 'He is opposed' means he is opposed due to adopting an opposing view. 'Wandering without settling' means wandering in a place without a fixed boundary.

7. Asappurisadānasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Discourse on the Gift of an Ignoble Person

147. Sattame [V 3.0054][M 3.0053] asakkaccaṃ detīti na sakkaritvā suciṃ katvā deti. Acittīkatvā detīti acittīkārena agāravavasena deti. Apaviddhaṃ detīti na nirantaraṃ deti, atha vā chaḍḍetukāmo viya deti. Anāgamanadiṭṭhiko detīti katassa nāma phalaṃ āgamissatīti na evaṃ āgamanadiṭṭhiṃ na uppādetvā deti.

146. In the seventh [discourse], 'he gives carelessly' means he gives without honoring, having made it unclean. 'He gives without respect' means he gives in a disrespectful manner, by way of irreverence. 'He gives as if discarding' means he does not give continuously, or alternatively, he gives as if wishing to discard it. 'He gives without belief in future results' means he gives without generating the view that a result of the deed done will come.

Sukkapakkhe cittīkatvā detīti deyyadhamme ca dakkhiṇeyyesu ca cittīkāraṃ upaṭṭhapetvā deti. Tattha deyyadhammaṃ paṇītaṃ ojavantaṃ katvā dento deyyadhamme cittīkāraṃ upaṭṭhapeti nāma. Puggalaṃ vicinitvā dento dakkhiṇeyyesu cittīkāraṃ upaṭṭhapeti nāma. Sahatthā detīti āṇattiyā parahatthena adatvā “anamatagge saṃsāre vicarantena me hatthapādānaṃ aladdhakālassa pamāṇaṃ nāma natthi, vaṭṭamokkhaṃ bhavanissaraṇaṃ karissāmī”ti sahattheneva deti. Āgamanadiṭṭhikoti “anāgatabhavassa paccayo bhavissatī”ti kammañca vipākañca saddahitvā detīti.

7. In the bright section: 'He gives with respect' means he gives after establishing respect for both the gift-object and for the recipients. Herein, one who gives after making the gift-object excellent and nutritious is called one who establishes respect for the gift-object. One who gives after investigating the person is called one who establishes respect for the recipients. 'He gives with his own hand' means, not giving by another's hand through a command, he gives with his own hand, thinking: 'For me, wandering in beginningless saṃsāra, there is no measure of the time I have been without hands and feet; I will bring about release from the round, an escape from existence.' 'With belief in future results' means he gives, having faith in both kamma and its result, thinking: 'This will be a condition for a future existence.'

8. Sappurisadānasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Discourse on the Gift of a Good Person

148. Aṭṭhame saddhāyāti dānañca dānaphalañca saddahitvā. Kālenāti yuttappattakālena. Anaggahitacittoti aggahitacitto muttacāgo hutvā. Anupahaccāti anupaghātetvā guṇe amakkhetvā. Kālāgatā cassa atthā pacurā hontīti atthā āgacchamānā vayovuḍḍhakāle [P 3.0292] anāgantvā yuttappattakāle paṭhamavayasmiṃyeva āgacchanti ceva bahū ca honti.

147. In the eighth [discourse], 'with faith' means having believed in the gift and the fruit of the gift. 'At the right time' means at a suitable, opportune time. 'With an unattached mind' means being one with an unattached mind and open-handed generosity. 'Without harming' means without causing offense, without disparaging the qualities. 'His benefits arrive in time and are abundant' means that benefits, when they come, do not arrive in old age, but arrive at a suitable time, in the first stage of life, and they are abundant.

9. Paṭhamasamayavimuttasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the First Discourse on Timely Liberation

149. Navame samayavimuttassāti appitappitakkhaṇeyeva vikkhambhitehi kilesehi vimuttattā samayavimuttisaṅkhātāya lokiyavimuttiyā vimuttacittassa. Dasamaṃ uttānatthameva.

In the ninth [discourse], 'of one liberated in time' means: of one whose mind is liberated by the mundane liberation designated as 'timely liberation' because of being liberated from defilements that are suppressed at the very moment of application. The tenth has a clear meaning.

Tikaṇḍakīvaggo pañcamo.

8. The Tikaṇḍakī Chapter, the Fifth.

Tatiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

148. The Third Fifty is concluded.

4. Catutthapaṇṇāsakaṃ

4. The Fourth Fifty

(16) 1. Saddhammavaggo

(16) 1. The Chapter on the True Dhamma

1. Paṭhamasammattaniyāmasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Discourse on Right Certainty

151. Catutthassa [V 3.0055][M 3.0054] paṭhame abhabbo niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattanti kusalesu dhammesu sammattabhūtaṃ magganiyāmaṃ okkamituṃ abhabbo abhājanaṃ. Kathaṃ paribhotītiādīsu “kiṃ kathā nāma esā”ti vadanto kathaṃ paribhoti nāma. “Kiṃ nāmesa katheti, kiṃ ayaṃ jānātī”ti vadanto kathikaṃ paribhoti nāma. “Mayaṃ kiṃ jānāma, kuto amhākaṃ etaṃ sotuṃ bala”nti vadanto attānaṃ paribhoti nāma. Vipariyāyena sukkapakkho veditabbo.

9. In the first of the fourth [chapter], 'he is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness in wholesome qualities' means he is incapable and unfit to enter the path, which is the fixed course of rightness in wholesome qualities. In such phrases as 'How does he disparage?', one who says, 'What kind of talk is this?' is said to disparage the talk. One who says, 'What is this person saying? What does he know?' is said to disparage the speaker. One who says, 'What do we know? Where is the benefit for us to hear this?' is said to disparage oneself. The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

2. Dutiyasammattaniyāmasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Second Discourse on Right Certainty

152. Dutiye anaññāte aññātamānīti aviññātasmiṃyeva “viññātamidaṃ mayā”ti evaṃmānī.

149. In the second [discourse], 'believing the unknown to be known' means regarding what is actually unknown, thinking, 'This is known by me.'

3. Tatiyasammattaniyāmasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Third Discourse on Right Certainty

153. Tatiye makkhī dhammaṃ suṇātīti makkhī hutvā guṇamakkhanacittena dhammaṃ suṇāti. Upārambhacittoti niggahāropanacitto. Randhagavesīti guṇarandhaṃ guṇacchiddaṃ gavesanto.

In the third [discourse], 'one who disparages listens to the Dhamma' means: being a disparager, one listens to the Dhamma with a mind that disparages virtues. 'With a fault-finding mind' means with a mind intent on censure. 'Seeking flaws' means seeking a flaw in virtue, a defect in virtue.

4. Paṭhamasaddhammasammosasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the First Discourse on the Disappearance of the True Dhamma

154. Catutthe [P 3.0293] na sakkaccaṃ dhammaṃ suṇantīti ohitasotā sukatakārino hutvā na suṇanti[V 3.0056]. Na pariyāpuṇantīti yathāsutaṃ dhammaṃ vaḷañjantāpi sakkaccaṃ na vaḷañjenti. Pañcamaṃ uttānameva.

In the fourth [discourse], 'they do not listen to the Dhamma respectfully' means they do not listen by becoming attentive-eared and dutiful. 'They do not master it' means that even while making use of the Dhamma as heard, they do not make use of it respectfully. The fifth has a clear meaning.

6. Tatiyasaddhammasammosasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Third Discourse on the Disappearance of the True Dhamma

156. Chaṭṭhe appaṭisaraṇoti appatiṭṭho. Ācariyā hi suttantassa paṭisaraṇaṃ nāma, tesaṃ abhāvā appaṭisaraṇo hoti. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

4. In the sixth [discourse], 'without reliance' means without a standing place. For the teachers who uphold the Pāli are the reliance for the discourses; due to their absence, one is without reliance. The rest here is of the same method as previously stated.

7. Dukkathāsuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Discourse on Unwholesome Talk

157. Sattame [M 3.0055] puggalaṃ upanidhāyāti taṃ taṃ puggalaṃ upanikkhipitvā, sakkhiṃ katvāti attho. Kacchamānāyāti kathiyamānāya. Sesamettha aṭṭhamañca uttānatthamevāti.

157. In the seventh, puggalaṃ upanidhāya means having established that very person as a witness. Kacchamānāya means 'while being discussed'. The rest here, and in the eighth, is clear in meaning.

9. Udāyīsuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Udāyī Sutta

159. Navame anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathessāmīti dānānantaraṃ sīlaṃ, sīlānantaraṃ sagganti evaṃ desanānupubbiṃ kathaṃ vā, yaṃ yaṃ suttapadaṃ vā gāthāpadaṃ vā nikkhittaṃ hoti, tassa tassa anurūpakathaṃ kathessāmīti cittaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā paresaṃ dhammo desetabbo. Pariyāyadassāvīti tassa tassa atthassa taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ dassento. Kāraṇañhi idha pariyāyoti vuttaṃ. Anuddayataṃ paṭiccāti “mahāsambādhappatte satte sambādhato mocessāmī”ti anukampaṃ āgamma. Na āmisantaroti na āmisahetuko, attano catupaccayalābhaṃ anāsīsantoti attho. Attānañca parañca anupahaccāti attukkaṃsanaparavambhanādivasena attānañca parañca guṇupaghātena anupahantvā.

159. In the ninth, 'I shall speak a gradual discourse' means that one should teach the Dhamma to others, having established in mind, 'After generosity comes virtue, after virtue comes heaven'—thus a gradual discourse of teaching; or, 'I shall speak a discourse suitable to each sutta passage or verse passage that has been laid down.' 'Showing the method' means showing the respective reason for each point, for here 'method' is said to refer to the reason. 'Based on compassion' means having come to compassion, thinking, 'I will free beings who have fallen into great constriction from that constriction.' 'Not for the sake of material reward' means not motivated by material gain, meaning not hoping for one's own acquisition of the four requisites. 'Without harming oneself or others' means without harming oneself and others by destroying their virtues through self-exaltation, disparagement of others, and so forth.

10. Duppaṭivinodayasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Discourse on What is Difficult to Dispel

160. Dasame duppaṭivinodayāti yāni hassādīni kiccāni nipphādetuṃ [P 3.0294] ṭhānāni uppannāni honti, tesu matthakaṃ asampattesu antarāyeva dunnīhārā duvikkhambhayā honti. Paṭibhānanti [V 3.0057] kathetukāmatā vuccati. Imāni pañca duppaṭivinodayāni, na suppaṭivinodayāni. Upāyena pana kāraṇena anurūpāhi paccavekkhaṇaanusāsanādīhi sakkā paṭivinodetunti.

160. In the tenth discourse, ‘difficult to dispel’ means that when occasions for laughter and so forth arise to accomplish their purpose, before they reach their culmination, they are difficult to remove and hard to suppress midway. ‘Readiness to speak’ is said to be the wish to speak. These five are difficult to dispel, not easy to dispel. However, by means of skillful methods, reasoning, and appropriate reflection, instruction, and so forth, it is possible to dispel them.

Saddhammavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on the True Dhamma, the First.

(17) 2. Āghātavaggo

(17) 2. The Chapter on Resentment

1. Paṭhamaāghātapaṭivinayasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Discourse on Removing Resentment

161. Dutiyassa [M 3.0056] paṭhame āghātaṃ paṭivinenti vūpasamentīti āghātapaṭivinayā. Yattha bhikkhuno uppanno āghāto sabbaso paṭivinetabboti yattha ārammaṇe bhikkhuno āghāto uppanno hoti, tattha so sabbo imehi pañcahi paṭivinodetabboti attho. Mettā tasmiṃ puggale bhāvetabbāti tikacatukkajjhānavasena mettā bhāvetabbā. Karuṇāyapi eseva nayo. Upekkhā pana catukkapañcakajjhānavasena bhāvetabbā. Yasmā pana yaṃ puggalaṃ passato cittaṃ na nibbāti, tasmiṃ muditā na saṇṭhahati, tasmā sā na vuttā. Asatiamanasikāroti yathā so puggalo na upaṭṭhāti, kuṭṭādīhi antarito viya hoti, evaṃ tasmiṃ asatiamanasikāro āpajjitabbo. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā uttānameva.

161. In the first discourse of the second chapter, they are called āghātapaṭivinayā because they dispel and appease resentment. ‘Wherever resentment arises in a bhikkhu, it should be entirely dispelled’ means that in whatever object resentment arises for a bhikkhu, all of it should be dispelled by these five methods. ‘Loving-kindness should be developed toward that person’ means loving-kindness should be developed by way of the jhānas of the triad and tetrad. The same method applies to compassion. Equanimity, however, should be developed by way of the jhānas of the tetrad and pentad. But since the mind is not appeased when seeing a certain person, sympathetic joy is not established in regard to them; therefore, it is not mentioned. ‘Non-recollection and non-attention’ means that one should apply non-recollection and non-attention to that person so that they do not come to mind, as if hidden by a wall and so forth. The rest is clear, as it is of the method stated previously.

2. Dutiyaāghātapaṭivinayasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Discourse on Removing Resentment

162. Dutiye āghāto etesu paṭivinetabboti āghātapaṭivinayā[P 3.0295]. Āghāto etehi paṭivinetabbotipi āghātapaṭivinayā. Paṭivinayoti hi paṭivinayavatthūnampi paṭivinayakāraṇānampi etaṃ adhivacanaṃ, tadubhayampi idha vaṭṭati. Pañca hi puggalā paṭivinayavatthū honti pañcahi upamāhi pañca paṭipattiyo paṭivinayakāraṇāni. Labhati ca kālena kālaṃ cetaso [V 3.0058] vivaraṃ cetaso pasādanti kāle kāle samathavipassanācittassa uppannokāsasaṅkhātaṃ vivarañceva saddhāsampannabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ pasādañca labhati.

162. In the second discourse, because resentment should be dispelled in regard to these persons, they are called āghātapaṭivinayā. Because resentment should be dispelled by these practices, they are also called āghātapaṭivinayā. For 'removal' is a designation for both the objects of removal and the causes of removal; and both are applicable here. For five persons are objects of removal, and five practices with five similes are causes of removal. ‘And from time to time one obtains an opening of mind and confidence of mind’ means that from time to time one obtains both an opening, reckoned as the opportunity that has arisen for the mind of serenity and insight, and confidence, reckoned as a state of being endowed with faith.

Rathiyāyāti antaravīthiyaṃ. Nantakanti pilotikakhaṇḍaṃ. Niggahetvāti akkamitvā. Yo tattha sāroti yaṃ tattha thiraṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ paripātetvāti taṃ luñcitvā. Evameva khoti ettha paṃsukūliko viya mettāvihārī daṭṭhabbo, rathiyāya nantakaṃ viya veripuggalo, dubbalaṭṭhānaṃ viya aparisuddhakāyasamācāratā, thiraṭṭhānaṃ viya parisuddhavacīsamācāratā, dubbalaṭṭhānaṃ chaḍḍetvā thiraṭṭhānaṃ ādāya gantvā sibbitvā rajitvā pārupitvā [M 3.0057] vicaraṇakālo viya aparisuddhakāyasamācārataṃ amanasikatvā parisuddhavacīsamācārataṃ manasikatvā verimhi cittuppādaṃ nibbāpetvā phāsuvihārakālo daṭṭhabbo.

‘On the road’ means on the main street. ‘A rag’ means a piece of worn-out cloth. ‘Having held it down’ means having stepped on it. ‘Whatever is the essence there’ means whatever firm part is there. ‘Having torn that off’ means having plucked that out. Just so, here, one who dwells in loving-kindness should be seen as like a rag-robe wearer; the hostile person as like the rag on the road; impure bodily conduct as like the weak spot; pure verbal conduct as like the firm spot. Just as is the time of discarding the weak spot, taking the firm spot, going, sewing it, dyeing it, wearing it, and wandering about, so too should the time of dwelling at ease be seen: by not attending to the impure bodily conduct, but attending to the pure verbal conduct, and extinguishing the arising of a mind of hate towards the hostile person.

Sevālapaṇakapariyonaddhāti sevālena ca udakapappaṭakena ca paṭicchannā. Ghammaparetoti ghammena anugato. Kilantoti [P 3.0296] maggakilanto. Tasitoti taṇhābhibhūto. Pipāsitoti pānīyaṃ pātukāmo. Apaviyūhitvāti apanetvā. Pivitvāti pasannaudakaṃ pivitvā. Evameva khoti ettha ghammābhitatto puriso viya mettāvihārī daṭṭhabbo, sevālapaṇakaṃ viya aparisuddhavacīsamācāratā, pasannaudakaṃ viya parisuddhakāyasamācāratā, sevālapaṇakaṃ apabyūhitvā pasannodakaṃ pivitvā gamanaṃ viya aparisuddhavacīsamācārataṃ amanasikatvā parisuddhakāyasamācārataṃ manasikatvā verimhi cittuppādaṃ nibbāpetvā phāsuvihārakālo daṭṭhabbo.

‘Covered with moss and water-plants’ means covered by both moss and water-scum. ‘Overcome by heat’ means followed along by heat. ‘Weary’ means weary from the road. ‘Thirsty’ means overcome by craving. ‘Parched’ means desiring to drink water. ‘Having parted it’ means having removed it. ‘Having drunk’ means having drunk the clear water. Just so, here, one who dwells in loving-kindness should be seen as like the man oppressed by heat; impure verbal conduct as like the moss and water-plants; pure bodily conduct as like the clear water. Just as is the act of parting the moss and water-plants, drinking the clear water, and going on one's way, so too should the time of dwelling at ease be seen: by not attending to the impure verbal conduct, but attending to the pure bodily conduct, and extinguishing the arising of a mind of hate towards the hostile person.

Khobhessāmīti cālessāmi. Loḷessāmīti ākulaṃ karissāmi. Apeyyampi taṃ karissāmīti pivituṃ asakkuṇeyyaṃ karissāmi. Catukkuṇḍikoti jāṇūhi ca hatthehi ca bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhānena catukkuṇḍiko hutvā. Gopītakaṃ pivitvāti gāviyo viya mukhena ākaḍḍhento pivitvā. Evameva khoti ettha ghammābhitatto puriso viya mettāvihārī daṭṭhabbo, gopadaṃ viya veripuggalo, gopade parittaudakaṃ viya tassabbhantare parittaguṇo, catukkuṇḍikassa gopītakaṃ pivitvā pakkamanaṃ viya tassa aparisuddhakāyavacīsamācārataṃ amanasikatvā yaṃ so kālena kālaṃ [P 3.0297] dhammassavanaṃ nissāya cetaso vivarappasādasaṅkhātaṃ pītipāmojjaṃ labhati, taṃ manasikatvā cittuppādanibbāpanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

‘I will stir it’ means I will shake it. ‘I will roil it’ means I will make it turbid. ‘I will make it undrinkable’ means I will make it unable to be drunk. ‘On all fours’ means having gone down on all fours by establishing oneself on the ground with knees and hands. ‘Having drunk in the manner of a cow’ means having drunk by drawing it in with the mouth like cows do. Just so, here, one who dwells in loving-kindness should be seen as like the man oppressed by heat; the hostile person as like a cow’s hoofprint; the little water in the hoofprint as like the few good qualities within him. Just as is the act of one on all fours drinking in the manner of a cow and then departing, so too the extinguishing of the arising of a mind of hate should be understood: by not attending to his impure bodily and verbal conduct, but by attending to whatever delight and joy—reckoned as an opening and confidence of mind—he obtains from time to time by relying on hearing the Dhamma.

Ābādhikoti [V 3.0059] iriyāpathabhañjanakena visabhāgābādhena ābādhiko. Puratopissāti puratopi bhaveyya. Anayabyasananti avaḍḍhivināsaṃ. Evameva khoti ettha so anāthagilāno viya sabbakaṇhadhammasamannāgato puggalo, addhānamaggo viya anamataggasaṃsāro, purato ca pacchato ca gāmānaṃ dūrabhāvo viya nibbānassa dūrabhāvo, sappāyabhojanānaṃ alābho viya sāmaññaphalabhojanānaṃ alābho, sappāyabhesajjānaṃ alābho [M 3.0058] viya samathavipassanānaṃ abhāvo, patirūpaupaṭṭhākānaṃ alābho viya ovādānusāsanīhi kilesatikicchakānaṃ abhāvo, gāmantanāyakassa alābho viya nibbānasampāpakassa tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā aladdhabhāvo, aññatarassa purisassa disvā kāruññupaṭṭhānaṃ viya tasmiṃ puggale mettāvihārikassa kāruññaṃ uppādetvā cittanibbāpanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

‘Sick’ means being afflicted with a discordant illness that destroys the bodily postures. ‘Ahead of him’ means it could also be in front. ‘Misfortune and ruin’ means decline and destruction. Just so, here, that person endowed with all dark qualities should be seen as like the sick person without a protector; the long-distance road as like beginningless saṃsāra; the farness of villages both ahead and behind as like the farness of Nibbāna; the lack of suitable food as like the non-obtaining of the food that is the fruits of the holy life; the lack of suitable medicine as like the absence of serenity and insight; the lack of suitable attendants as like the absence of teachers who cure the disease of the defilements with admonition and instruction; the lack of a guide to the next village as like the state of not having found the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata who can lead one to Nibbāna. Just as compassion arises upon seeing a certain man, so too the extinguishing of the mind of hate should be understood by arousing compassion for that person on the part of one who dwells in loving-kindness.

Acchodakāti pasannodakā. Sātodakāti madhurodakā. Sītodakāti tanusītasalilā. Setakāti ūmibhijjanaṭṭhānesu setavaṇṇā. Supatitthāti samatitthā. Evameva khoti ettha ghammābhitatto puriso viya mettāvihārī daṭṭhabbo, sā pokkharaṇī viya parisuddhasabbadvāro puriso, nhatvā pivitvā paccuttaritvā rukkhacchāyāya nipajjitvā yathākāmaṃ gamanaṃ viya tesu dvāresu [P 3.0298] yaṃ icchati, taṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cittanibbāpanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tatiyacatutthāni heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva.

‘Of clear water’ means having transparent water. ‘Of pleasant water’ means having sweet water. ‘Of cool water’ means having cool, refreshing water. ‘White’ means having a white color in the places where the waves break. ‘With good bathing places’ means having even fords. Just so, here, one who dwells in loving-kindness should be seen as like the man oppressed by heat; a person whose every door is pure as like that pond. Just as is the act of bathing, drinking, getting out, lying down in the shade of a tree, and going as one pleases, so too the extinguishing of the mind of hate should be understood by making whatever one wishes among that person's doors of conduct one's object of attention. The third and fourth are by the same method as explained previously.

5. Pañhapucchāsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Sutta on Asking Questions

165. Pañcame paribhavanti paribhavanto, evaṃ paribhavissāmīti paribhavanatthāya pucchatīti attho. Aññātukāmoti jānitukāmo hutvā.

165. In the fifth, `paribhavanti` means: desiring to despise, he asks for the purpose of despising, thinking, 'Thus I will despise.' This is the meaning. `Aññātukāmo` means being one who desires to know.

6. Nirodhasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Sutta on Cessation

166. Chaṭṭhe atthetaṃ ṭhānanti atthi etaṃ kāraṇaṃ. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṃ ārādheyyāti no ce imasmiṃyeva attabhāve arahattaṃ pāpuṇeyya. Kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṃ devānanti kāmāvacaradevānaṃ. Aññataraṃ manomayaṃ kāyanti jhānamanena nibbattaṃ aññataraṃ suddhāvāsabrahmakāyaṃ. Udāyīti lāḷudāyī. So hi “manomaya”nti sutvā “āruppe na bhavitabba”nti [V 3.0060] paṭibāhi. Thero “sāriputto kiṃ jānāti, yassa sammukhā evaṃ bhikkhū vacanaṃ paṭikkosantī”ti evaṃ bālānaṃ laddhiuppattipaṭibāhanatthaṃ taṃ vacanaṃ anadhivāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.

166. In the sixth, `atthe taṃ ṭhānaṃ` means this reason exists. `No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṃ ārādheyya` means if one were not to attain arahantship in this very existence. `Kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṃ devānaṃ` means of the devas of the sensual sphere. `Aññataraṃ manomayaṃ kāyaṃ` means a certain body of the Pure Abode Brahmās produced by the jhāna-mind. `Udāyī` is Lāḷudāyī. Indeed, having heard 'mind-made,' he rejected it, thinking, 'It must be in the formless realm.' The Elder, in order to prevent the arising of a wrong view among foolish people, did not endure that statement and approached the Blessed One.

Atthi nāmāti amarisanatthe nipāto. Teneva cettha “ajjhupekkhissathā”ti anāgatavacanaṃ kataṃ. Ayañhetthattho – ānanda, tumhe theraṃ [M 3.0059] bhikkhuṃ viheṭhiyamānaṃ ajjhupekkhatha, na vo etaṃ marisayāmi na sahāmi nādhivāsemīti. Kasmā pana bhagavā ānandatheraṃyeva evamāhāti? Dhammabhaṇḍāgārikattā. Dhammabhaṇḍāgārikassa hi evaṃ vadanto paṭibāhituṃ bhāro. Apicesa sāriputtattherassa piyasahāyo, tenāpissa esa bhāro. Tattha kiñcāpi bhagavā [P 3.0299] ānandattheraṃ garahanto evamāha, na panesā tasseva garahā, sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃyeva garahāti veditabbā. Vihāranti gandhakuṭiṃ.

`Atthi nāma` is a particle that occurs in the sense of impatience. For that very reason, the future tense word `ajjhupekkhissatha` is used here. Herein, this is the meaning: 'Ānanda, can it be that you are indifferent to a monk harassing the Elder? I cannot bear this from you, I cannot tolerate it, I cannot endure it.' Why, then, did the Blessed One speak thus only to the Elder Ānanda? Because of his being the custodian of the Dhamma. Indeed, it is the responsibility of the custodian of the Dhamma to restrain those who speak thus. Moreover, he was a dear companion of the Elder Sāriputta; for that reason also, this was his responsibility. Therein, although the Blessed One spoke thus as if rebuking the Elder Ānanda, this was not a rebuke of him alone; it should be known as a rebuke of all who were present. `Vihāraṃ` means to the perfumed chamber.

Anacchariyanti na acchariyaṃ. Yathāti kāraṇavacanaṃ. Āyasmantaṃyevettha upavānaṃ paṭibhāseyyāti ettha bhagavatā ca evaṃ etadeva kāraṇaṃ ārabbha udāhaṭe āyasmatoyeva upavānassa paṭivacanaṃ paṭibhātu upaṭṭhātūti dīpeti. Sārajjaṃ okkantanti domanassaṃ anupaviṭṭhaṃ. Sīlavātiādīhi khīṇāsavasīlādīniyeva kathitāni. Khaṇḍiccenātiādīni sakkārādīnaṃ kāraṇapucchāvasena vuttāni. Kiṃ khaṇḍiccādīhi kāraṇehi taṃ taṃ sabrahmacāriṃ sakkareyyunti ayañhettha adhippāyo.

`Anacchariyaṃ` means it is not surprising. The word `yathā` is a word that expresses reason. In the passage `āyasmantaṃyevettha upavānaṃ paṭibhāseyya`, it shows this meaning: when this very reason was brought up by the Blessed One, 'Let a reply occur only to the Venerable Upavāṇa; let it be present to him.' `Sārajjaṃ okkantaṃ` means dejection has entered. By `sīlavā` and so on, the virtue and other qualities of one whose cankers are destroyed are spoken of. `Khaṇḍiccena` and so on are spoken by way of asking the reason for respect and so on. Herein, this is the intended meaning: 'For what reasons, such as being broken-toothed, would his fellow practitioners respect him?'

7. Codanāsuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Codanā Sutta

167. Sattame codakenāti vatthusandassanā āpattisandassanā saṃvāsappaṭikkhepo sāmīcippaṭikkhepoti catūhi codanāvatthūhi codayamānena. Kālena vakkhāmi no akālenāti ettha cuditakassa kālo kathito, na codakassa. Paraṃ codentena hi parisamajjhe vā uposathapavāraṇagge vā āsanasālābhojanasālādīsu vā na codetabbo, divāṭṭhāne nisinnakāle “karotāyasmā okāsaṃ, ahaṃ āyasmantaṃ vattukāmo”ti evaṃ okāsaṃ kāretvā codetabbo. Puggalaṃ pana upaparikkhitvā yo lolapuggalo abhūtaṃ vatvā bhikkhūnaṃ ayasaṃ āropeti, so okāsakammaṃ vināpi codetabbo. Bhūtenāti [P 3.0300] tacchena sabhāvena. Saṇhenāti maṭṭhena mudukena. Atthasaṃhitenāti [V 3.0061] atthakāmatāya hitakāmatāya upetena. Avippaṭisāro upadahātabboti amaṅkubhāvo upanetabbo. Alaṃ [M 3.0060] te avippaṭisārāyāti yuttaṃ te amaṅkubhāvāya. Sesamettha uttānamevāti. Aṭṭhamaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayattā pākaṭameva.

167. In the seventh sutta, `codakena` (by a reprover) means by one who reproaches with the four grounds for reproof: pointing out the matter, pointing out the offense, rejecting association, and rejecting proper conduct. In the passage, 'I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time,' the time for the one being reproved is stated, not for the reprover. For when reproaching another, one should not reproach in the midst of an assembly, in the Uposatha or Pavāraṇā hall, or in places like the sitting hall or the dining hall. Instead, when seated in a daytime resting place, one should request permission, saying, ‘Venerable, may you grant me leave? I wish to speak to you,’ and then reproach. However, having investigated the individual, if he is a fickle individual who, by speaking untruths, brings the monks into disrepute, such a person should be reproached even without seeking permission. ‘Truthfully’ (bhūtena) means with truth, in accordance with the actual nature. ‘Gently’ (saṇhena) means smoothly and mildly. ‘With beneficial intent’ (atthasaṃhitena) means endowed with a desire for their welfare and benefit. ‘Freedom from remorse should be established’ (avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo) means a state of not being downcast should be brought about. ‘It is enough for you to be free from remorse’ (alaṃ te avippaṭisārāya) means it is suitable for you to not be downcast. The rest here is indeed straightforward. The eighth sutta is evident, as its method has been previously explained.

9. Khippanisantisuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Khippanisanti Sutta

169. Navame khippaṃ nisāmayati upadhāretīti khippanisanti. Suggahitaṃ katvā gaṇhātīti suggahitaggāhī. Atthakusaloti aṭṭhakathāya cheko. Dhammakusaloti pāḷiyaṃ cheko. Niruttikusaloti niruttivacanesu cheko. Byañjanakusaloti akkharappabhede cheko. Pubbāparakusaloti atthapubbāparaṃ, dhammapubbāparaṃ, akkharapubbāparaṃ, byañjanapubbāparaṃ, anusandhipubbāparanti imasmiṃ pañcavidhe pubbāpare cheko. Tattha atthapubbāparakusaloti heṭṭhā atthena upari atthaṃ jānāti, upari atthena heṭṭhā atthaṃ jānāti. Kathaṃ? So hi heṭṭhā atthaṃ ṭhapetvā upari atthe vutte “heṭṭhā attho atthī”ti jānāti. Upari atthaṃ ṭhapetvā heṭṭhā atthe vuttepi “upari attho atthī”ti jānāti. Ubhato ṭhapetvā majjhe atthe vutte “ubhato attho atthī”ti jānāti. Majjhe atthaṃ ṭhapetvā ubhatobhāgesu atthe vutte “majjhe attho atthī”ti jānāti. Dhammapubbāparādīsupi eseva nayo. Anusandhipubbāpare pana sīlaṃ ādiṃ katvā āraddhe suttante matthake chasu abhiññāsu [P 3.0301] āgatāsu “yathānusandhiṃ yathānuparicchedaṃ suttanto gato”ti jānāti. Diṭṭhivasena āraddhe upari saccesu āgatesupi “yathānusandhinā gato”ti jānāti. Kalahabhaṇḍanavasena āraddhe upari sāraṇīyadhammesu āgatesupi, dvattiṃsatiracchānakathāvasena āraddhe upari dasakathāvatthūsu (a. ni. 10.69; udā.31) āgatesupi “yathānusandhinā gato”ti jānātīti.

169. In the ninth sutta, `khippanisanti` is so called because one quickly treasures in the heart and remembers. `Suggahitaggāhī` is so called because one grasps what has been well-grasped. `Atthakusalo` (skilled in meaning) means one is skilled in the commentary. `Dhammakusalo` (skilled in the Dhamma) means one is skilled in the Pāḷi. `Niruttikusalo` (skilled in language) means one is skilled in expressions of language. `Byañjanakusalo` (skilled in letters) means one is skilled in the distinctions of letters. `Pubbāparakusalo` (skilled in sequence) means one is skilled in this fivefold sequence: the sequence of meaning, the sequence of the Pāḷi, the sequence of letters, the sequence of words, and the sequence of connection. Therein, `atthapubbāparakusalo` (skilled in the sequence of meaning) means that by means of the meaning stated below, one knows the meaning stated above, and by means of the meaning stated above, one knows the meaning stated below. How? When a meaning above is stated, having set aside the meaning below, one knows, 'There is a meaning below.' When a meaning below is stated, having set aside the meaning above, one knows, 'There is a meaning above.' When a meaning in the middle is stated, having set aside both ends, one knows, 'There is a meaning on both ends.'
