'Having illuminated Pokkharaṇiyā' (pokkharaṇiyaṃ obhāsetvā) means having pervaded the great monastery named Pokkharaṇiyā with one's own radiance. 'Samanuñño' means having a like-minded, well-pleased mind. 'Dovacassatā' means the state of being difficult to speak to. 'Pāpamittatā' means the state of having base friends. In this sutta, only the dhammas that are causes for decline are taught. In the second, the dhammas that are not causes for decline, mixed with the supramundane, are taught.

3. Bhayasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Bhaya Sutta

23. Tatiye kāmarāgarattāyanti kāmarāgaratto ayaṃ. Chandarāgavinibaddhoti chandarāgena vinibaddho. Bhayāti cittutrāsabhayā. Paṅkāti kilesapaṅkato. Saṅgo paṅko ca ubhayanti saṅgo ca paṅko ca idampi ubhayaṃ. Ete kāmā pavuccanti, yattha satto puthujjanoti yasmiṃ saṅge ca paṅke ca puthujjano satto laggo laggito palibuddho. Upādāneti catubbidhe upādāne. Jātimaraṇasambhaveti jātiyā ca maraṇassa ca sambhave paccayabhūte. Anupādā [P 3.0354] vimuccantīti anupādiyitvā vimuccanti. Jātimaraṇasaṅkhayeti jātimaraṇānaṃ saṅkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne, nibbānārammaṇāya vimuttiyā vimuccantīti attho. Imasmiṃ ṭhāne vivaṭṭetvā arahattameva patto esa bhikkhu. Idāni taṃ khīṇāsavaṃ thomento te khemappattātiādimāha. Tattha khemappattāti khemabhāvaṃ pattā. Sukhinoti lokuttarasukhena sukhitā. Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutāti abbhantare kilesābhāvena diṭṭhadhammeyeva abhinibbutā. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭameva kathetvā gāthāsu vaṭṭavivaṭaṃ kathitaṃ.

23. In the third, 'kāmarāgarattāyaṃ' means this being is attached through sensual lust. 'Chandarāgavinibaddho' means bound by passionate desire. 'Bhayā' means from fear, that is, the terror of the mind. 'Saṅgā' means from attachment, that is, from the attachment of defilements. 'Saṅgo ca paṅko ca ubhayaṃ' means both attachment and mire; this pair is also meant. 'Ete kāmā pavuccanti, yattha satto puthujjanoti' means: in which attachment and mire the ordinary person is attached, stuck, ensnared, and entangled. 'Upādāne' means in the fourfold clinging. 'Jātimaraṇasambhave' means in what has become the cause for the arising of birth and death. 'Anupādā vimuccanti' means not clinging, they are liberated. 'Jātimaraṇasaṅkhaye' means in the destruction of birth and death, that is, in Nibbāna, which is called the complete destruction of birth and death; the meaning is that they are liberated by the liberation that has Nibbāna as its object. In this context, this monk, having turned away from the round of existence, has attained only Arahantship. Now, praising that one whose cankers are destroyed, he spoke the words beginning with 'te khemappattā'. Therein, 'khemappattā' means having reached the state of security. 'Sukhino' means being happy with supramundane happiness. 'Diṭṭhadhammābhinibbutā' means being extinguished in this very life due to the absence of defilements within. In this sutta, having spoken only of the round of existence, in the verses, both the round and the unbinding from the round are taught.

4. Himavantasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Himavanta Sutta

24. Catutthe [V 3.0103] padāleyyāti bhindeyya. Chavāyāti lāmikāya. Samādhissa samāpattikusalo hotīti āhārasappāyautusappāyāni pariggahetvā samādhiṃ samāpajjituṃ kusalo hoti cheko samattho paṭibalo. Samādhissa ṭhitikusaloti samādhissa ṭhitiyaṃ kusalo, samādhiṃ ṭhapetuṃ sakkotīti attho. Samādhissa vuṭṭhānakusaloti samādhissa vuṭṭhāne kusalo, yathāparicchedena vuṭṭhātuṃ sakkotīti attho. Samādhissa kallitakusaloti samādhissa kallatāya kusalo, samādhicittaṃ hāsetuṃ kallaṃ kātuṃ sakkotīti attho. Samādhissa gocarakusaloti samādhissa asappāye anupakārake dhamme vajjetvā sappāye upakārake sevantopi, “ayaṃ samādhinimittārammaṇo [M 3.0101] ayaṃ lakkhaṇārammaṇo”ti jānantopi samādhissa gocarakusalo nāma hoti. Samādhissa abhinīhārakusaloti upariuparisamāpattisamāpajjanatthāya [P 3.0355] paṭhamajjhānādisamādhiṃ abhinīharituṃ sakkonto samādhissa abhinīhārakusalo nāma hoti. So paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhāya dutiyaṃ samāpajjati, dutiyajjhānā…pe… tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhāya catutthaṃ samāpajjatīti.

24. In the fourth, 'padāleyyāti' means 'one should split'. 'Chavāyāti' means 'base'. 'Skilled in attaining concentration' means: having taken suitable food and suitable seasons, one is skilled, clever, capable, and able to attain concentration. 'Skilled in the stability of concentration' means: one is skilled in the stability of concentration; the meaning is that one is able to establish concentration. 'Skilled in emerging from concentration' means: one is skilled in emerging from concentration; the meaning is that one is able to emerge according to the determination. 'Skilled in the readiness of concentration' means: one is skilled in the readiness of concentration; the meaning is that one is able to make the concentrated mind joyful and ready. 'Skilled in the range of concentration' means: one who avoids states that are unsuitable and unhelpful for concentration and resorts to those that are suitable and helpful, and one who knows, "This concentration has a sign as its object; this one has a characteristic as its object," is called skilled in the range of concentration. 'Skilled in directing concentration' means: one who is able to direct the concentration of the first jhāna and so on for the purpose of attaining higher and higher attainments is called skilled in directing concentration. That person, emerging from the first jhāna, attains the second. Emerging from the second jhāna... and so on... emerging from the third jhāna, one attains the fourth.

5. Anussatiṭṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Anussatiṭṭhāna Sutta

25. Pañcame anussatiṭṭhānānīti anussatikāraṇāni. Itipi so bhagavātiādīni visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.123 ādayo) vitthāritāneva. Idampi kho, bhikkhave, ārammaṇaṃ karitvāti idaṃ buddhānussatikammaṭṭhānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ karitvā. Visujjhantīti paramavisuddhiṃ nibbānaṃ pāpuṇanti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthameva. Imasmiṃ pana sutte cha anussatiṭṭhānāni missakāni kathitānīti veditabbāni.

25. In the fifth, 'anussatiṭṭhānāni' means the causes for recollection. Those beginning with 'Itipi so bhagavā' have been explained in detail in the Visuddhimagga. 'Having made this the object, O bhikkhus' means: having made this meditation subject, the recollection of the Buddha, the object. 'They are purified' means: they attain Nibbāna, the supreme purity. The rest has an obvious meaning everywhere. In this sutta, however, it should be known that six bases of recollection are taught as mixed.

6. Mahākaccānasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Mahākaccāna Sutta

26. Chaṭṭhe sambādheti pañcakāmaguṇasambādhe. Okāsādhigamoti ettha okāsā vuccanti cha anussatiṭṭhānāni, tesaṃ adhigamo. Visuddhiyāti visujjhanatthāya. Sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāyāti sokānañca paridevānañca samatikkamatthāya. Atthaṅgamāyāti atthaṃ gamanatthāya[V 3.0104]. Ñāyassa adhigamāyāti sahavipassanakassa maggassa adhigamanatthāya. Nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyāti apaccayaparinibbānassa paccakkhakiriyatthāya.

26. In the sixth, 'in confinement' means in the confinement of the five strands of sensual pleasure. Regarding 'attainment of an opportunity', here, the six bases of recollection are called 'opportunities'; their attainment is meant. 'For purity' means for the purpose of purification. 'For the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation' means for the purpose of overcoming sorrow and lamentation. 'For cessation' means for the purpose of going to cessation. 'For the attainment of the true way' means for the purpose of attaining the path together with insight. 'For the realization of Nibbāna' means for the purpose of directly experiencing unconditioned Parinibbāna.

Sabbasoti sabbākārena. Ākāsasamenāti alagganaṭṭhena ceva apalibuddhaṭṭhena ca ākāsasadisena. Vipulenāti na parittakena. Mahaggatenāti mahantabhāvaṃ gatena, mahantehi vā ariyasāvakehi gatena, paṭipannenāti attho. Appamāṇenāti [P 3.0356] pharaṇaappamāṇatāya appamāṇena. Averenāti akusalaverapuggalaverarahitena. Abyāpajjhenāti kodhadukkhavajjitena. Sabbametaṃ buddhānussaticittameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paratopi eseva nayo. Visuddhidhammāti visujjhanasabhāvā. Imasmimpi sutte cha anussatiṭṭhānāni missakāneva kathitānīti.

'In every way' means in all aspects. 'Like space' means like space because of being unattached and unobstructed. 'Vast' means not limited. 'Gone to greatness' means having reached a great state, or reached and practiced by great noble disciples; this is the meaning. 'Immeasurable' means immeasurable due to the immeasurability of its pervasion. 'Without enmity' means free from the enmity of the unwholesome and the enmity of persons. 'Without affliction' means devoid of the suffering of anger. All this is said with reference to the mind associated with the recollection of the Buddha. This same method applies to what follows. 'States of purity' means having the nature of purification. In this sutta too, the six bases of recollection are taught as mixed.

7. Paṭhamasamayasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the First Occasion Sutta

27. Sattame [M 3.0102] manobhāvanīyassāti ettha manaṃ bhāveti vaḍḍhetīti manobhāvanīyo. Dassanāyāti dassanatthaṃ. Nissaraṇanti niggamanaṃ vūpasamanaṃ. Dhammaṃ desetīti kāmarāgappajahanatthāya asubhakammaṭṭhānaṃ katheti. Dutiyavārādīsu byāpādappahānāya mettākammaṭṭhānaṃ, thinamiddhappahānāya thinamiddhavinodanakammaṭṭhānaṃ, ālokasaññaṃ vā vīriyārambhavatthuādīnaṃ vā aññataraṃ, uddhaccakukkuccappahānāya samathakammaṭṭhānaṃ, vicikicchāpahānāya tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ guṇakathaṃ kathento dhammaṃ desetīti veditabbo. Āgammāti ārabbha. Manasikarototi ārammaṇavasena citte karontassa. Anantarā āsavānaṃ khayo hotīti anantarāyena āsavānaṃ khayo hoti.

27. In the seventh, regarding 'manobhāvanīyassa': because one develops (bhāveti)—that is, increases (vaḍḍheti)—the mind, one is called 'manobhāvanīyo', one who develops the mind. 'Dassanāya' means for the purpose of seeing. 'Nissaraṇa' means escape, appeasement. 'He teaches the Dhamma' means he speaks on the meditation subject of unattractiveness for the purpose of abandoning sensual lust. In the second and subsequent instances, it should be understood that 'he teaches the Dhamma' by speaking on the meditation subject of loving-kindness for abandoning ill will; for abandoning sloth and torpor, he speaks on the perception of light or one of the bases for arousing energy; for abandoning restlessness and remorse, he speaks on the meditation subject of tranquility; and for abandoning doubt, he teaches the Dhamma by speaking on the virtues of the Three Jewels. 'Āgammā' means with reference to. 'Manasikaroto' means for one who makes it present in the mind by way of an object. 'Anantarā āsavānaṃ khayo hoti' means the destruction of the taints occurs without obstacle.

8. Dutiyasamayasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Second Occasion Sutta

28. Aṭṭhame maṇḍalamāḷeti bhojanasālāya. Cārittakilamathoti piṇḍapātacariyāya uppannakilamatho. Bhattakilamathoti bhattadaratho. Vihārapacchāyāyanti vihārapaccante chāyāya. Yadevassa [P 3.0357] divā samādhinimittaṃ manasikataṃ hotīti yaṃ eva tassa tato purimadivasabhāge samathanimittaṃ citte kataṃ hoti. Tadevassa tasmiṃ samaye samudācaratīti taṃyeva etassa tasmiṃ samaye divāvihāre nisinnassa manodvāre sañcarati. Ojaṭṭhāyīti ojāya ṭhito patiṭṭhito. Phāsukassa [V 3.0105] hotīti phāsukaṃ assa hoti. Sammukhāti kathentassa sammukhaṭṭhāne. Sutanti sotena sutaṃ. Paṭiggahitanti cittena paṭiggahitaṃ.

28. In the eighth, maṇḍalamāḷe means in the dining hall. Cārittakilamatho is the weariness that has arisen from going on the alms-round. Bhattakilamatho is distress from food. Vihārapacchāyāyaṃ means in the shade at the edge of the monastery. Yad ev’ assa divā samādhinimittaṃ manasikataṃ hoti means whatever sign of tranquility was made present in the mind for that person in the earlier part of that day. Tad ev’ assa tasmiṃ samaye samudācarati means that very sign of tranquility moves about in the mind-door of this one sitting in the day-dwelling at that time. Ojaṭṭhāyī means standing on or established in vitality. Phāsukassa hoti means it is comfortable for him. Sammukhā means in a place directly in front of the one speaking. Sutan means heard with the ear. Paṭiggahitan means received with the mind.

9. Udāyīsuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Udāyī Sutta

29. Navame udāyinti lāḷudāyittheraṃ. Suṇomahaṃ, āvusoti, āvuso, nāhaṃ badhiro, suṇāmi bhagavato vacanaṃ, pañhaṃ pana upaparikkhāmīti. Adhicittanti samādhivipassanācittaṃ. Idaṃ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānanti idaṃ jhānattayasaṅkhātaṃ anussatikāraṇaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṃvattatīti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve sukhavihāratthāya pavattati. Ālokasaññanti ālokanimitte uppannasaññaṃ. Divā saññaṃ adhiṭṭhātīti divāti saññaṃ ṭhapeti[M 3.0103]. Yathā divā tathā rattinti yathānena divā ālokasaññā manasikatā, rattimpi tatheva taṃ manasi karoti. Yathā rattiṃ tathā divāti yathā vānena rattiṃ ālokasaññā manasikatā, divāpi taṃ tatheva manasi karoti. Vivaṭenāti pākaṭena. Apariyonaddhenāti nīvaraṇehi anonaddhena. Sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāvetīti dibbacakkhuñāṇatthāya sahobhāsakaṃ cittaṃ brūheti vaḍḍheti. Yaṃ pana “ālokasaññaṃ [P 3.0358] manasi karotī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ thinamiddhavinodanālokasaññaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na dibbacakkhuñāṇālokanti veditabbaṃ. Ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāyāti dibbacakkhusaṅkhātassa ñāṇadassanassa paṭilābhāya.

29. In the ninth, Udāyiṃ refers to the Elder Lāḷudāyī. Suṇom’ ahaṃ, āvuso means: 'Friend, I am not deaf; I hear the Blessed One’s question, but I am examining the question.' Adhicittan means the mind of tranquility and insight. Idaṃ, bhante, anussatiṭṭhānan means this cause for recollection, which is designated as the threefold jhāna. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṃvattati means it conduces to dwelling happily in this very existence. Ālokasaññan means the perception that has arisen in the sign of light. Divā saññaṃ adhiṭṭhāti means he establishes the perception 'as day.' Yathā divā tathā rattiṃ means just as he has attended to the perception of light by day, so too he attends to it at night. Yathā rattiṃ tathā divā means just as he has attended to the perception of light at night, so too he attends to it by day. Vivaṭena means manifest. Apariyonaddhena means not covered by the hindrances. Sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti means for the purpose of the knowledge of the divine eye, he increases and develops the luminous insight mind. However, what is said as 'he attends to the perception of light' is said in reference to the perception of light for dispelling sloth and torpor; it should be understood that this is not the light of the divine eye knowledge. Ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya means for obtaining the knowledge and vision designated as the divine eye.

Imameva kāyantiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ sabbaṃ sabbākārena vitthārato visuddhimagge kāyagatāsatikammaṭṭhāne vuttaṃ. Kāmarāgappahānāyāti pañcakāmaguṇikassa rāgassa pahānatthāya. Seyyathāpi passeyyāti yathā passeyya. Sarīranti matasarīraṃ. Sivathikāya chaḍḍitanti susāne apaviddhaṃ. Ekāhaṃ matassa assāti ekāhamataṃ. Dvīhaṃ matassa assāti dvīhamataṃ. Tīhaṃ matassa assāti tīhamataṃ. Bhastā viya vāyunā uddhaṃ jīvitapariyādānā yathānukkamaṃ samuggatena sūnabhāvena dhumātattā uddhumātaṃ, uddhumātameva uddhumātakaṃ. Paṭikūlattā vā kucchitaṃ uddhumātanti uddhumātakaṃ. Vinīlaṃ vuccati viparibhinnavaṇṇaṃ, vinīlameva vinīlakaṃ. Paṭikūlattā vā kucchitaṃ vinīlanti vinīlakaṃ. Maṃsussadaṭṭhānesu rattavaṇṇassa pubbasannicayaṭṭhānesu setavaṇṇassa yebhuyyena ca nīlavaṇṇassa nīlaṭṭhāne nīlasāṭakapārutasseva chavasarīrassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Paribhinnaṭṭhānehi navahi vā vaṇamukhehi vissandamānaṃ pubbaṃ vipubbaṃ, vipubbameva [V 3.0106] vipubbakaṃ. Paṭikūlattā vā kucchitaṃ vipubbanti vipubbakaṃ. Vipubbakaṃ jātaṃ tathābhāvaṃ gatanti vipubbakajātaṃ.

In the sections beginning with Imam eva kāyaṃ, whatever should be said has all been stated by me in every way and in detail in the Visuddhimagga, in the section on the meditation subject of mindfulness directed to the body. Kāmarāgappahānāya means for the purpose of abandoning the lust that has the five strands of sensual pleasure as its object. Seyyathāpi passeyya means just as one might see. Sarīran means a dead body. Sivathikāya chaḍḍitan means discarded in a charnel ground. Ekāhamataṃ means it has been dead for one day. Dvīhamataṃ means it has been dead for two days. Tīhamataṃ means it has been dead for three days. Because it is puffed up with a swollen state that has risen up sequentially after the exhaustion of the life faculty, like a leather bag due to wind, it is called uddhumātaṃ, bloated. Uddhumātam eva uddhumātakaṃ, a bloated thing is just a bloated thing. Or, because of its repulsiveness, a disgusting bloated thing is uddhumātakaṃ. A body of changed color is called vinīlaṃ, discolored. Vinīlam eva vinīlakaṃ, a discolored thing is just a discolored thing. Or, because of its repulsiveness, a disgusting discolored thing is vinīlakaṃ. This is a term for a corpse that is red in places with much flesh, white in places where pus has collected, and in blue places is mostly blue, as if wrapped in a blue cloth. A body with pus flowing from broken places or from the nine wound-openings is vipubbaṃ, festering. Vipubbam eva vipubbakaṃ, a festering thing is just a festering thing. Or, because of its repulsiveness, a disgusting festering thing is vipubbakaṃ. Vipubbakajātaṃ means it has become a festering thing, it has gone to such a state.

So [P 3.0359] imameva kāyanti so bhikkhu imaṃ attano kāyaṃ tena kāyena saddhiṃ ñāṇena upasaṃharati upaneti. Kathaṃ? Ayampi kho kāyo evaṃdhammo evaṃbhāvī evaṃanatītoti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – āyu usmā viññāṇanti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ dhammānaṃ atthitāya ayaṃ kāyo ṭhānagamanādikhamo hoti, imesaṃ pana vigamā ayampi evaṃdhammo evaṃpūtikasabhāvoyevāti. Evaṃbhāvīti evamevaṃ uddhumātādibhedo bhavissati. Evaṃ anatītoti evaṃ uddhumātādibhāvaṃ anatikkanto.

So imam eva kāyan means: that bhikkhu, with knowledge, brings this body of his to bear upon and compares it with that (dead) body. How? 'This body, too, has such a nature, it is bound to become so, it has not gone beyond that.' This is what is meant: because of the existence of these three things—life, heat, and consciousness—this body is capable of standing, going, and so on. But because of the absence of these, this body too has such a nature, it has a putrid nature. Evaṃbhāvī means it will become of such a kind, distinguished as bloated and so on. Evaṃanatīto means not having gone beyond such a state as being bloated and so on.

Khajjamānanti [M 3.0104] udarādīsu nisīditvā udaramaṃsaoṭṭhamaṃsaakkhikamaṃsādīni luñcitvā luñcitvā khādiyamānaṃ. Samaṃsalohitanti sesāvasesamaṃsalohitayuttaṃ. Nimmaṃsalohitamakkhitanti maṃse khīṇepi lohitaṃ na sussati, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “nimmaṃsalohitamakkhita”nti. Aññenāti aññena disābhāgena. Hatthaṭṭhikanti catusaṭṭhibhedampi hatthaṭṭhikaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ vippakiṇṇaṃ. Pādaṭṭhikādīsupi eseva nayo. Terovassikānīti atikkantasaṃvaccharāni. Pūtīnīti abbhokāse ṭhitāni vātātapavuṭṭhisamphassena terovassikāneva pūtīni honti, antobhūmigatāni pana cirataraṃ tiṭṭhanti. Cuṇṇakajātānīti cuṇṇavicuṇṇaṃ hutvā vippakiṇṇāni. Sabbattha [P 3.0360] so imamevāti vuttanayena khajjamānādīnaṃ vasena yojanā kātabbā. Asmimānasamugghātāyāti asmīti pavattassa navavidhassa mānassa samugghātatthāya. Anekadhātupaṭivedhāyāti anekadhātūnaṃ paṭivijjhanatthāya. Satova abhikkamatīti gacchanto satipaññāhi samannāgatova gacchati. Satova paṭikkamatīti paṭinivattantopi satipaññāhi samannāgatova nivattati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Satisampajaññāyāti satiyā ca ñāṇassa ca atthāya. Iti imasmiṃ sutte satiñāṇāni missakāni kathitānīti.

'Being eaten' means: staying on the belly and so on, and tearing out again and again the flesh of the belly, the flesh of the lips, the flesh of the eyes, and so on, it is eaten. 'With flesh and blood' means: endowed with the remaining flesh and blood. 'Smeared with blood but without flesh' means: even when the flesh is consumed, the blood does not dry up; referring to that, it is said, 'smeared with blood but without flesh.' 'By another' means: by another direction or part. 'Hand bone' means: the hand bone, of sixty-four kinds, scattered individually, one by one. For foot bones and so on, this is the method. 'Over a year old' means: having passed years. 'Rotten' means: those situated in the open, through contact with wind, sun, and rain, become rotten over a long period of time; but those that have gone inside the earth last for a very long time. 'Become powder' means: having become powder and dust, they are scattered. Everywhere, the application should be made by way of 'being eaten,' etc., according to the method stated as 'he, this very...' 'For the uprooting of the conceit "I am"' means: for the purpose of uprooting the ninefold conceit that proceeds as 'I am.' 'For the penetration of the many elements' means: for the purpose of penetrating the many elements. 'He goes forward mindfully' means: when going, he goes endowed with mindfulness and wisdom. 'He returns mindfully' means: when turning back, he turns back endowed with mindfulness and wisdom. For the remaining phrases, this is the method. 'For mindfulness and clear comprehension' means: for the sake of mindfulness and for the sake of knowledge.

10. Anuttariyasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Sutta on the Unsurpassables

30. Dasame [V 3.0107] uccāvacanti yaṃ kiñci mahantakhuddakaṃ, uccanīcaṃ vā. Hīnanti nihīnaṃ. Gammanti gāmavāsikānaṃ dassanaṃ. Pothujjanikanti puthujjanānaṃ santakaṃ. Anariyanti na ariyaṃ na uttamaṃ na parisuddhaṃ. Anatthasaṃhitanti na atthasannissitaṃ. Na nibbidāyāti na vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāya. Na virāgāyāti na rāgādīnaṃ virajjanatthāya. Na nirodhāyāti na rāgādīnaṃ appavattinirodhāya. Na upasamāyāti na rāgādīnaṃ vūpasamanatthāya. Na abhiññāyāti na abhijānanatthāya. Na sambodhāyāti na sambodhisaṅkhātassa catumaggañāṇassa paṭivijjhanatthāya. Na nibbānāyāti na nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya.

30. In the tenth sutta, 'high and low' means: whatever is great or small, or high and low. 'Inferior' means: base. 'Vulgar' means: seen by village-dwellers. 'Worldly' means: belonging to ordinary people. 'Ignoble' means: not noble, not supreme, not pure. 'Not connected with the goal' means: not based on benefit. 'Not for disenchantment' means: it does not lead to the purpose of becoming disenchanted with the round of existence. 'Not for dispassion' means: it does not lead to the purpose of becoming free from lust and so on. 'Not for cessation' means: it does not lead to the purpose of the non-arising cessation of lust and so on. 'Not for peace' means: it does not lead to the purpose of calming lust and so on. 'Not for direct knowledge' means: it does not lead to the purpose of knowing with higher knowledge. 'Not for enlightenment' means: it does not lead to the purpose of penetrating the knowledge of the four paths called enlightenment. 'Not for Nibbāna' means: it does not lead to the purpose of realizing Nibbāna.

Niviṭṭhasaddhoti patiṭṭhitasaddho. Niviṭṭhapemoti [P 3.0361] patiṭṭhitapemo. Ekantagatoti ekantaṃ gato, acalappattoti attho. Abhippasannoti ativiya pasanno. Etadānuttariyanti etaṃ anuttaraṃ. Hatthismimpi sikkhatīti hatthinimittaṃ [M 3.0105] sikkhitabbaṃ hatthisippaṃ sikkhati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Uccāvacanti mahantakhuddakaṃ sippaṃ sikkhati.

'One with settled faith' means: one with established faith. 'One with settled love' means: one with established love. 'Gone to the ultimate' means: gone certainly; the meaning is having reached the unshakable. 'Exceedingly pleased' means: very pleased. `Etadānuttariyaṃ` means: this is unsurpassable. 'He trains even in [the art of] the elephant' means: he trains in the elephant craft, a skill to be learned based on the signs of an elephant. For the remaining phrases, this is the method. 'High and low' means: he trains in great and small crafts.

Upaṭṭhitā pāricariyeti pāricariyāya paccupaṭṭhitā. Bhāvayanti anussatinti anuttaraṃ anussatiṃ bhāventi. Vivekappaṭisaṃyuttanti nibbānanissitaṃ katvā. Khemanti nirupaddavaṃ. Amatagāminanti nibbānagāminaṃ, ariyamaggaṃ bhāventīti attho. Appamāde pamoditāti satiyā avippavāsasaṅkhāte appamāde āmoditā pamoditā. Nipakāti nepakkena samannāgatā. Sīlasaṃvutāti sīlena saṃvutā pihitā. Te ve kālena paccentīti te ve yuttappayuttakāle jānanti. Yattha dukkhaṃ nirujjhatīti yasmiṃ ṭhāne sakalaṃ vaṭṭadukkhaṃ nirujjhati, taṃ amataṃ mahānibbānaṃ te bhikkhū jānantīti. Imasmiṃ sutte cha anuttariyāni missakāni kathitānīti.

`Upaṭṭhitā pāricariyā` means: they are established in service. 'They develop recollection' means: they develop the unsurpassable recollection. 'Connected with seclusion' means: having made it based on Nibbāna. 'Safety' means: without affliction. 'Leading to the deathless' means: leading to Nibbāna; the meaning is that they cultivate the noble path. 'Delighting in heedfulness' means: they rejoice and delight in heedfulness, which is defined as the non-absence of mindfulness. 'Discerning' means: endowed with discernment. 'Restrained by virtue' means: restrained and covered by virtue. 'They truly know in time' means: they truly know at a suitable and proper time. 'Where suffering ceases' means: in whichever place all the suffering of the round ceases, those monks know that deathless, great Nibbāna. In this sutta, six unsurpassable qualities are taught as mixed.

Anuttariyavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Unsurpassables, the Third.

4. Devatāvaggo

4. The Chapter on Deities.

1. Sekhasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on the Trainee.

31. Catutthassa [V 3.0108][P 3.0362] paṭhame sekhassāti sattavidhassa sekhassa. Puthujjane pana vattabbameva natthi. Parihānāyāti uparūpariguṇaparihānāya.

31. In the first [sutta] of the fourth [chapter], `sekhassa` means: of the sevenfold trainee. But concerning an ordinary person, there is nothing to be said. `Parihānāya` means: for the decline of the higher and higher qualities.

2-3. Aparihānasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

2-3. Commentary on the Two Discourses on Non-Decline.

32-33. Dutiye satthugāravatāti satthari garubhāvo. Dhammagāravatāti navavidhe lokuttaradhamme garubhāvo. Saṅghagāravatāti saṅghe garubhāvo. Sikkhāgāravatāti tīsu sikkhāsu garubhāvo. Appamādagāravatāti appamāde garubhāvo. Paṭisanthāragāravatāti dhammāmisavasena duvidhe paṭisanthāre garubhāvo. Satthā garu assāti satthugaru. Dhammo garu assāti dhammagaru. Tibbagāravoti bahalagāravo. Paṭisanthāre [M 3.0106] gāravo assāti paṭisanthāragāravo. Tatiye sappatissoti sajeṭṭhako sagāravo. Hirottappaṃ panettha missakaṃ kathitaṃ.

In the second [sutta], `satthugāravatā` means: reverence for the Teacher. `Dhammagāravatā` means: reverence for the ninefold supramundane Dhamma. `Saṅghagāravatā` means: reverence for the Saṅgha. `Sikkhāgāravatā` means: reverence for the three trainings. `Appamādagāravatā` means: reverence for heedfulness. `Paṭisanthāragāravatā` means: reverence for the two kinds of hospitality, by way of the Dhamma and material things. `Satthugaru` means: one for whom the Teacher is revered. `Dhammagaru` means: one for whom the Dhamma is revered. `Tibbagāravo` means: having abundant reverence. `Paṭisanthāragāravo` means: one who has reverence for hospitality. In the third [sutta], `sappatisso` means: with a senior, with reverence. Here, shame and fear of wrongdoing are taught in combination.

4. Mahāmoggallānasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Mahāmoggallāna Sutta.

34. Catutthe tisso nāma bhikkhūti therasseva saddhivihāriko. Mahiddhiko mahānubhāvoti ijjhanaṭṭhena mahatī iddhi assāti mahiddhiko. Anupharaṇaṭṭhena mahā ānubhāvo assāti mahānubhāvo. Cirassaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, imaṃ pariyāyamakāsīti evarūpaṃ loke pakatiyā piyasamudāhāravacanaṃ hoti. Lokiyā [P 3.0363] hi cirassaṃ āgatampi anāgatapubbampi manāpajātiyaṃ āgataṃ disvā “kuto bhavaṃ āgato, cirassaṃ bhavaṃ āgato, kathaṃ te idhāgamanamaggo ñāto, kiṃ maggamūḷhosī”tiādīni vadanti. Ayaṃ pana āgatapubbattāyeva evamāha. Thero hi kālena kālaṃ brahmalokaṃ gacchatiyeva. Tattha pariyāyamakāsīti vāraṃ akāsi. Yadidaṃ idhāgamanāyāti yo ayaṃ idhāgamanāya vāro, taṃ cirassaṃ akāsīti vuttaṃ hoti. Idamāsanaṃ paññattanti [V 3.0109] mahārahaṃ brahmapallaṅkaṃ paññāpetvā evamāha. Aveccappasādenāti adhigatena acalena maggappasādena. Imasmiṃ sutte sotāpattimaggañāṇaṃ kathitaṃ.

34. In the fourth sutta, the monk named Tissa was the elder’s co-resident disciple. ‘Of great psychic power and great might’ (mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo): ‘Of great psychic power’ (mahiddhiko) means he possessed great psychic power (mahatī iddhi) in the sense of accomplishment (ijjhanaṭṭhena). ‘Of great might’ (mahānubhāvo) means he possessed great might (mahā ānubhāvo) in the sense of pervading (anupharaṇaṭṭhena). ‘It has been a long time, friend Moggallāna, since you made this visit’ (cirassaṃ kho, mārisa moggallāna, imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi): such a phrase is a conventional term of fond address in the world. For worldly people, when they see someone agreeable who has arrived after a long absence or who has never come before, they say things like, ‘Where have you come from? It’s been a long time since you came. How did you know the way here? Were you lost on the way?’ and so on. But this one said this precisely because he had come before. For the elder indeed goes to the Brahmā realm from time to time. Therein, ‘made a visit’ (pariyāyamakāsi) means he made a turn (vāraṃ akāsi). ‘That is, for coming here’ (yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya) means: the turn that is for coming here, he is said to have made after a long time. ‘This seat is prepared’ (idamāsanaṃ paññattaṃ): having prepared a Brahmā-couch worthy of a great one, he spoke thus. ‘With unwavering confidence’ (aveccappasādena) means with the attained, unshakeable confidence of the path. In this discourse, the knowledge of the path of stream-entry is taught.

5. Vijjābhāgiyasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Vijjābhāgiya Sutta

35. Pañcame vijjābhāgiyāti vijjākoṭṭhāsikā. Aniccasaññāti aniccānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā. Anicce dukkhasaññāti dukkhānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā. Dukkhe anattasaññāti anattānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā. Pahānasaññāti pahānānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā. Virāgasaññāti virāgānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā. Nirodhasaññāti nirodhānupassanāñāṇe uppannasaññā.

35. In the fifth sutta, ‘partaking of knowledge’ (vijjābhāgiyā) means pertaining to the portion of knowledge (vijjākoṭṭhāsikā). ‘Perception of impermanence’ (aniccasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of impermanence. ‘Perception of suffering in the impermanent’ (anicce dukkhasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of suffering. ‘Perception of not-self in suffering’ (dukkhe anattasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of not-self. ‘Perception of abandoning’ (pahānasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of abandoning. ‘Perception of dispassion’ (virāgasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of dispassion. ‘Perception of cessation’ (nirodhasaññā) is the perception that has arisen in the knowledge of contemplation of cessation.

6. Vivādamūlasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sutta on the Roots of Dispute

36. Chaṭṭhe [M 3.0107] vivādamūlānīti vivādassa mūlāni. Kodhanoti kujjhanalakkhaṇena kodhena samannāgato. Upanāhīti veraappaṭinissaggalakkhaṇena upanāhena samannāgato. Ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānanti dvinnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vivādo kathaṃ devamanussānaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattati? Kosambakakkhandhake viya dvīsu bhikkhūsu vivādaṃ āpannesu tasmiṃ vihāre tesaṃ antevāsikā vivadanti, tesaṃ ovādaṃ gaṇhanto bhikkhunisaṅgho vivadati. Tato tesaṃ upaṭṭhākā vivadanti, atha manussānaṃ ārakkhadevatā [P 3.0364] dve koṭṭhāsā honti. Tathā dhammavādīnaṃ ārakkhadevatā dhammavādiniyo honti, adhammavādīnaṃ adhammavādiniyo. Tato ārakkhadevatānaṃ mittā bhummadevatā bhijjanti. Evaṃ paramparāya yāva brahmalokā ṭhapetvā ariyasāvake sabbe devamanussā dve koṭṭhāsā honti. Dhammavādīhi pana adhammavādinova bahutarā honti. Tato yaṃ bahukehi gahitaṃ, taṃ gacchanti. Dhammaṃ vissajjetvā bahutarāva adhammaṃ gaṇhanti. Te adhammaṃ purakkhatvā viharantā apāye nibbattanti. Evaṃ dvinnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vivādo devamanussānaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya hoti. Ajjhattaṃ vāti tumhākaṃ abbhantaraparisāya. Bahiddhāti paresaṃ parisāya.

36. In the sixth sutta, ‘roots of dispute’ (vivādamūlāni) means the roots of dispute. ‘One who is angry’ (kodhano) is one endowed with anger, characterized by being prone to anger. ‘One who is resentful’ (upanāhī) is one endowed with resentment, characterized by not relinquishing enmity. ‘For the harm and suffering of devas and humans’ (ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṃ): How does a dispute between two monks lead to harm and suffering for devas and humans? As in the Kosambaka chapter, when two monks engage in a dispute, their pupils in that monastery also dispute, and the community of bhikkhunīs that receives their advice also disputes. Then their supporters dispute, and the guardian deities of humans divide into two factions. Similarly, the guardian deities of those who speak according to the Dhamma become proponents of the Dhamma, while those of the non-Dhamma speakers become proponents of non-Dhamma. Then the friends of the guardian deities, the earth deities, also split. Thus, in succession, all devas and humans, up to the Brahma world, except for noble disciples, divide into two factions. However, the non-Dhamma speakers are more numerous than the Dhamma speakers. Thus, they go with what is held by the majority. Rejecting the Dhamma, the majority take up the non-Dhamma. Those who live prioritizing the non-Dhamma are reborn in the lower realms. In this way, the dispute between two monks leads to harm and suffering for devas and humans. ‘Internally’ (ajjhattaṃ vā) means within your own community. ‘Externally’ (bahiddhā) means in the community of others.

Makkhīti paresaṃ guṇamakkhanalakkhaṇena makkhena samannāgato. Paḷāsīti yugaggāhalakkhaṇena [V 3.0110] paḷāsena samannāgato. Issukīti parassa sakkārādīni issāyanalakkhaṇāya issāya samannāgato. Maccharīti āvāsamacchariyādīhi samannāgato. Saṭhoti kerāṭiko. Māyāvīti katapaṭicchādako. Pāpicchoti asantasambhāvanicchako dussīlo. Micchādiṭṭhīti natthikavādī, ahetuvādī, akiriyavādī. Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsīti sayaṃ diṭṭhameva parāmasati. Ādhānaggāhīti daḷhaggāhī. Duppaṭinissaggīti na sakkā hoti gahitaṃ vissajjāpetuṃ. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭameva kathitaṃ.

‘One who is hypocritical’ (makkhī) is one endowed with hypocrisy (makkha), characterized by disparaging others’ virtues. ‘One who is spiteful’ (paḷāsī) is one endowed with spite (paḷāsa), characterized by partisanship. ‘One who is envious’ (issukī) is one endowed with envy (issā), characterized by being envious of others’ gains, etc. ‘One who is stingy’ (maccharī) is one endowed with stinginess regarding dwellings, etc. ‘One who is deceitful’ (saṭho) is a cheat (kerāṭiko). ‘One who is a trickster’ (māyāvī) is one who conceals what has been done. ‘One of evil wishes’ (pāpiccho) is an immoral person who desires to display non-existent qualities. ‘One of wrong view’ (micchādiṭṭhī) is a nihilist, a proponent of causelessness, and a proponent of inaction. ‘One who clings to his own view’ (sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī) grasps only the view he himself has seen. ‘One who is tenacious’ (ādhānaggāhī) is one who grasps firmly. ‘One who relinquishes with difficulty’ (duppaṭinissaggī) is one whom it is not possible to make relinquish what has been grasped. In this sutta, only the round of rebirth is discussed.

7. Dānasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Discourse on Giving

37. Sattame [P 3.0365] veḷukaṇḍakīti veḷukaṇḍakanagaravāsinī. Chaḷaṅgasamannāgatanti chahi guṇaṅgehi samannāgataṃ. Dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpetīti dānaṃ deti. Pubbeva dānā sumanoti dānaṃ dassāmīti māsaḍḍhamāsato paṭṭhāya [M 3.0108] somanassappatto hoti. Ettha hi pubbecetanā dassāmīti cittuppādakālato paṭṭhāya “ito uṭṭhitena dānaṃ dassāmī”ti khettaggahaṇaṃ ādiṃ katvā cintentassa labbhati. Dadaṃ cittaṃ pasādetīti evaṃ vuttā muñcacetanā pana dānakāleyeva labbhati. Datvā attamano hotīti ayaṃ pana aparacetanā aparāparaṃ anussarantassa labbhati. Vītarāgāti vigatarāgā khīṇāsavā. Rāgavinayāya vā paṭipannāti rāgavinayapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā. Ukkaṭṭhadesanā cesā, na kevalaṃ pana khīṇāsavānaṃ, anāgāmi-sakadāgāmi-sotāpannānampi antamaso tadahupabbajitassa bhaṇḍagāhakasāmaṇerassāpi dinnā dakkhiṇā chaḷaṅgasamannāgatāva hoti. Sopi hi sotāpattimaggatthameva pabbajito.

37. In the seventh sutta, 'Veḷukaṇḍakī' means a female resident of the city of Veḷukaṇḍaka. 'Endowed with six factors' means endowed with six factors that are qualities. 'Establishes an offering' means gives a gift. 'Joyful even before giving' means from a month or half a month before giving, one becomes joyful with the thought, “I will give a gift.” Here, the preliminary volition is obtained by one who, starting from the time the thought 'I will give' arises, thinks, beginning with taking a field, 'With what has arisen from this, I will give a gift.' 'While giving, one clarifies the mind' refers to the so-called volition of relinquishing, which is obtained only at the time of giving. 'Having given, one is delighted' refers to this subsequent volition, which is obtained by one who recollects it again and again. 'Free from passion' means those free from passion, the arahants. 'Or practicing for the removal of passion' means those who have undertaken the practice for the removal of passion. And this is a superlative teaching. However, an offering endowed with six factors is not only one given to arahants, but also to non-returners, once-returners, and stream-enterers, and at the very least, even to a novice who is a storekeeper and who ordained that very day. For he too ordained solely for the sake of the path to stream-entry.

Yaññassa sampadāti dānassa paripuṇṇatā. Saññatāti sīlasaññamena saññatā. Sayaṃ ācamayitvānāti attanāva hatthapāde dhovitvā mukhaṃ vikkhāletvā. Sakehi pāṇibhīti attano hatthehi. Sayehītipi pāṭho. Saddhoti ratanattayaguṇe saddahanto. Muttena cetasāti lābhamacchariyādīhi vimuttena cittena. Abyāpajjhaṃ [P 3.0366] sukhaṃ lokanti niddukkhaṃ uḷārasukhasomanassaṃ devalokaṃ.

‘The accomplishment of sacrifice’ means the completeness of the gift. ‘Restrained’ means restrained by the restraint of virtue. ‘Sayaṃ ācamayitvāna’ means having washed the hands and feet and rinsed the mouth oneself. ‘With one’s own hands’ means with one’s own hands. There is also the reading ‘sayehi’. ‘Faithful’ means believing in the virtues of the Triple Gem. ‘With a mind freed’ means with a mind freed from stinginess regarding gain and so on. ‘A world of unafflicted happiness’ means the heavenly world, free from suffering, with sublime happiness and gladness.

8. Attakārīsuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Attakārī Sutta

38. Aṭṭhame [V 3.0111] addasaṃ vā assosiṃ vāti akkhīni ummīletvā mā addasaṃ, asukasmiṃ nāma ṭhāne vasatīti mā assosiṃ, kathentassa vā vacanaṃ mā assosiṃ. Kathañhi nāmāti kena nāma kāraṇena. Ārambhadhātūti ārabhanavasena pavattavīriyaṃ. Nikkamadhātūti kosajjato nikkhamanasabhāvaṃ vīriyaṃ. Parakkamadhātūti parakkamasabhāvo. Thāmadhātūti thāmasabhāvo. Ṭhitidhātūti ṭhitisabhāvo. Upakkamadhātūti upakkamasabhāvo. Sabbaṃ cetaṃ tena tenākārena pavattassa vīriyasseva nāmaṃ.

38. In the eighth, the phrase ‘I did not see or hear’ means: I did not open my eyes to see; I did not hear that someone lives in such and such a place; or I did not hear the words of someone speaking. ‘How indeed’ means by what reason. ‘The element of initiative’ means energy that proceeds by way of initiating. ‘The element of exertion’ means energy that has the nature of emerging from sloth. ‘The element of striving’ means the nature of striving. ‘The element of strength’ means the nature of strength. ‘The element of steadfastness’ means the nature of steadfastness. ‘The element of endeavor’ means the nature of endeavor. And all these are names for energy itself, proceeding in this or that manner.

9-10. Nidānasuttādivaṇṇanā

9-10. Explanation of the Nidāna Sutta, etc.

39-40. Navame kammānanti vaṭṭagāmikammānaṃ. Samudayāyāti piṇḍakaraṇatthāya. Nidānanti paccayo. Lobhajenāti lobhato jātena. Na [M 3.0109] paññāyantīti “evarūpena kammena nibbattā”ti na dissanti. Sukkapakkhe kammānanti vivaṭṭagāmikammānaṃ. Iti imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ. Dasame niculavaneti mahāmucalindavane. Saddhammoti sāsanasaddhammo.

In the ninth, ‘actions’ means actions that lead to the round of existence. ‘For the sake of arising’ means for the purpose of combination. ‘Source’ means condition. ‘Born from greed’ means born from greed. ‘They do not appear’ means ‘produced by such an action’ they are not seen. In the bright side, ‘actions’ means actions that lead to release from the round of existence. Thus, in this sutta, the round and the release from it are taught. In the tenth, ‘in the Niculavana’ means in the great Mucalinda grove. ‘The true Dhamma’ means the true Dhamma of the Dispensation.

11. Dārukkhandhasuttavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Dārukkhandha Sutta

41. Ekādasame cetovasippattoti cittavasibhāvaṃ patto. Pathavītveva adhimucceyyāti thaddhākāraṃ pathavīdhātūti sallakkheyya. Yaṃ [P 3.0367] nissāyāti yaṃ vijjamānaṃ thaddhākāraṃ pathavīdhātuṃ nissāya amuṃ dārukkhandhaṃ pathavītveva adhimucceyya, sā ettha pathavīdhātu atthīti. Iminā nayena sesapadānipi veditabbāni. Yatheva hi tasmiṃ thaddhākārā pathavīdhātu atthi, evaṃ yūsākārā āpodhātu, uṇhākārā tejodhātu, vitthambhanākārā vāyodhātu, rattavaṇṇamhi sāre padumapupphavaṇṇā subhadhātu, pūtibhūte cuṇṇe ceva pheggupapaṭikāsu ca amanuññavaṇṇā asubhadhātu, taṃ nissāya amuṃ dārukkhandhaṃ asubhantveva adhimucceyya sallakkheyyāti. Imasmiṃ sutte missakavihāro nāma kathito.

41. In the eleventh sutta, ‘one who has attained mastery of mind’ means one who has attained the state of mastery over the mind. ‘One should resolve upon it as just earth’ means one should perceive the earth element as being of a solid nature. ‘Depending on which’ means: depending on which existing earth element of a solid nature, one should resolve upon this log as just earth, thinking, ‘That earth element exists here.’ By this method, the remaining terms should also be understood. For just as the earth element of a solid nature exists in that log, so too the water element of a cohesive nature, the fire element of a hot nature, and the air element of a distending nature exist. In the red-colored heartwood, the beautiful element with the color of a lotus flower exists. In the powder that has become putrid and in the sapwood and bark, the foul element of a disagreeable color exists. Depending on that, one should resolve upon and perceive that log as just ‘foul’. In this sutta, what is called the ‘mixed dwelling’ is taught.

12. Nāgitasuttavaṇṇanā

12. Explanation of the Nāgita Sutta

42. Dvādasame [V 3.0112] gāmantavihārinti gāmantasenāsanavāsiṃ. Samāhitaṃ nisinnanti tasmiṃ gāmantasenāsane samādhiṃ appetvā nisinnaṃ. Idānimanti idāni imaṃ. Samādhimhā cāvessatīti samādhito uṭṭhāpessati. Na attamano homīti na sakamano homi. Pacalāyamānanti niddāyamānaṃ. Ekattanti ekasabhāvaṃ, ekaggatābhūtaṃ araññasaññaṃyeva citte karissatīti attho. Anurakkhissatīti anuggaṇhissati. Avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimocessatīti aññasmiṃ kāle avimuttaṃ cittaṃ idāni pañcahi vimuttīhi vimocayissati. Riñcatīti vajjeti vissajjeti. Paṭipaṇāmetvāti [P 3.0368] panuditvā vissajjetvā. Uccārapassāvakammāyāti uccārapassāvakaraṇatthāya. Iminā ettakena ṭhānena satthārā araññasenāsanassa vaṇṇo kathito. Suttassa pana paṭhamakoṭṭhāse yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttamevāti.

42. In the twelfth sutta, ‘dwelling near a village’ means residing in a lodging near a village. ‘Seated in concentration’ means seated in that lodging near a village, having entered into concentration. ‘Now this…’ means at this time, this person. ‘Will disturb from concentration’ means will cause to rise from concentration. ‘I would not be pleased’ means I would not be of my own mind. ‘Drowsy’ means sleepy. ‘Oneness’ means a single nature, having become one-pointed; the meaning is that one will establish only the perception of the forest in the mind. ‘Will protect’ means will support. ‘Or will free the unfreed mind’ means at another time, the mind that was unfreed, one will now free by the five kinds of freedom. ‘Leaves’ means avoids, relinquishes. ‘Having set aside’ means having dispelled, having relinquished. ‘For the act of defecation and urination’ means for the purpose of performing the act of defecation and urination. By this much, the Teacher has spoken the praise of a forest lodging. As for what should be said in the first section of the sutta, that has already been stated below.

Devatāvaggo catuttho.

The Devatā Chapter, the Fourth.

5. Dhammikavaggo

5. The Dhammika Chapter

1. Nāgasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Nāga Sutta

43. Pañcamassa [M 3.0110] paṭhame āyasmatā ānandena saddhinti idaṃ “āyāmānandā”ti theraṃ āmantetvā gatattā vuttaṃ, satthā pana anūnehi pañcahi bhikkhusatehi parivuto tattha agamāsīti veditabbo. Tenupasaṅkamīti teheva pañcahi bhikkhusatehi parivuto upasaṅkami. Parisiñcitvāti vohāravacanametaṃ, nhāyitvāti attho. Pubbāpayamānoti rattadupaṭṭaṃ nivāsetvā uttarāsaṅgacīvaraṃ dvīhi hatthehi gahetvā pacchimalokadhātuṃ piṭṭhito katvā puratthimalokadhātuṃ abhimukho vodakabhāvena gattāni pubbasadisāni kurumāno aṭṭhāsīti attho. Bhikkhusaṅghopi tena tena ṭhānena otaritvā nhatvā paccuttaritvā satthāraṃyeva parivāretvā aṭṭhāsi. Iti tasmiṃ samaye [V 3.0113] ākāsato patamānaṃ rattasuvaṇṇakuṇḍalaṃ viya sūriyo pacchimalokadhātuṃ paṭipajji, parisuddharajatamaṇḍalo viya pācīnalokadhātuto cando abbhuggañchi, majjhaṭṭhānepi pañcabhikkhusataparivāro sammāsambuddho chabbaṇṇabuddharasmiyo [P 3.0369] vissajjetvā pubbakoṭṭhakanadītīre lokaṃ alaṅkurumāno aṭṭhāsi.

43. In the first sutta of the fifth vagga, the phrase ‘with the Venerable Ānanda’ was said because of having gone after addressing the elder, ‘Let us go, Ānanda.’ It should be known, however, that the Teacher went there surrounded by no less than five hundred monks. ‘He approached’ means he approached surrounded by those very five hundred monks. ‘Parisiñcitvā’ (having sprinkled) is a conventional expression; the meaning is ‘having bathed’. The meaning of ‘Pubbāpayamāno’ is: having put on a red, double-layered lower garment, holding the upper robe with both hands, with the western world-sphere behind him and facing the eastern world-sphere, making his limbs dry and as they were before, he stood. The community of monks also, descending at various places, having bathed, and having come up again, stood surrounding only the Teacher. Thus, at that time, the sun, like a red-gold earring falling from the sky, went to the western world-sphere; the moon, like a circle of pure silver, rose from the eastern world-sphere; and in the middle place, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surrounded by five hundred monks, emitting the six-colored Buddha-rays, stood on the bank of the river at the eastern bathing place, adorning the world.

Tena kho pana samayena…pe… seto nāma nāgoti setavaṇṇatāya evaṃ laddhanāmo hatthināgo. Mahātūriyatāḷitavāditenāti mahantena tūriyatāḷitavāditena. Tattha paṭhamaṃ saṅghaṭṭanaṃ tāḷitaṃ nāma hoti, tato paraṃ vāditaṃ. Janoti hatthidassanatthaṃ sannipatitamahājano. Disvā evamāhāti aṅgapaccaṅgāni ghaṃsitvā nhāpetvā uttāretvā bahitīre ṭhapetvā gattāni vodakāni katvā hatthālaṅkārena alaṅkataṃ taṃ mahānāgaṃ disvā idaṃ “abhirūpo vata, bho”ti pasaṃsāvacanamāha. Kāyupapannoti sarīrasampattiyā upapanno, paripuṇṇaṅgapaccaṅgoti attho. Āyasmā udāyīti paṭisambhidāppatto kāḷudāyitthero. Etadavocāti taṃ mahājanaṃ hatthissa vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇantaṃ disvā “ayaṃ jano ahetukapaṭisandhiyaṃ nibbattahatthino vaṇṇaṃ katheti, na buddhahatthissa. Ahaṃ dāni iminā hatthināgena upamaṃ katvā buddhanāgassa vaṇṇaṃ [M 3.0111] kathessāmī”ti cintetvā etaṃ “hatthimeva nu kho, bhante”tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha mahantanti ārohasampannaṃ. Brahantanti pariṇāhasampannaṃ. Evamāhāti evaṃ vadati. Atha bhagavā yasmā ayaṃ nāgasaddo hatthimhiceva assagoṇauragarukkhamanussesu cāpi pavattati, tasmā hatthimpi khotiādimāha.

At that time… 'Seto nāma nāgo' means a bull elephant who received the name Seto because of his white color. 'Mahātūriyatāḷitavāditenāti' means with a great striking and playing of musical instruments. Therein, the first striking is called tāḷita, and the striking that comes after that is vādita. 'Jano' means the great populace assembled for the purpose of seeing the elephant. 'Disvā evamāha' means: having seen that great nāga—which had been adorned with elephant ornaments after its major and minor limbs were scrubbed, it was bathed, brought up, placed on the outer bank, and its limbs were made dry—they spoke this word of praise: 'Oh, how very beautiful!' 'Kāyupapanno' means endowed with bodily perfection; the meaning is having complete major and minor limbs. 'The Venerable Udāyī' is the Elder Kāḷudāyī who had attained the analytical knowledges. 'Etadavoca' means: seeing that great populace speaking of the elephant's beauty, he thought, 'This populace speaks of the beauty of an elephant born with a rootless relinking-consciousness, not of the Buddha-elephant. Now I, having made a simile with this bull elephant, will speak of the beauty of the Buddha-nāga.' And having thought thus, he spoke this utterance beginning, 'Is it only the elephant, venerable sir?' Therein, 'mahanta' means endowed with stature. 'Brahanta' means endowed with girth. 'Evamāha' means thus he speaks. Then, because this word 'nāga' applies to elephants, and also to horses, cattle, serpents, trees, and humans, the Blessed One said, 'Even an elephant…' and so on.

Āgunti [P 3.0370] pāpakaṃ lāmakaṃ akusaladhammaṃ. Tamahaṃ nāgoti brūmīti taṃ ahaṃ imehi tīhi dvārehi dasannaṃ akusalakammapathānaṃ dvādasannañca akusalacittānaṃ akaraṇato nāgoti vadāmi. Ayañhi na āguṃ karotīti iminā atthena nāgo. Imāhi gāthāhi anumodāmīti imāhi catusaṭṭhipadāhi soḷasahi gāthāhi anumodāmi abhinandāmi.

'Āgu' means an evil, wicked, unwholesome quality. 'That I call a nāga' means: I call him a nāga because of not doing the ten unwholesome courses of action and the twelve unwholesome states of consciousness through these three doors. Indeed, this one does no āgu (evil); for this reason, he is a nāga. 'I rejoice in these verses' means: I rejoice in, I delight in these sixteen verses with sixty-four lines.

Manussabhūtanti devādibhāvaṃ anupagantvā manussameva bhūtaṃ. Attadantanti attanāyeva dantaṃ, na aññehi damathaṃ upanītaṃ. Bhagavā hi attanā uppāditeneva maggadamathena cakkhutopi danto, sotatopi, ghānatopi, jivhātopi, kāyatopi, manatopīti imesu chasu ṭhānesu danto santo nibbuto parinibbuto. Tenāha – “attadanta”nti. Samāhitanti duvidhenāpi samādhinā samāhitaṃ. [V 3.0114] Iriyamānanti viharamānaṃ. Brahmapatheti seṭṭhapathe, amatapathe, nibbānapathe. Cittassūpasame ratanti paṭhamajjhānena pañca nīvaraṇāni vūpasametvā, dutiyajjhānena vitakkavicāre, tatiyajjhānena pītiṃ, catutthajjhānena sukhadukkhaṃ vūpasametvā tasmiṃ cittassūpasame rataṃ abhirataṃ.

'Manussabhūta' means having become a human being, not having attained the state of a deva or other beings. 'Attadanta' means tamed by oneself, not led to taming by others. Indeed, the Blessed One, by the taming of the path generated by himself, is tamed in these six places—through the eye, through the ear, through the nose, through the tongue, through the body, and through the mind; he is tamed, peaceful, quenched, completely quenched. Therefore, he said: 'attadanta' (self-tamed). 'Samāhita' means concentrated by both kinds of concentration. 'Iriyamāna' means abiding. 'Brahmapathe' means on the best path, the deathless path, the path to Nibbāna. 'Delighting in the stilling of the mind' means: having stilled the five hindrances with the first jhāna, thought-conception and discursive thinking with the second jhāna, zest with the third jhāna, and pleasure and pain with the fourth jhāna, he delights and greatly delights in that stilling of the mind.

Namassantīti kāyena namassanti, vācāya namassanti, manasā namassanti, dhammānudhammapaṭipattiyā namassanti, sakkaronti garuṃ karonti. Sabbadhammānapāragunti sabbesaṃ khandhāyatanadhātudhammānaṃ abhiññāpāragū, pariññāpāragū, pahānapāragū, bhāvanāpāragū, sacchikiriyāpāragū, samāpattipāragūti chabbidhena pāragamanena pāragataṃ pārappattaṃ matthakappattaṃ. Devāpi taṃ namassantīti dukkhappattā subrahmadevaputtādayo [P 3.0371] sukhappattā ca sabbeva dasasahassacakkavāḷavāsino devāpi tumhe namassanti. Iti me arahato sutanti iti mayā catūhi kāraṇehi arahāti laddhavohārānaṃ tumhākaṃyeva santike sutanti dīpeti.

'They pay homage' means: they pay homage with the body, they pay homage with speech, they pay homage with the mind, they pay homage by the practice in conformity with the Dhamma; they honor and revere. 'One who has gone to the far shore of all dhammas' means: one who has gone to the far shore of all dhammas of the aggregates, sense bases, and elements through direct knowledge, full understanding, abandoning, development, realization, and attainment. Thus, by these six kinds of going to the far shore, he has gone to the far shore, reached the far shore, reached the summit. 'Even the devas pay homage to him' means: devas who have encountered suffering, such as the devaputta Subrahma and others, and also all the devas who have encountered happiness, who dwell in the ten-thousand-world-system, pay homage to you. 'Thus have I heard from the Arahant' clarifies this meaning: 'Thus have I heard it in the very presence of you who have received the designation "Arahant" for four reasons.'

Sabbasaṃyojanātītanti [M 3.0112] sabbāni dasavidhasaṃyojanāni atikkantaṃ. Vanā nibbanamāgatanti kilesavanato nibbanaṃ kilesavanarahitaṃ nibbānaṃ āgataṃ sampattaṃ. Kāmehi nekkhammaratanti duvidhehi kāmehi nikkhantattā pabbajjā aṭṭha samāpattiyo cattāro ca ariyamaggā kāmehi nekkhammaṃ nāma, tattha rataṃ abhirataṃ. Muttaṃ selāva kañcananti seladhātuto muttaṃ kañcanasadisaṃ.

'Sabbasaṃyojanātīta' means having transcended all ten kinds of fetters. 'Vanā nibbanamāgataṃ' (Having come from the forest to the forest-free) means having come from the forest of defilements to Nibbāna, which is devoid of the forest of defilements, having reached it. 'Kāmehi nekkhammarataṃ' (Delighting in renunciation from sensual pleasures) means: because of having gone out from the two kinds of sensual pleasures, the going forth, the eight attainments, and the four noble paths are called 'renunciation from sensual pleasures'; he delights and greatly delights therein. 'Muttaṃ selāva kañcanaṃ' (Freed like gold from rock) means like pure gold released from its ore.

Sabbe accarucīti sabbasatte atikkamitvā pavattaruci. Aṭṭhamakañhi atikkamitvā pavattarucitāya sotāpanno accaruci nāma, sotāpannaṃ atikkamitvā pavattarucitāya sakadāgāmī…pe… khīṇāsavaṃ atikkamitvā pavattarucitāya paccekasambuddho, paccekasambuddhaṃ atikkamitvā pavattarucitāya sammāsambuddho accaruci nāma. Himavāvaññe siluccayeti yathā himavā pabbatarājā aññe pabbate atirocati, evaṃ atirocatīti attho. Saccanāmoti tacchanāmo bhūtanāmo āguṃ akaraṇeneva nāgoti evaṃ avitathanāmo.

'Sabbe accarucī' means one of excelling delight: having a delight that has arisen by transcending all beings. For, by reason of a delight that has arisen from transcending the eighth person, the stream-enterer is called 'one of excelling delight'. By reason of a delight that has arisen from transcending the stream-enterer, the once-returner… and so on… By reason of a delight that has arisen from transcending the Arahant, the Paccekabuddha is called 'one of excelling delight'. By reason of a delight that has arisen from transcending the Paccekabuddha, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One is called 'one of excelling delight'. 'Himavāvaññe siluccaye' (Like the Himavā surpasses other mountains) means: just as Himavā, the king of mountains, surpasses other mountains in splendor, so does he surpass in splendor. This is the meaning. 'Saccanāmo' (True in name) means: having a true name, a real name. Because he does no evil (`āgu`), he is called a Nāga. Thus, his name is unerring.

Soraccanti sucisīlaṃ. Avihiṃsāti karuṇā ca karuṇāpubbabhāgo ca. Pādā nāgassa te duveti te buddhanāgassa duve purimapādā.

'Soracca' (gentleness) means pure virtue. 'Avihiṃsā' (non-harming) means both the jhāna of compassion and the access concentration which is the preliminary part of compassion. 'Pādā nāgassa te duve' (These two are the feet of the Nāga) means: these two are the front feet of the Buddha-Nāga.

Tapoti [V 3.0115][P 3.0372] dhutasamādānaṃ. Brahmacariyanti ariyamaggasīlaṃ. Caraṇā nāgassa tyāpareti te buddhanāgassa apare dve pacchimapādā. Saddhāhatthoti saddhāmayāya soṇḍāya samannāgato. Upekkhāsetadantavāti chaḷaṅgupekkhāmayehi setadantehi samannāgato.

'Tapo' (austerity) means the undertaking of ascetic practices. 'Brahmacariya' (the holy life) means the virtue of the Noble Path. 'Caraṇā nāgassa tyāpare' (The other feet of the Nāga) means these are the other two hind feet of the Buddha-Nāga. 'Saddhāhattho' (Having faith as a trunk) means endowed with a trunk made of faith. 'Upekkhāsetadantavā' (Having white tusks of equanimity) means endowed with white tusks consisting of the six-factored equanimity.

Sati gīvāti yathā nāgassa aṅgapaccaṅgasmiṃ sirājālānaṃ gīvā patiṭṭhā, evaṃ buddhanāgassa soraccādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ sati. Tena vuttaṃ – “sati gīvā”ti. Siro paññāti yathā hatthināgassa siro uttamaṅgo, evaṃ buddhanāgassa sabbaññutañāṇaṃ. Tena hi so sabbadhamme jānāti. Tena vuttaṃ – “siro paññā”ti. Vīmaṃsā dhammacintanāti yathā hatthināgassa aggasoṇḍo vīmaṃsā nāma hoti. So tāya thaddhamudukaṃ khāditabbākhāditabbañca vīmaṃsati, tato pahātabbaṃ pajahati, ādātabbaṃ ādiyati, evameva buddhanāgassa dhammakoṭṭhāsaparicchedakañāṇasaṅkhātā dhammacintanā vīmaṃsā. Tena hi ñāṇena so bhabbābhabbe jānāti. Tena vuttaṃ – “vīmaṃsā dhammacintanā”ti[M 3.0113]. Dhammakucchisamātapoti dhammo vuccati catutthajjhānasamādhi, kucchiyeva samātapo kucchisamātapo. Samātapo nāma samātapanaṭṭhānaṃ. Dhammo kucchisamātapo assāti dhammakucchisamātapo. Catutthajjhānasamādhismiṃ ṭhitassa hi te te iddhividhādidhammā ijjhanti, tasmā so kucchisamātapoti vutto. Vivekoti [P 3.0373] kāyacittaupadhiviveko. Yathā nāgassa vāladhi makkhikā vāreti, evaṃ tathāgatassa viveko gahaṭṭhapabbajite vāreti. Tasmā so vāladhīti vutto.

Mindfulness is the neck: just as the neck is the support for the network of the major and minor limbs of a nāga, so too is mindfulness the support for the qualities of pure virtue and so on of the Buddha-Nāga. Therefore, it is said: 'Mindfulness is the neck.' Wisdom is the head: just as the head is the foremost limb of the elephant-nāga, so too is the Buddha-Nāga’s omniscience-knowledge the foremost limb. Indeed, by that knowledge he knows all dhammas. Therefore, it is said: 'Wisdom is the head.' Investigation is reflection on the Dhamma: just as an elephant-nāga investigates with the tip of its trunk what is hard and soft, what should be eaten and not eaten, and then rejects what should be rejected and takes up what should be taken up; even so, for the Buddha-Nāga, investigation is the reflection on the Dhamma, which is described as the knowledge that distinguishes the categories of the Dhamma. Indeed, by that knowledge he knows what is suitable and unsuitable. Therefore, it is said: 'Investigation is reflection on the Dhamma.' The Dhamma-belly which is the foundation of practice: 'Dhamma' refers to the concentration of the fourth jhāna; the belly itself is the foundation of practice, hence 'the belly which is the foundation of practice.' 'Samātapa' means the place of practice. He has the Dhamma which is the belly that is the foundation of practice, thus he is called 'Dhammakucchisamātapo'. Indeed, for one established in the concentration of the fourth jhāna, those various qualities such as the kinds of psychic power are accomplished. Therefore, it is called 'the belly which is the foundation of practice'. Seclusion is the tail: this is seclusion of body, seclusion of mind, and seclusion from the substrata of existence. Just as the nāga’s tail wards off flies, so too does the Tathāgata’s seclusion ward off householders and monastics. Therefore, it is called the tail.

Jhāyīti duvidhena jhānena jhāyī. Assāsaratoti nāgassa hi assāsapassāsā viya buddhanāgassa phalasamāpatti, tattha rato, assāsapassāsehi viya tāya vinā na vattatīti attho. Sabbattha saṃvutoti sabbadvāresu saṃvuto. Anavajjānīti sammāājīvena uppannabhojanāni. Sāvajjānīti pañcavidhamicchājīvavasena uppannabhojanāni.

One who enters jhāna: one who is accustomed to entering jhāna by means of the two kinds of jhāna. 'Delighting in the in-breath': just as a nāga has in-breaths and out-breaths, so the Buddha-Nāga has the attainment of fruition, and in that he delights. The meaning is that just as one cannot exist without in-breaths and out-breaths, so he does not exist without that attainment of fruition. 'Restrained in all respects' means: restrained in all doors. 'Blameless' refers to foods that have arisen through right livelihood. 'Blameworthy' refers to foods that have arisen by means of the five kinds of wrong livelihood.

Aṇuṃthūlanti khuddakañca mahantañca. Sabbaṃ chetvāna bandhananti sabbaṃ dasavidhampi saṃyojanaṃ chinditvāna. Nupalippati lokenāti lokena saddhiṃ taṇhāmānadiṭṭhilepehi na lippati. Mahāginīti mahāaggi. Viññūhi desitāti idha paṭisambhidāppatto kāḷudāyittherova viññū paṇḍito, tena desitāti attho. Viññassanti mahānāgā, nāgaṃ nāgena desitanti udāyittheranāgena desitaṃ buddhanāgaṃ itare khīṇāsavā nāgā vijānissanti.

'Subtle and gross' means small and great. 'Having cut all bonds' means having severed all ten kinds of fetters. 'He is not smeared by the world' means he is not smeared by the smears of craving, conceit, and views, together with the world. 'A great fire' means a great fire. 'Taught by the wise': here, the Elder Kāḷudāyi, who attained the analytical knowledges, is indeed the wise, learned one; it was taught by him—this is the meaning. 'The great Nāgas will understand, the Nāga taught by a Nāga' means: the other Arahant-nāgas will understand the Buddha-Nāga who was taught by the Elder Udāyi-nāga.

Sarīraṃ [V 3.0116] vijahaṃ nāgo, parinibbissatīti bodhipallaṅke kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto, yamakasālantare anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyissati. Evaṃ paṭisambhidāppatto udāyitthero soḷasahi gāthāhi catusaṭṭhiyā padehi dasabalassa vaṇṇaṃ kathento desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi[P 3.0374]. Bhagavā anumodi. Desanāvasāne caturāsītipāṇasahassāni amatapānaṃ piviṃsūti.

'The Nāga, shedding his body, will attain final Nibbāna' means: having been fully extinguished on the seat of enlightenment through the parinibbāna of the defilements, he will attain parinibbāna between the twin sāla trees with the nibbāna-element without residue remaining. Thus, the Elder Udāyi, having attained the analytical knowledges, concluded his discourse, speaking the praise of the Ten-Powered One with sixteen verses. The Blessed One rejoiced. At the end of the discourse, eighty-four thousand beings drank the drink of the deathless.

2. Migasālāsuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Migasālā Sutta

44. Dutiye kathaṃ kathaṃ nāmāti kena kena kāraṇena. Aññeyyoti ājānitabbo. Yatra hi nāmāti yasmiṃ nāma dhamme. Samasamagatikāti [M 3.0114] samabhāveneva samagatikā. Bhavissantīti jātā. Sakadāgāmipatto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapannoti sakadāgāmipuggalo hutvā tusitabhavaneyeva nibbatto. Kathaṃ kathaṃ nāmāti kena kena nu kho kāraṇena, kiṃ nu kho jānitvā desito, udāhu ajānitvāti. Thero kāraṇaṃ ajānanto evaṃ kho panetaṃ bhagini bhagavatā byākatanti āha.

44. In the second sutta, ‘how, how indeed?’ means by what, by what reason. ‘Should be understood’ means should be known. ‘Where indeed’ means in what phenomenon. ‘Of the same destiny’ means having an equal destiny. ‘Will be’ means born. ‘A once-returner attained, reborn in the Tusita realm’ means, having become a once-returner individual, he was reborn in the Tusita plane itself. ‘How, how indeed?’ means by what reason, by what reason? Was it taught having known, or was it taught without knowing? The elder, not knowing the reason, said, “But, sister, it was declared by the Blessed One thus.”

Ammakā ammakapaññāti itthī hutvā itthisaññāya eva samannāgatā. Ke ca purisapuggalaparopariyañāṇeti ettha purisapuggalaparopariyañāṇaṃ vuccati purisapuggalānaṃ tikkhamuduvasena indriyaparopariyañāṇaṃ. Tasmā kā ca bālā migasālā, ke ca purisapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyañāṇe appaṭihatavisayā sammāsambuddhā, ubhayametaṃ dūre suvidūreti ayamettha saṅkhepo.

‘Ammakā, with a woman's perception’ means, being a woman, she is endowed only with a woman's perception. In this passage, ‘And what is the knowledge of the faculties of other individuals,’ the knowledge of the faculties of other individuals is said to be the knowledge of the faculties of individuals with regard to their sharpness or dullness. Therefore, what sort of person is the foolish Migasālā, and what sort of persons are the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, whose domain is unobstructed regarding the knowledge of the faculties of other individuals? Both of these are far, very far apart. This is the summary here.

Idāni migasālāya attano dūrabhāvaṃ dassento chayime, ānandātiādimāha. Sorato hotīti pāpato suṭṭhu orato virato hoti. Suratotipi pāṭho. Abhinandanti sabrahmacārī ekattavāsenāti tena saddhiṃ ekatovāsena [P 3.0375] sabrahmacārī abhinandanti tussanti. Ekantavāsenātipi pāṭho, satatavāsenāti attho. Savanenapi akataṃ hotīti sotabbayuttakaṃ asutaṃ hoti. Bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hotīti ettha bāhusaccaṃ vuccati vīriyaṃ, vīriyena kattabbayuttakaṃ akataṃ hotīti attho. Diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hotīti diṭṭhiyā paṭivijjhitabbaṃ appaṭividdhaṃ [V 3.0117] hoti. Sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ na labhatīti kālānukālaṃ dhammassavanaṃ nissāya pītipāmojjaṃ na labhati. Hānagāmīyeva hotīti parihānimeva gacchati.

Now, showing his own distance with respect to Migasālā, he says, ‘These six, Ānanda,’ and so on. ‘He is well-restrained’ means from evil he is well and thoroughly restrained. There is also a reading ‘surato.’ ‘Fellow practitioners delight in living together’ means fellow practitioners delight and rejoice in living together with him. There is also a reading ‘ekantavāsenā,’ the meaning of which is ‘by constant living.’ ‘Not done even by hearing’ means what ought to be heard is not heard. ‘Not done even by great learning’: here 'great learning' refers to energy; the meaning is that what ought to be done with energy is not done. ‘Not penetrated even by view’ means what should be penetrated by wisdom is not penetrated. ‘Does not attain even temporary liberation’ means he does not obtain joy and gladness by relying on hearing the Dhamma from time to time. ‘He is one who goes to decline’ means he goes only to decline.

Pamāṇikāti puggalesu pamāṇaggāhakā. Paminantīti pametuṃ tuletuṃ ārabhanti. Eko hīnoti eko guṇehi hīno. Eko paṇītoti eko guṇehi paṇīto. Taṃ hīti taṃ pamāṇakaraṇaṃ.

‘Those who measure’ means those who take the measure of individuals. ‘They measure’ means they strive to compare and weigh. ‘One is inferior’ means one is inferior in qualities. ‘One is superior’ means one is superior in qualities. ‘That’ means that act of measuring.

Abhikkantataroti sundarataro. Paṇītataroti uttamataro. Dhammasoto nibbahatīti sūraṃ hutvā pavattamānavipassanāñāṇaṃ nibbahati, ariyabhūmiṃ [M 3.0115] sampāpeti. Tadantaraṃ ko jāneyyāti taṃ antaraṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ aññatra tathāgatena ko jāneyyāti attho.

‘More surpassing’ means more beautiful. ‘More refined’ means more supreme. ‘The Dhamma-stream carries forth’ means insight knowledge that has arisen powerfully carries forth, bringing one to the noble plane. ‘Who would know that difference?’—the meaning is, who other than the Tathāgata would know that difference, that cause?

Kodhamānoti kodho ca māno ca. Lobhadhammāti lobhoyeva. Vacīsaṅkhārāti ālāpasallāpavasena vacanāneva. Yo vā panassa mādisoti yo vā pana aññopi mayā sadiso sammāsambuddhoyeva [P 3.0376] assa, so puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyāti attho. Khaññatīti guṇakhaṇanaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ime kho, ānanda, cha puggalāti dve soratā, dve adhigatakodhamānalobhadhammā, dve adhigatakodhamānavacīsaṅkhārāti ime cha puggalā. Gatinti ñāṇagatiṃ. Ekaṅgahīnāti ekekena guṇaṅgena hīnā. Pūraṇo sīlena visesī ahosi, isidatto paññāya. Pūraṇassa sīlaṃ isidattassa paññāṭhāne ṭhitaṃ, isidattassa paññā pūraṇassa sīlaṭṭhāne ṭhitāti.

‘Anger and conceit’ means anger and conceit. ‘Greedy nature’ means greed itself. ‘Verbal formations’ means words themselves, by way of conversation and discussion. ‘Or one like me’ means: or another who is like me, a Perfectly Enlightened One, could take the measure of individuals. ‘Is undermined’ means he comes to the undermining of his qualities. ‘These six individuals, Ānanda’ means these six individuals: two who are well-restrained, two who are not free from anger, conceit, and greed, and two who are not free from anger, conceit, and verbal formations. ‘Destiny’ means the course of knowledge. ‘Deficient in one aspect’ means deficient in one or another aspect of a quality. Pūraṇa was distinguished by virtue, Isidatta by wisdom. Pūraṇa’s virtue stood in the place of Isidatta’s wisdom, and Isidatta’s wisdom stood in the place of Pūraṇa’s virtue.

3. Iṇasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Iṇasutta

45. Tatiye dāliddiyanti daliddabhāvo. Kāmabhoginoti kāme bhuñjanakasattassa. Assakoti attano santakena rahito. Anāḷhikoti na aḍḍho. Iṇaṃ ādiyatīti jīvituṃ asakkonto iṇaṃ ādiyati. Vaḍḍhiṃ paṭissuṇātīti dātuṃ asakkonto vaḍḍhiṃ dassāmīti paṭijānāti. Anucarantipi nanti parisamajjhagaṇamajjhādīsu ātapaṭhapanapaṃsuokiraṇādīhi vippakāraṃ pāpento pacchato pacchato anubandhanti. Saddhā natthīti okappanakasaddhāmattakampi natthi. Hirī natthīti hirīyanākāramattakampi natthi. Ottappaṃ [P 3.0377] natthīti bhāyanākāramattakampi natthi. Vīriyaṃ natthīti kāyikavīriyamattakampi natthi. Paññā natthīti kammassakatapaññāmattakampi [V 3.0118] natthi. Iṇādānasmiṃ vadāmīti iṇaggahaṇaṃ vadāmi. Mā maṃ jaññūti mā maṃ jānātu.

45. In the third sutta, ‘poverty’ means the state of being poor. ‘One who indulges in sensual pleasures’ refers to a being who enjoys sensual objects. ‘Without property’ means devoid of one’s own possessions. ‘Destitute’ means not wealthy. ‘Takes on debt’ means being unable to make a living, he takes on debt. ‘Agrees to interest’ means being unable to pay, he promises, “I will give interest.” ‘They follow and harass him’ means they follow him from behind, causing him distress in places like the midst of an assembly by making him stand in the sun, throwing dust, and so on. ‘No faith’ means not even a mere conviction based on settled trust exists. ‘No shame’ means not even a mere semblance of shame exists. ‘No fear of wrongdoing’ means not even a mere semblance of fear exists. ‘No energy’ means not even a mere physical energy exists. ‘No wisdom’ means not even the mere wisdom of the ownership of kamma exists. ‘I speak of taking on debt’ means I speak of taking on debt. ‘Let them not know me’ means let them not know me.

Dāliddiyaṃ dukkhanti dhanadaliddabhāvo dukkhaṃ. Kāmalābhābhijappinanti kāmalābhaṃ patthentānaṃ. Pāpakammavinibbayoti pāpakammavaḍḍhako. Saṃsappatīti paripphandati. Jānanti jānanto. Yassa vippaṭisārajāti ye assa [M 3.0116] vippaṭisārato jātā. Yonimaññataranti ekaṃ tiracchānayoniṃ. Dadaṃ cittaṃ pasādayanti cittaṃ pasādento dadamāno.

‘Poverty is suffering’ means the state of being poor in wealth is suffering. ‘For one who craves sensual gains’ means for those who long for the gain of sensual objects. ‘A producer of evil kamma’ means an increaser of evil kamma. ‘He struggles’ means he writhes. ‘Knowing’ means knowing. ‘From which remorse is born’ means those things which are born from his remorse. ‘One or another womb’ means one animal womb. ‘Giving while gladdening the mind’ means giving while gladdening the mind.

Kaṭaggāhoti jayaggāho, anaparādhaggāho hoti. Gharamesinoti gharāvāsaṃ pariyesantassa vasamānassa vā. Cāgo puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatīti cāgoti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhati. Cāgā puññanti vā pāṭho. Patiṭṭhitāti patiṭṭhitasaddhā nāma sotāpannassa saddhā. Hirimanoti hirisampayuttacitto. Nirāmisaṃ sukhanti tīṇi jhānāni nissāya uppajjanakasukhaṃ. Upekkhanti catutthajjhānupekkhaṃ. Āraddhavīriyoti paripuṇṇapaggahitavīriyo. Jhānāni [P 3.0378] upasampajjāti cattāri jhānāni patvā. Ekodi nipako satoti ekaggacitto kammassakatañāṇasatīhi ca samannāgato.

‘The taking of the prize’ means the taking of victory, the state of being without fault. ‘For one seeking a home’ means for one who seeks the household life or who is living in it. ‘Generosity increases merit’ means the merit that is reckoned as generosity increases. Or, there is the reading ‘merit from generosity.’ ‘Established’ means established faith, which is the faith of a stream-enterer. ‘Having shame’ means having a mind associated with shame. ‘Unworldly happiness’ means the happiness that arises depending on the three jhānas. ‘Equanimity’ means the equanimity of the fourth jhāna. ‘With energy aroused’ means one whose energy is fully and well exerted. ‘Having attained the jhānas’ means having reached the four jhānas. ‘Unified, prudent, and mindful’ means having a unified mind and being endowed with wisdom and mindfulness.

Evaṃ ñatvā yathābhūtanti evaṃ ettakaṃ kāraṇaṃ yathāsabhāvaṃ jānitvā. Sabbasaṃyojanakkhayeti nibbāne. Sabbasoti sabbākārena. Anupādāyāti aggahetvā. Sammā cittaṃ vimuccatīti idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – sabbasaṃyojanakkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne sabbaso anupādiyitvā sammā hetunā nayena maggacittaṃ vimuccati. “Etaṃ ñatvā yathābhūtaṃ, sabbasaṃyojanakkhaya”ntipi pāḷiyaṃ likhitaṃ, tassa etaṃ sabbasaṃyojanakkhayasaṅkhātaṃ nibbānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñatvāti attho. Purimapacchimehi pana saddhiṃ na ghaṭīyati.

‘Thus having known as it really is’ means having known this much of a cause thus, in accordance with its true nature. ‘In the destruction of all fetters’ means in Nibbāna. ‘In every way’ means in all aspects. ‘Without grasping’ means not taking up any object by way of craving and views. ‘The mind is rightly liberated’ means this is what is said: in Nibbāna, which is designated as the destruction of all fetters, by not grasping in any way, the path-mind is rightly liberated by the appropriate cause and method. It is also written in the Pāḷi as, “Having known this as it really is, the destruction of all fetters.” The meaning of this is: “having known as it really is this Nibbāna, which is designated as the destruction of all fetters.” However, it does not connect with what comes before and after.

Tassa sammā vimuttassāti tassa sammā vimuttassa khīṇāsavassa. Ñāṇaṃ hotīti paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ hoti. Tādinoti taṃsaṇṭhitassa. Akuppāti akuppārammaṇattā kuppakāraṇānaṃ kilesānañca abhāvena akuppā. Vimuttīti maggavimuttipi phalavimuttipi. Bhavasaṃyojanakkhayeti bhavasaṃyojanakkhayasaṅkhāte nibbāne bhavasaṃyojanānañca khayante uppannā. Etaṃ kho paramaṃ ñāṇanti etaṃ maggaphalañāṇaṃ paramañāṇaṃ nāma. Sukhamanuttaranti etadeva maggaphalasukhaṃ anuttaraṃ [V 3.0119] sukhaṃ nāma. Āṇaṇyamuttamanti sabbesaṃ aṇaṇānaṃ khīṇāsavo uttamaaṇaṇo[P 3.0379], tasmā arahattaphalaṃ āṇaṇyamuttamanti arahattaphalena desanāya kūṭaṃ gaṇhi. Imasmiñca sutte vaṭṭameva kathetvā gāthāsu vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitanti.

‘Of one who is rightly liberated’ means of that one rightly liberated, the one whose taints are destroyed. ‘There is knowledge’ means there is the reviewing knowledge. ‘Of such a one’ means of one who is stable in that state. ‘Unshakable’ means it is unshakable because its object is unshakable and because of the absence of the defilements that cause shaking. ‘Liberation’ means both the liberation of the path and the liberation of the fruit. ‘In the destruction of the fetters of existence’ means in Nibbāna, which is designated as the destruction of the fetters of existence; or, it refers to what has arisen at the end of the destruction of the fetters of existence. ‘This indeed is the supreme knowledge’ means this knowledge of the path and fruit is called the supreme knowledge. ‘The unsurpassed bliss’ means this very bliss of the path and fruit is called the unsurpassed bliss. ‘The supreme freedom from debt’ means that among all those free from debt, the one whose taints are destroyed is the supreme one free from the debt of defilements; therefore, the fruit of Arahantship is the supreme freedom from debt. Thus, with the fruit of Arahantship, he brings the teaching to its climax. And in this sutta, in the prose, only the round of existence was taught, but in the verses, both the round and what is free from the round were taught. Thus ends the third sutta.

4. Mahācundasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Mahācunda Sutta

46. Catutthe [M 3.0117] cetīsūti cetiraṭṭhe. Sayaṃjātiyanti evaṃnāmake nigame. Mahācundoti dhammasenāpatissa kaniṭṭhabhātiko. Dhamme yogo anuyogo etesanti dhammayogā. Dhammakathikānaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ. Jhāyantīti jhāyī. Apasādentīti ghaṭṭenti hiṃsanti. Jhāyantīti cintenti. Pajjhāyantītiādīni upasaggavasena vaḍḍhitāni. Kimime jhāyantīti kiṃ nāma ime jhāyanti. Kintime jhāyantīti kimatthaṃ ime jhāyanti. Kathaṃ ime jhāyantīti kena kāraṇena ime jhāyanti. Amataṃ dhātuṃ kāyena phusitvā viharantīti maraṇavirahitaṃ nibbānadhātuṃ sandhāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā viharantā anukkamena taṃ nāmakāyena phusitvā viharanti. Gambhīraṃ atthapadanti guḷhaṃ paṭicchannaṃ khandhadhātuāyatanādiatthaṃ. Paññāya [P 3.0380] ativijjha passantīti sahavipassanāya maggapaññāya paṭivijjhitvā passanti. Imasmiṃ panatthe sammasanapaṭivedhapaññāpi uggahaparipucchāpaññāpi vaṭṭatiyevāti.

46. In the fourth, cetīsu means in the Cetī country. Sayaṃjātiyaṃ means in the town of that name. Mahācundo is the younger brother of the General of the Dhamma. Because for them there is the Dhamma which is repeatedly practiced, they are called dhammayogā; this is a name for Dhamma-preachers. They contemplate, therefore they are jhāyī (meditators). Apasādenti means they strike, they harm. Jhāyanti means they contemplate. Pajjhāyanti and so on are intensified by means of a prefix. Kimime jhāyanti means: what is it that these contemplate? Kintime jhāyanti means: for what purpose do these contemplate? Kathaṃ ime jhāyanti means: for what reason do these contemplate? Amataṃ dhātuṃ kāyena phusitvā viharanti means: referring to the Nibbāna-element which is free from death, those dwelling having taken up a meditation subject, gradually contact it with the body of name and dwell. Gambhīraṃ atthapadaṃ means a profound matter of meaning: a hidden, concealed meaning concerning the aggregates, elements, sense bases, and so on. Paññāya ativijjha passanti means: they see by penetrating with the wisdom of the path together with insight. In this context, however, the wisdom of comprehension and penetration, and also the wisdom of learning and questioning, are indeed applicable.

5-6. Sandiṭṭhikasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

5-6. Commentary on the Two Sandiṭṭhika Suttas

47-48. Pañcame santaṃ vā ajjhattanti niyakajjhatte vijjamānaṃ. Lobhotiādīhi tīṇi akusalamūlāni dassitāni. Lobhadhammātiādīhi taṃsampayuttakā dhammā. Chaṭṭhe kāyasandosanti kāyadvārassa dussanākāraṃ. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Imesu dvīsu suttesu paccavekkhaṇāva kathitā.

In the fifth, santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ means existing in one's own interior. By lobho, and so on, the three unwholesome roots are shown. By lobhadhammā, and so on, are shown the states associated with them. In the sixth, kāyasandosaṃ means the manner of corrupting the body-door. In the remaining two as well, this is the method. In these two suttas, only reflection is taught.

7. Khemasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Khema Sutta

49. Sattame vusitavāti vutthabrahmacariyavāso. Katakaraṇīyoti catūhi maggehi kattabbaṃ katvā ṭhito. Ohitabhāroti khandhabhāraṃ kilesabhāraṃ abhisaṅkhārabhārañca otāretvā ṭhito. Anuppattasadatthoti [V 3.0120] sadattho vuccati arahattaṃ, taṃ pattoti attho. Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanoti khīṇabhavabandhano. Sammadaññā vimuttoti sammā hetunā kāraṇena jānitvā vimutto.
