The state of existence of one who is reborn in the lower realms due to the perfection of bad conduct is called a 'non-meritorious portion'. 'This, monks, is called the result of sensual pleasures' (ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, kāmānaṃ vipāko) means: because this twofold state of existence also arises dependent on the aspiration for sensual pleasures, it is called the result of sensual pleasures. 'He... this penetrative [teaching]' (so imaṃ nibbedhikaṃ) means: that monk knows this superior practice which is penetrative in the thirty-six instances. 'The cessation of sensual pleasure' (kāmanirodhaṃ) means: the noble path, which has obtained the name 'kāmanirodha' because of the cessation of sensual pleasure. Indeed, in this instance, the noble path itself, designated as the holy life, is called 'the cessation of sensual pleasure'.

Sāmisāti kilesāmisasampayuttā. Iminā nayena sabbaṭhānesu attho veditabbo. Apicettha vohāravepakkanti vohāravipākaṃ. Kathāsaṅkhāto hi vohāro saññāya vipāko nāma. Yathā [P 3.0408] yathā nanti ettha naṃ-iti nipātamattameva. Iti yasmā yathā yathā sañjānāti, tathā [M 3.0136] tathā evaṃsaññī ahosinti katheti, tasmā vohāravepakkāti attho.

'With bait' (sāmisā) means conjoined with the bait of defilements. By this method, the meaning should be understood in all instances. Moreover, here, 'result of expression' (vohāravepakkaṃ) means the result of expression. Indeed, expression, designated as speech, is the result of perception. Here, in 'yathā yathā naṃ', 'naṃ' is merely a particle. Thus, because as one perceives, so one says, 'He was one who perceived in this way,' therefore, the meaning is 'the result of expression'.

Avijjāti aṭṭhasu ṭhānesu aññāṇabhūtā bahalaavijjā. Nirayaṃ gamentīti nirayagamanīyā, niraye nibbattipaccayāti attho. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Cetanāhanti cetanaṃ ahaṃ. Idha sabbasaṅgāhikā saṃvidahanacetanā gahitā. Cetayitvāti dvārappavattacetanā. Manasāti cetanāsampayuttacittena. Nirayavedanīyanti niraye vipākadāyakaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Adhimattanti balavadukkhaṃ. Dandhavirāgīti garukaṃ na khippaṃ saṇikaṃ vigacchanakadukkhaṃ. Urattāḷiṃ kandatīti uraṃ tāḷetvā rodati. Pariyeṭṭhinti pariyesanaṃ. Ekapadaṃ dvipadanti ekapadamantaṃ vā dvipadamantaṃ vā, ko mantaṃ jānātīti attho. Sammohavepakkanti sammohavipākaṃ. Dukkhassa hi sammoho nissandavipāko nāma. Dutiyapadepi eseva nayo. Pariyesanāpi hi tassa nissandavipākoti. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ.

'Ignorance' (avijjā) is dense ignorance, the state of not knowing in eight instances. They are called 'leading to hell' (nirayagamanīyā) because they cause one to go to hell; the meaning is that they are a condition for arising in hell. The same method applies to the remaining terms. 'Volition, I say' (cetanāhaṃ) means 'I declare volition'. Here, all-encompassing volition, the volition that arranges, is intended. 'Having willed' (cetayitvā) refers to volition that proceeds at the [sense] doors. 'With the mind' (manasā) means with the mind associated with volition. 'To be experienced in hell' (nirayavedanīyaṃ) means that which gives its result in hell. The same method applies to the remaining terms. 'Intense' (adhimattaṃ) means strong suffering. 'Slow to fade' (dandhavirāgī) means heavy suffering that does not cease quickly, but slowly. 'Beating the breast and wailing' (urattāḷiṃ kandati) means striking the breast and weeping. 'Searching' (pariyeṭṭhiṃ) means seeking. 'One line or two' (ekapadaṃ dvipadaṃ) means a mantra of one line or a mantra of two lines; the meaning is that the person afflicted by suffering does not know that mantra. 'Resulting in delusion' (sammohavepakkaṃ) means the result which is delusion. For delusion is called the resultant-effect of suffering. The same method applies to the second term. For searching, too, is its resultant-effect. In this discourse, the round and what is free from the round are spoken of.

10. Sīhanādasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Sīhanāda Sutta

64. Dasame āsabhaṃ ṭhānanti seṭṭhaṃ niccalaṭṭhānaṃ. Sīhanādanti [P 3.0409] abhītanādaṃ pamukhanādaṃ. Brahmacakkanti seṭṭhañāṇacakkaṃ paṭivedhañāṇañceva desanāñāṇañca. Ṭhānañca ṭhānatoti kāraṇañca kāraṇato. Yampīti yena ñāṇena. Idampi tathāgatassāti idampi ṭhānāṭṭhānañāṇaṃ tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ sabbapadesu attho veditabbo. Kammasamādānānanti samādiyitvā katānaṃ kusalākusalakammānaṃ, kammameva vā kammasamādānaṃ. Ṭhānaso hetusoti paccayato ceva hetuto [V 3.0138] ca. Tattha gatiupadhikālapayogā vipākassa ṭhānaṃ, kammaṃ hetu. Jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnanti catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ vimokkhānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ samādhīnaṃ navannaṃ anupubbasamāpattīnañca. Saṃkilesanti hānabhāgiyaṃ dhammaṃ. Vodānanti visesabhāgiyaṃ dhammaṃ. Vuṭṭhānanti “vodānampi vuṭṭhānaṃ, tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhānampi vuṭṭhāna”nti (vibha. 828) evaṃ vuttaṃ paguṇajjhānañceva bhavaṅganaphalasamāpattiyo ca. Heṭṭhimaṃ heṭṭhimañhi paguṇajjhānaṃ uparimassa uparimassa padaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, tasmā “vodānampi vuṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Bhavaṅgena pana [M 3.0137] sabbajjhānehi vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, phalasamāpattiyā nirodhasamāpattito vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Taṃ sandhāya “tamhā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhānampi vuṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ. Anekavihitantiādīni visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.402) vaṇṇitāni. Āsavakkhayañāṇaṃ heṭṭhā vuttatthameva. Purimassāpi ñāṇattayassa vitthārakathaṃ icchantena majjhimaṭṭhakathāya mahāsīhanādavaṇṇanā (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.146 ādayo) oloketabbā. Samāhitassāti [P 3.0410] ekaggacittassa. Samādhi maggoti samādhi etesaṃ ñāṇānaṃ adhigamāya upāyo. Asamādhīti anekaggabhāvo. Kummaggoti micchāmaggo. Imasmiṃ sutte tathāgatassa ñāṇabalaṃ kathitanti.

64. In the tenth sutta, 'the foremost position' (āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ) means the supreme, unshakeable position. 'Lion's roar' (sīhanādaṃ) means a fearless roar, a foremost roar. 'Brahma-wheel' (brahmacakkaṃ) means the supreme wheel of knowledge, which is both the knowledge of penetration and the knowledge of teaching. 'A possibility as a possibility' (ṭhānañca ṭhānato) means a cause as a cause. 'By which' (yampi) means by which knowledge. 'This too belongs to the Tathāgata' (idampi tathāgatassāti) means this knowledge of the possible and the impossible is a power of the Tathāgata. Thus, the meaning should be understood in all terms. 'Of the undertaking of kamma' (kammasamādānānaṃ) means: of wholesome and unwholesome kamma that has been done having been undertaken; or, kamma itself is the undertaking of kamma. 'By way of condition, by way of cause' (ṭhānaso hetuso) means by way of condition and by way of root-cause. Therein, destination, substratum, time, and endeavor are the 'condition' for the result; kamma is the 'root-cause'. 'Of jhānas, liberations, concentrations, and attainments' (jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ) means of the four jhānas, eight liberations, three concentrations, and nine successive attainments. 'Defilement' (saṃkilesaṃ) means a state partaking of decline. 'Purification' (vodānaṃ) means a state partaking of distinction. 'Emergence' (vuṭṭhānaṃ): "Purification is also emergence, and emergence from that particular concentration is also emergence"—thus it is said of both proficient jhāna and the attainments of bhavaṅga and fruition. Indeed, a lower proficient jhāna is the proximate cause for a higher one; therefore it is said, "purification is also emergence". Furthermore, emergence from all jhānas occurs through bhavaṅga; emergence from the attainment of cessation occurs through the attainment of fruition. With reference to that, it is said, "emergence from that particular concentration is also emergence". 'Various kinds', etc., are explained in the Visuddhimagga. The knowledge of the destruction of the taints has the meaning already stated. One who desires a detailed account of the previous three knowledges should look in the commentary on the Mahāsīhanāda Sutta in the Majjhima Nikāya Commentary. 'Of one who is concentrated' (samāhitassa) means of one with a one-pointed mind. 'Concentration is the path' (samādhi maggo) means concentration is the means for the attainment of these knowledges. 'Lack of concentration' (asamādhi) means the state of not being one-pointed. 'A wrong path' (kumaggo) means a false path. In this sutta, the Tathāgata's power of knowledge is taught.

Mahāvaggo chaṭṭho.

The Great Chapter, the Sixth.

7. Devatāvaggo

7. The Chapter on Deities

1-3. Anāgāmiphalasuttādivaṇṇanā

1-3. Commentary on the Anāgāmiphala Sutta, etc.

65-67. Sattamassa paṭhame assaddhiyanti assaddhabhāvaṃ. Duppaññatanti nippaññabhāvaṃ. Dutiye pamādanti sativippavāsaṃ. Tatiye ābhisamācārikanti uttamasamācārabhūtaṃ vattavasena paṇṇattisīlaṃ. Sekhadhammanti sekhapaṇṇattisīlaṃ. Sīlānīti cattāri mahāsīlāni.

In the first sutta of the seventh chapter, 'lack of faith' (assaddhiyaṃ) means the state of faithlessness. 'Lack of wisdom' (duppaññataṃ) means the state of lacking wisdom. In the second, 'heedlessness' (pamādaṃ) means the absence of mindfulness. In the third, 'conduct according to discipline' (ābhisamācārikaṃ) refers to the virtue laid down by way of the code of conduct, which is the noble practice. 'Qualities of a trainee' (sekhadhammaṃ) means the virtue laid down for trainees. 'Virtues' (sīlāni) refers to the four great virtues.

4. Saṅgaṇikārāmasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Saṅgaṇikārāma Sutta

68. Catutthe [V 3.0139] saṅgaṇikārāmoti gaṇasaṅgaṇikārāmo. Suttantikagaṇādīsu pana gaṇesu attano vā parisāsaṅkhāte gaṇe ramatīti gaṇārāmo. Paviveketi kāyaviveke. Cittassa nimittanti samādhivipassanācittassa nimittaṃ samādhivipassanākāraṃ. Sammādiṭṭhinti vipassanāsammādiṭṭhiṃ. Samādhinti maggasamādhiñceva phalasamādhiñca. Saṃyojanānīti dasa saṃyojanāni. Nibbānanti apaccayaparinibbānaṃ.

68. In the fourth sutta, 'one who delights in company' (saṅgaṇikārāmo) means one who delights in company and association. However, among groups such as those devoted to the suttas, etc., 'one who delights in a group' (gaṇārāmo) means one who delights in one's own group or in a group designated as an assembly. 'In seclusion' (paviveke) means in bodily seclusion. 'The mind's sign' (cittassa nimittaṃ) means the cause for the mind of concentration and insight, the mode of concentration and insight. 'Right view' (sammādiṭṭhiṃ) means the right view that is insight. 'Concentration' (samādhiṃ) means both path concentration and fruition concentration. 'Fetters' (saṃyojanāni) means the ten fetters. 'Nibbāna' (nibbānaṃ) means Nibbāna without conditions.

5. Devatāsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Devatā Sutta

69. Pañcame sovacassatāti subbacabhāvo. Kalyāṇamittatāti sucimittatā. Satthugāravoti satthari gāravayutto. Esa nayo sabbattha.

69. In the fifth, 'amenability' (sovacassatā) means the state of being easy to admonish. 'Good friendship' (kalyāṇamittatā) means having pure friends. 'Respect for the Teacher' (satthugāravo) means one who is endowed with respect for the Teacher. This is the method everywhere.

6. Samādhisuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Samādhi Sutta

70. Chaṭṭhe [M 3.0138][P 3.0411] na santenāti paccanīkakilesehi avūpasantena. Na paṇītenāti na atappakena. Na paṭippassaddhiladdhenāti kilesappaṭippassaddhiyā aladdhena appattena. Na ekodibhāvādhigatenāti na ekaggabhāvaṃ upagatena.

70. In the sixth, 'not by a peaceful one' (na santena) means not being calmed of opposing defilements. 'Not by a sublime one' (na paṇītena) means not being satisfying. 'Not by one who has obtained tranquility' (na paṭippassaddhiladdhena) means not having obtained the calming of defilements, not having reached it. 'Not by one who has attained unification' (na ekodibhāvādhigatena) means not having reached the state of one-pointedness.

7. Sakkhibhabbasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Sakkhibhabba Sutta

71. Sattame tatra tatrāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ visese. Sakkhibhabbatanti paccakkhabhāvaṃ. Āyataneti kāraṇe. Hānabhāgiyādayo visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.39) saṃvaṇṇitā. Asakkaccakārīti na sukatakārī, na ādarakārī. Asappāyakārīti na sappāyakārī, na upakārabhūtadhammakārī.

71. In the seventh, 'in each and every case' (tatra tatra) means in that and that particular state. 'Capability of realization' (sakkhibhabbatā) means the state of being directly experienced. 'As a basis' (āyatane) means as a cause. The sections on decline, etc., are explained in the Visuddhimagga. 'One who acts disrespectfully' (asakkaccakārī) means not one who acts well, not one who acts with respect. 'One who acts unsuitably' (asappāyakārī) means not one who acts suitably, not one who practices states that are beneficial.

8. Balasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Bala Sutta

72. Aṭṭhame [V 3.0140] balatanti balabhāvaṃ thāmabhāvaṃ. Asātaccakārīti na satatakārī. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayameva.

72. In the eighth, 'power' (balataṃ) means the state of power, the state of strength. 'One who does not act persistently' (asātaccakārī) means not one who acts constantly. The rest is according to the method already stated.

9-10. Tajjhānasuttadvayavaṇṇanā

9-10. Commentary on the Two Suttas on That Jhāna

73-74. Navame na yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭho hotīti vatthukāmakilesakāmesu ādīnavo na yathāsabhāvato jhānapaññāya sudiṭṭho hoti. Dasamaṃ uttānatthamevāti.

In the ninth, 'it is not well seen with right wisdom as it really is' (na yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭho hoti) means that the danger in sensual pleasures as objects and sensual pleasures as defilements is not well seen according to its true nature with the wisdom associated with jhāna. The tenth has a clear meaning.

Devatāvaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Deities is the seventh.

8. Arahattavaggo

8. The Chapter on Arahantship

1. Dukkhasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on Suffering

75. Aṭṭhamassa paṭhame savighātanti saupaghātaṃ sopaddavaṃ. Sapariḷāhanti kāyikacetasikena pariḷāhena sapariḷāhaṃ. Pāṭikaṅkhāti icchitabbā avassaṃbhāvinī.

75. In the first sutta of the eighth chapter, 'with distress' (savighātaṃ) means with affliction, with calamity. 'With anguish' (sapariḷāhaṃ) means with burning, that is, with bodily and mental burning. 'Is to be expected' (pāṭikaṅkhā) means it is to be expected, it is inevitable.

2. Arahattasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on Arahantship

76. Dutiye [M 3.0139][P 3.0412] mānanti jātiādīhi maññanaṃ. Omānanti hīnohamasmīti mānaṃ. Atimānanti atikkamitvā pavattaṃ accuṇṇatimānaṃ. Adhimānanti adhigatamānaṃ. Thambhanti kodhamānehi thaddhabhāvaṃ. Atinipātanti hīnassa hīnohamasmīti mānaṃ.

76. In the second sutta, 'conceit' (mānaṃ) means conceiving by way of birth and so on. 'Self-deprecation' (omānaṃ) means the conceit, 'I am inferior.' 'Arrogance' (atimānaṃ) means conceit that has occurred having surpassed, excessive conceit. 'Overestimation' (adhimānaṃ) means the conceit of attainment. 'Stubbornness' (thambhaṃ) means the state of being stubborn due to anger and conceit. 'Self-contempt' (atinipātaṃ) means, for an inferior person, the conceit, 'I am inferior.'

3. Uttarimanussadhammasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on Superhuman States

77. Tatiye [V 3.0141] uttarimanussadhammāti manussadhammato uttari. Alamariyañāṇadassanavisesanti ariyabhāvaṃ kātuṃ samatthaṃ ñāṇadassanavisesaṃ, cattāro magge cattāri ca phalānīti attho. Kuhananti tividhaṃ kuhanavatthuṃ. Lapananti lābhatthikatāya ukkhipitvā avakkhipitvā vā lapanaṃ.

77. In the third [sutta], `uttarimanussadhammā` means superior to the states of humans. `Alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ` means the special quality of knowledge and vision capable of bringing about the state of a noble one; this is the meaning: the four paths and the four fruits. `Kuhanaṃ` means the threefold basis of deceit. `Lapanaṃ` means speaking by either extolling or disparaging out of a desire for gain.

4. Sukhasomanassasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse on Happiness and Gladness

78. Catutthe yoni cassa āraddhā hotīti kāraṇañcassa paripuṇṇaṃ paggahitaṃ hoti. Dhammārāmoti dhamme ratiṃ vindati. Bhāvanāya ramati, bhāvento vā ramatīti bhāvanārāmo. Pahāne ramati, pajahanto vā ramatīti pahānārāmo. Tividhe paviveke ramatīti pavivekārāmo. Abyāpajjhe niddukkhabhāve ramatīti abyāpajjhārāmo. Nippapañcasaṅkhāte nibbāne ramatīti nippapañcārāmo.

78. In the fourth [sutta], `yoni cassa āraddhā hoti` means: for him the reason is fully and well undertaken. `Dhammārāmo` means: he finds delight in the Dhamma. `Bhāvanārāmo` means: he delights in development, or he delights while developing. `Pahānārāmo` means: he delights in abandoning, or he delights while abandoning. `Pavivekārāmo` means: he delights in the threefold seclusion. `Abyāpajjhārāmo` means: he delights in the state of non-affliction, of being without suffering. `Nippapañcārāmo` means: he delights in Nibbāna, which is designated as being without proliferation.

5. Adhigamasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse on Attainment

79. Pañcame na āyakusaloti na āgamanakusalo. Na apāyakusaloti na apagamanakusalo. Chandanti kattukamyatāchandaṃ. Na ārakkhatīti na rakkhati.

79. In the fifth [sutta], `na āyakusalo` means not skilled in the cause [of wholesome and unwholesome states]. `Na apāyakusalo` means not skilled in the cessation [of wholesome and unwholesome states]. `Chandaṃ` means the desire which is the wish to do. `Na ārakkhati` means does not guard.

6. Mahantattasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on Greatness

80. Chaṭṭhe ālokabahuloti ñāṇālokabahulo. Yogabahuloti yoge bahulaṃ karoti. Vedabahuloti pītipāmojjabahulo. Asantuṭṭhibahuloti [P 3.0413] kusaladhammesu asantuṭṭho. Anikkhittadhuroti aṭṭhapitadhuro paggahitavīriyo. Uttari ca patāretīti sampati ca uttariñca vīriyaṃ karoteva. Sattamaṃ uttānameva.

80. In the sixth [sutta], `ālokabahulo` means abounding in the light of wisdom. `Yogabahulo` means he does much in the way of exertion. `Vedabahulo` means abounding in rapture and joy. `Asantuṭṭhibahulo` means not content with wholesome states. `Anikkhittadhuro` means one who has not put down the burden, one with aroused energy. `Uttari ca patāreti` means he makes effort even further than his capacity. The seventh [sutta] is self-evident.

8-10. Dutiyanirayasuttādivaṇṇanā

8–10. Commentary on the Second Niraya Sutta and others.

82-84. Aṭṭhame [M 3.0140][V 3.0142] pagabbhoti kāyapāgabbhiyādīhi samannāgato. Navamaṃ uttānatthameva. Dasame vighātavāti mahicchataṃ nissāya uppannena lobhadukkhena dukkhito. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

In the eighth [sutta], `pagabbho` means endowed with bodily presumptuousness and so on. The ninth [sutta] is self-evident in meaning. In the tenth [sutta], `vighātavā` means afflicted with the suffering of greed born from great ambition. The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Arahattavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Arahantship Chapter, the Eighth.

9. Sītivaggo

9. The Coolness Chapter

1. Sītibhāvasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on the State of Coolness

85. Navamassa paṭhame sītibhāvanti sītalabhāvaṃ. Yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ niggaṇhitabbantiādīsu uddhaccasamaye cittaṃ samādhinā niggahetabbaṃ nāma, kosajjānupatitakāle vīriyena paggahetabbaṃ nāma, nirassādagatakāle samādhinā sampahaṃsitabbaṃ nāma, samappavattakāle bojjhaṅgupekkhāya ajjhupekkhitabbaṃ nāma.

85. In the first [sutta] of the ninth [chapter], `sītibhāvaṃ` means the state of being cool. Regarding `yasmiṃ samaye cittaṃ niggaṇhitabbaṃ` and so on: at a time of restlessness, the mind should be restrained by concentration; when fallen into laziness, it should be roused by energy; when it has reached a state of joylessness, it should be gladdened by concentration; when it is proceeding evenly, it should be regarded with the equanimity of an enlightenment factor.

2. Āvaraṇasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on Hindrances

86. Dutiye kammāvaraṇatāyāti pañcānantariyakammehi. Kilesāvaraṇatāyāti niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā. Vipākāvaraṇatāyāti akusalavipākapaṭisandhiyā vā kusalavipākehi ahetukapaṭisandhiyā vāti.

86. In the second [sutta], `kammāvaraṇatāya` refers to the five deeds with immediate retribution. `Kilesāvaraṇatāya` refers to fixed wrong view. `Vipākāvaraṇatāya` refers to rebirth that is an unwholesome result, or, in the case of a wholesome result, a rootless or two-rooted rebirth.

4-5. Sussūsatisuttādivaṇṇanā

4–5. Commentary on the Sussūsati Sutta and others.

88-89. Catutthe [V 3.0143] anatthanti avaḍḍhiṃ. Atthaṃ riñcatīti vaḍḍhiatthaṃ chaḍḍeti. Ananulomikāyāti [P 3.0414] sāsanassa ananulomikāya. Pañcame diṭṭhisampadanti sotāpattimaggaṃ.

In the fourth [sutta], `anatthaṃ` means decline. `Atthaṃ riñcati` means one discards the benefit that is increase. `Ananulomikāya` means unconducive to the Teaching. In the fifth [sutta], `diṭṭhisampadaṃ` means the path of stream-entry.

8-11. Abhabbaṭṭhānasuttacatukkavaṇṇanā

8–11. Commentary on the Quartet of Discourses on Impossible States

92-95. Aṭṭhame anāgamanīyaṃ vatthunti anupagantabbaṃ kāraṇaṃ, pañcannaṃ verānaṃ dvāsaṭṭhiyā ca diṭṭhigatānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Aṭṭhamaṃ bhavanti kāmāvacare aṭṭhamaṃ paṭisandhiṃ. Navame kotūhalamaṅgalenāti diṭṭhasutamutamaṅgalena[M 3.0141]. Dasame sayaṃkatantiādīni attadiṭṭhivasena vuttāni. Adhiccasamuppannanti ahetunibbattaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

In the eighth [sutta], `anāgamanīyaṃ vatthuṃ` means a reason not to be approached; this is a term for the five enmities and the sixty-two views. `Aṭṭhamaṃ bhavaṃ` refers to the eighth rebirth in the desire realm. In the ninth [sutta], `kotūhalamaṅgalena` refers to auspicious rites based on what is seen, heard, or sensed. In the tenth [sutta], `sayaṃkataṃ` and so on are stated with reference to the self-view. `Adhiccasamuppannaṃ` means produced without a cause. The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Sītivaggo navamo.

The Coolness Chapter, the Ninth.

10. Ānisaṃsavaggo

10. The Chapter on Benefits

1-2. Pātubhāvasuttādivaṇṇanā

1–2. Commentary on the Discourse on Appearance and others.

96-97. Dasamassa paṭhame ariyāyataneti majjhimadese. Indriyānanti manacchaṭṭhānaṃ. Dutiye saddhammaniyatoti sāsanasaddhamme niyato. Asādhāraṇenāti puthujjanehi asādhāraṇena.

In the first [sutta] of the tenth [chapter], `ariyāyatane` means the Middle Country. `Indriyānaṃ` means the six [faculties], with mind as the sixth. In the second [sutta], `saddhammaniyato` means fixed in the true Dhamma of the Dispensation. `Asādhāraṇena` means uncommon to ordinary people.

7. Anavatthitasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Discourse on the Unstable

102. Sattame anodhiṃ karitvāti “ettakāva saṅkhārā aniccā, na ito pare”ti evaṃ sīmaṃ mariyādaṃ akatvā. Anavatthitāti avatthitāya rahitā, bhijjamānāva hutvā upaṭṭhahissantīti [V 3.0144] attho. Sabbaloketi sakale tedhātuke. Sāmaññenāti [P 3.0415] samaṇabhāvena, ariyamaggenāti attho.

102. In the seventh [sutta], `anodhiṃ karitvā` means not setting a limit or boundary by thinking, 'Only this many formations are impermanent, not those beyond this.' `Anavatthitā` means devoid of stability; the meaning is that, being only in a state of perishing, they will not endure. `Sabbaloke` means in the entire threefold realm. `Sāmaññena` means by the state of a recluse; the meaning is, by the noble path.

8. Ukkhittāsikasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Discourse on the Upraised Sword

103. Aṭṭhame mettāvatāyāti mettāyuttāya pāricariyāya. Satta hi sekhā tathāgataṃ mettāvatāya paricaranti, khīṇāsavo pariciṇṇasatthuko.

103. In the eighth [sutta], `mettāvatāya` means with service endowed with loving-kindness. Indeed, the seven trainees attend to the Tathāgata with loving-kindness; the one whose taints are destroyed is one who has already served the Teacher.

9. Atammayasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Discourse on Not Being Made of That

104. Navame atammayoti tammayā vuccanti taṇhādiṭṭhiyo, tāhi rahito. Ahaṃkārāti ahaṃkāradiṭṭhi. Mamaṃkārāti mamaṃkārataṇhā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

104. In the ninth [sutta], regarding `atammayo`: craving and views are called `tammayā`; it means one is devoid of them. `Ahaṃkāra` is the view of 'I-making.' `Mamaṃkāra` is the craving of 'mine-making.' The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Ānisaṃsavaggo dasamo.

The Chapter on Benefits, the Tenth.

Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Second Fifty is concluded.

11. Tikavaggo

11. The Chapter of Threes

1. Rāgasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on Lust

107. Ekādasamassa [M 3.0142] paṭhame asubhāti asubhakammaṭṭhānaṃ. Mettāti mettākammaṭṭhānaṃ. Paññāti sahavipassanā maggapaññā.

107. In the first [sutta] of the eleventh [chapter], `asubhā` means the meditation subject of foulness. `Mettā` means the meditation subject of loving-kindness. `Paññā` means path-wisdom together with insight.

6. Assādasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Discourse on Gratification

112. Chaṭṭhe [V 3.0145] assādadiṭṭhīti sassatadiṭṭhi. Attānudiṭṭhīti attānaṃ anugatā vīsativatthukā sakkāyadiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhīti dvāsaṭṭhividhāpi diṭṭhi. Sammādiṭṭhīti maggasammādiṭṭhi, natthi dinnantiādikā vā micchādiṭṭhi, kammassakatañāṇaṃ sammādiṭṭhi.

112. In the sixth [sutta], `assādadiṭṭhi` is the eternalism view. `Attānudiṭṭhi` is the twenty-based identity view that follows the self. `Micchādiṭṭhi` is the sixty-two kinds of wrong view. `Sammādiṭṭhi` is path right view. Or alternatively, the view such as 'There is nothing in what is given,' etc., is wrong view, while the knowledge of ownership of kamma is right view.

7. Aratisuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Discourse on Discontent

113. Sattame adhammacariyāti dasa akusalakammapathā.

113. In the seventh [sutta], `adhammacariyā` means the ten unwholesome courses of action.

10. Uddhaccasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Discourse on Restlessness

116. Dasame asaṃvaroti anadhivāsakabhāvo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

116. In the tenth [sutta], `asaṃvaro` means the state of non-endurance. The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Tikavaggo ekādasamo.

The Eleventh Chapter.

12. Sāmaññavaggavaṇṇanā

12. Commentary on the Sāmañña Vagga

119-121. Ito [P 3.0416] paresu tapussoti dvevācikupāsako. Tathāgate niṭṭhaṅgatoti buddhaguṇesu patiṭṭhitacitto pahīnakaṅkho. Amataṃ addasāti amataddaso. Ariyenāti niddosena lokuttarasīlena. Ñāṇenāti paccavekkhaṇañāṇena. Vimuttiyāti sekhaphalavimuttiyā[M 3.0143]. Tavakaṇṇikoti evaṃnāmako gahapati. Tapakaṇṇikotipi pāḷi.

119-121. In the following sections, 'Tapussa' is a lay follower with two-phrased refuge. 'Gone to the goal in the Tathāgata' means one whose mind is established in the virtues of the Buddha, with doubt abandoned. Because 'he saw the Deathless,' he is a 'seer of the Deathless.' 'By the noble' means by faultless supramundane virtue. 'By knowledge' means by reviewing knowledge. 'By liberation' means by the fruition-liberation of a trainee. 'Tavakaṇṇika' is a householder of that name. 'Tapakaṇṇika' is also a Pāli reading.

24. Rāgapeyyālavaṇṇanā

24. Commentary on the Abbreviated Passage Beginning with Lust

140. Rāgassāti [V 3.0146] pañcakāmaguṇikarāgassa. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

140. Rāgassa means the lust associated with the five strands of sensual pleasure. The rest has a clear meaning everywhere.

Manorathapūraṇiyā aṅguttaranikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

In the Manorathapūraṇī, the Commentary on the Aṅguttara Nikāya:

Chakkanipātassa saṃvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Book of Sixes is concluded.

. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Aṅguttaranikāye

In the Aṅguttara Nikāya:

Sattakanipāta-aṭṭhakathā

Commentary on the Book of the Sevens

Paṇṇāsakaṃ

The Fifty

1. Dhanavaggo

1. The Chapter on Wealth

1-5. Paṭhamapiyasuttādivaṇṇanā

1-5. Commentary on the First Pīya Sutta and so forth

1-5. Sattakanipātassa [V 3.0147][M 3.0145][P 4.0001] paṭhame anavaññattikāmoti abhiññātabhāvakāmo. Tatiye yoniso vicine dhammanti upāyena catusaccadhammaṃ vicināti. Paññāyatthaṃ vipassatīti sahavipassanāya maggapaññāya saccadhammaṃ vipassati. Pajjotassevāti dīpasseva. Vimokkho hoti cetasoti tassa imehi balehi samannāgatassa khīṇāsavassa dīpanibbānaṃ viya carimakacittassa vatthārammaṇehi vimokkho hoti, gataṭṭhānaṃ na paññāyati. Catutthe saddho hotītiādīni pañcakanipāte vaṇṇitāneva. Pañcame dhanānīti adāliddiyakaraṇaṭṭhena dhanāni.

1-5. In the first of the Book of the Sevens, anavaññattikāmo means desiring the state of not being known by others. In the third, yoniso vicine dhammaṃ means one investigates the Dhamma of the Four Truths by means of a suitable method. Paññāya atthaṃ vipassati means one sees the Dhamma of the Truths with the wisdom of the path together with insight. Pajjotassa eva means 'of a lamp'. Vimokkho hoti cetaso means for that taint-destroyed one who is endowed with these powers, like the extinguishing of a lamp, there is liberation for the final consciousness from its bases and objects; its destination is not known. In the fourth, saddho hoti, and so on, have already been explained in the Book of Fives. In the fifth, dhanāni means wealth in the sense of not causing poverty.

7. Uggasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Ugga Sutta

7. Sattame [V 3.0148] uggo rājamahāmattoti pasenadikosalassa mahāamacco. Upasaṅkamīti bhuttapātarāso upasaṅkami. Aḍḍhoti nidhānagatena dhanena aḍḍho. Migāro [P 4.0002] rohaṇeyyoti rohaṇaseṭṭhino nattāraṃ migāraseṭṭhiṃ sandhāyevamāha. Mahaddhanoti vaḷañjanadhanena mahaddhano. Mahābhogoti upabhogaparibhogabhaṇḍassa mahantatāya mahābhogo. Hiraññassāti suvaṇṇasseva. Suvaṇṇāmeva hissa koṭisaṅkhyaṃ ahosi. Rūpiyassāti sesassa taṭṭakasarakaattharaṇapāvuraṇādino paribhogaparikkhārassa pamāṇasaṅkhāne vādoyeva natthi.

7. In the seventh, uggo rājamahāmatto (Ugga the royal minister) means the great minister of King Pasenadi of Kosala. Upasaṅkami (he approached) means he approached after having eaten his morning meal. Aḍḍho (wealthy) means wealthy with buried wealth. Migāro rohaṇeyyo (Migāra of Rohaṇa) was said in reference to Migāra the wealthy man, the grandson of Rohaṇa the wealthy man. Mahaddhano (of great wealth) means having great wealth in terms of wealth for daily use. Mahābhogo (of great possessions) means having great possessions due to the abundance of goods for use and enjoyment. Hiraññassāti means of gold itself; his gold alone amounted to a crore. Rūpiyassāti: of the remaining requisites for use—such as trays, bowls, floor-coverings, and cloaks—there is no way even to state the measure.

8. Saṃyojanasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Saṃyojana Sutta

8. Aṭṭhame [M 3.0146] anunayasaṃyojananti kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ. Sabbāneva cetāni bandhanaṭṭhena saṃyojanānīti veditabbāni. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭameva kathitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

8. In the eighth, anunayasaṃyojanaṃ (the fetter of attachment) means the fetter of sensual lust. And all these should be understood as 'fetters' in the sense of binding. In this sutta, only the round of existence is spoken of. The rest has a clear meaning everywhere.

Dhanavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Wealth.

2. The Chapter on Latent Dispositions.

3. Commentary on the Discourse on Families.

13. Dutiyassa tatiye nālanti na yuttaṃ nānucchavikaṃ. Na manāpenāti na manamhi appanakena ākārena nisinnāsanato paccuṭṭhenti, anādarameva dassenti. Santamassa pariguhantīti vijjamānampi deyyadhammaṃ etassa niguhanti paṭicchādenti. Asakkaccaṃ denti no sakkaccanti lūkhaṃ vā hotu paṇītaṃ vā, asahatthā acittīkārena denti, no cittīkārena.

13. In the third [sutta] of the second [vagga]: `nālaṃ` means not suitable, not appropriate. `Not in a pleasing manner` (na manāpena) means they do not rise from their seated position even with a slight gesture in the mind, showing only disrespect. `They conceal what he has` (santamassa pariguhanti) means they conceal or cover up a gift-worthy item even though it is present. `They give disrespectfully, not respectfully` (asakkaccaṃ denti no sakkaccaṃ) means whether it is coarse or excellent, they give it not with their own hand and without respect, not with respect.

4. Puggalasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse on Persons.

14. Catutthe [V 3.0149] ubhatobhāgavimuttoti dvīhi bhāgehi vimutto, arūpasamāpattiyā rūpakāyato vimutto, maggena nāmakāyato. So catunnaṃ arūpasamāpattīnaṃ ekekato vuṭṭhāya saṅkhāre sammasitvā [P 4.0003] arahattaṃ pattānaṃ catunnaṃ, nirodhā vuṭṭhāya arahattaṃ pattaanāgāmino ca vasena pañcavidho hoti. Pāḷi panettha “katamo ca puggalo ubhatobhāgavimutto? Idhekacco puggalo aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā hontī”ti (pu. pa. 208) evaṃ aṭṭhavimokkhalābhino vasena āgatā.

14. In the fourth [sutta]: `liberated in both ways` (ubhatobhāgavimutto) means liberated from two parts: liberated from the material body by means of the formless attainments, and from the mental body by means of the path. That person is of five kinds by way of: the four persons who, having emerged from each one of the four formless attainments and contemplated the conditioned phenomena, attain Arahantship; and the Non-returner who, having emerged from the attainment of cessation, attains Arahantship. Here, the Pāli text comes by way of one who has obtained the eight liberations: “And what kind of person is one liberated in both ways? Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations with the body, and his taints are destroyed through wisdom, having seen.”

Paññāya vimuttoti paññāvimutto. So sukkhavipassako, catūhi jhānehi vuṭṭhāya arahattaṃ pattā cattāro cāti imesaṃ vasena pañcavidho hoti. Pāḷi panettha aṭṭhavimokkhapaṭikkhepavaseneva āgatā. Yathāha – “na heva kho aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya [M 3.0147] cassa disvā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo paññāvimutto”ti.

`Liberated by wisdom` (paññāya vimutto) is one liberated by wisdom (paññāvimutto). He is of five kinds: the dry-insight practitioner, and the four types of persons who attain Arahantship after emerging from the four formless jhānas. Here, the Pāli text comes by way of the rejection of the eight liberations. As it is said: “Indeed, he does not dwell having touched the eight liberations with the body, but his taints are destroyed through wisdom, having seen. This person is called one liberated by wisdom.”

Phuṭṭhantaṃ sacchikatoti kāyasakkhī. So jhānaphassaṃ paṭhamaṃ phusati, pacchā nirodhaṃ nibbānaṃ sacchikaroti. So sotāpattiphalaṭṭhaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva arahattamaggaṭṭhā chabbidho hoti. Tenāha – “idhekacco puggalo aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati, paññāya cassa disvā ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo kāyasakkhī”ti (pu. pa. 208).

`He has directly realized the limit of what is touched` (phuṭṭhantaṃ sacchikato); therefore, he is a body-witness (kāyasakkhī). He first touches the contact of jhāna and afterwards directly realizes Nibbāna, which is cessation. He is of six kinds, beginning with one established in the fruit of stream-entry up to one established in the path of Arahantship. Therefore, it is said: “Here, a certain person dwells having touched the eight liberations with the body, and through wisdom, having seen, some of his taints are destroyed. This person is called a body-witness.”

Diṭṭhantaṃ pattoti diṭṭhippatto. Tatridaṃ saṅkhepalakkhaṇaṃ – dukkhā saṅkhārā, sukho nirodhoti ñātaṃ hoti diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phusitaṃ paññāyāti diṭṭhippatto. Vitthārato pana sopi kāyasakkhī viya chabbidho hoti. Tenevāha – “idhekacco puggalo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, tathāgatappaveditā cassa dhammā paññāya vodiṭṭhā honti vocaritā paññāya…pe… ayaṃ vuccati puggalo diṭṭhippatto”ti.

`He has attained the limit of what is seen` (diṭṭhantaṃ patto); therefore, he is one who has attained to view (diṭṭhippatto). In this regard, this is the concise characteristic: “Conditioned phenomena are suffering; cessation is bliss”—this having been known, seen, understood, directly realized, and touched by wisdom, he is therefore one who has attained to view. But in detail, he too is of six kinds, like the body-witness. Therefore it is said: “Here, a certain person understands as it actually is: ‘This is suffering’… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are well seen and well traversed by his wisdom… This person is called one who has attained to view.”

Saddhāya [V 3.0150][P 4.0004] vimuttoti saddhāvimutto. Sopi vuttanayeneva chabbidho hoti. Tenāha – “idhekacco puggalo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, tathāgatappaveditā cassa dhammā paññāya vodiṭṭhā honti vocaritā paññāya…pe… no ca kho yathādiṭṭhippattassa. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo saddhāvimutto”ti. Etassa hi saddhāvimuttassa pubbabhāgamaggakkhaṇe saddahantassa viya okappentassa viya adhimuccantassa viya ca kilesakkhayo hoti, diṭṭhippattassa pubbabhāgamaggakkhaṇe kilesacchedakañāṇaṃ adandhaṃ tikhiṇaṃ sūraṃ hutvā vahati. Tasmā yathā nāma nātitikhiṇena asinā kadaliṃ chindantassa chinnaṭṭhānaṃ maṭṭhaṃ na hoti, asi sīghaṃ na vahati, saddo suyyati, balavataro vāyāmo kātabbo hoti, evarūpā saddhāvimuttassa pubbabhāgamaggabhāvanā. Yathā pana sunisitena asinā kadaliṃ chindantassa chinnaṭṭhānaṃ maṭṭhaṃ hoti, asi sīghaṃ vahati, saddo na suyyati, balavavāyāmakiccaṃ [M 3.0148] na hoti, evarūpā paññāvimuttassa pubbabhāgamaggabhāvanā veditabbā.

`Liberated by faith` (saddhāya vimutto) is one liberated by faith (saddhāvimutto). He, too, is of six kinds in the way already stated. Therefore, it is said: “Here, a certain person understands as it really is, ‘This is suffering’… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are well seen and well traversed by his wisdom… but not like one who has attained to view. This person is called one liberated by faith.” For this person liberated by faith, at the moment of the preliminary-part path, the destruction of defilements occurs as if believing, as if accepting, as if resolving. But for one who has attained to view, at the moment of the preliminary-part path, the knowledge that cuts off defilements proceeds without delay, sharp, and valiant. Therefore, just as when cutting a banana trunk with a not-so-sharp sword the cut is not smooth, the sword does not move swiftly, a sound is heard, and a stronger effort must be made—such is the development of the preliminary-part path for the one liberated by faith. But just as when cutting a banana trunk with a well-sharpened sword the cut is smooth, the sword moves swiftly, no sound is heard, and no great effort is needed—such should the development of the preliminary-part path for the one liberated by wisdom be understood.

Dhammaṃ anussaratīti dhammānusārī. Dhammoti paññā, paññāpubbaṅgamaṃ maggaṃ bhāvetīti attho. Saddhānusārimhipi eseva nayo. Ubhopete sotāpattimaggaṭṭhāyeva. Vuttampi cetaṃ – “yassa [P 4.0005] puggalassa sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa paññindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti, paññāvāhiṃ paññāpubbaṅgamaṃ ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo dhammānusārī. Yassa puggalassa sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa saddhindriyaṃ adhimattaṃ hoti, saddhāvāhiṃ saddhāpubbaṅgamaṃ ariyamaggaṃ bhāveti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo saddhānusārī”ti (pu. pa. 208). Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthārato panesā ubhatobhāgavimuttādikathā visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.771, 889) paññābhāvanādhikāre vuttā. Tasmā tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbāti.

`He follows after the Dhamma` (dhammaṃ anussarati); therefore, he is a Dhamma-follower (dhammānusārī). Here, `Dhamma` means wisdom; the meaning is that one develops the path with wisdom as its forerunner. The same principle applies to the faith-follower (saddhānusārī). Both of these are established only in the path of stream-entry. It is also said: “For a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, when the faculty of wisdom is predominant, they develop the noble path that is led by wisdom and has wisdom as its forerunner. Such a person is called a Dhamma-follower. For a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, when the faculty of faith is predominant, they develop the noble path that is led by faith and has faith as its forerunner. Such a person is called a faith-follower.” This is the summary here. In detail, however, this discussion on the one liberated in both ways and so on is stated in the Visuddhimagga in the section on the development of wisdom. Therefore, it should be understood according to the method stated there.

5. Udakūpamāsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the Udakūpama Sutta

15. Pañcame udakūpamāti nimujjanādiākāraṃ gahetvā udakena upamitā. Sakiṃ nimuggoti ekavārameva nimuggo. Ekantakāḷakehīti niyatamicchādiṭṭhiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ummujjatīti uṭṭhahati. Sādhūti sobhanā bhaddakā. Hāyatiyevāti caṅkavāre āsittaudakaṃ viya parihāyateva[V 3.0151]. Ummujjitvā vipassati viloketīti uṭṭhahitvā gantabbadisaṃ vipassati viloketi. Pataratīti gantabbadisābhimukho tarati nāma. Paṭigādhappatto hotīti uṭṭhāya viloketvā pataritvā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne patiṭṭhāpatto nāma hoti, tiṭṭhati na punāgacchati. Tiṇṇo [P 4.0006] pāraṅgato thale tiṭṭhatīti sabbakilesoghaṃ taritvā paratīraṃ gantvā nibbānathale patiṭṭhito nāma hoti. Imasmiṃ sutte vaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ kathitaṃ.

5. In the fifth sutta, 'the simile of water' refers to individuals who are compared with water, taking into account the manner of sinking and so forth. 'Sinks once' means he sinks only one time. 'Utterly dark' is said in reference to fixed wrong view. 'Emerges' means he rises up. 'Excellent' means beautiful, good. 'Declines indeed' means he declines just like water poured on a straining cloth. 'Having emerged, he sees and observes' means having risen up, he sees and observes the direction to be gone to. 'He crosses over' means he crosses while facing the direction to be gone to. 'He gains a firm footing' means having risen up, observed, and crossed over, he is said to have reached a state of establishment in one place; he stands and does not return again. 'Having crossed over, gone beyond, he stands on dry ground' means having crossed the flood of all defilements and gone to the far shore, he is said to be established on the ground of Nibbāna. In this discourse, the cycle and the escape from the cycle are spoken of.

6. Aniccānupassīsuttavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Aniccānupassī Sutta

16. Chaṭṭhe aniccāti evaṃ paññāya pharanto anupassatīti aniccānupassī. Aniccāti evaṃ saññā assāti aniccasaññī. Aniccāti evaṃ ñāṇena paṭisaṃveditā assāti aniccapaṭisaṃvedī. Satatanti sabbakālaṃ. Samitanti yathā [M 3.0149] purimacittena pacchimacittaṃ samitaṃ samupagataṃ ghaṭṭitaṃ hoti, evaṃ. Abbokiṇṇanti nirantaraṃ aññena cetasā asaṃmissaṃ. Cetasā adhimuccamānoti cittena sanniṭṭhāpayamāno. Paññāya pariyogāhamānoti vipassanāñāṇena anupavisamāno.

15. In the sixth sutta, 'one who contemplates impermanence' contemplates, pervading with wisdom thus: 'impermanent.' 'One with the perception of impermanence' is one who has the perception thus: 'impermanent.' 'One who experiences impermanence' is one for whom there are things experienced with knowledge thus: 'impermanent.' 'Continuously' means at all times. 'Connected' means just as a subsequent thought is connected with, comes together with, and is joined to a preceding thought, so it is. 'Uninterruptedly' means without interval, unmixed with another thought. 'Resolving with the mind' means determining with the mind. 'Penetrating with wisdom' means entering with insight-knowledge.

Apubbaṃ acarimanti apure apacchā ekakkhaṇeyeva. Idha samasīsī kathito. So catubbidho hoti rogasamasīsī, vedanāsamasīsī, iriyāpathasamasīsī, jīvitasamasīsīti. Tattha yassa aññatarena rogena phuṭṭhassa sato rogavūpasamo ca āsavakkhayo ca ekappahāreneva hoti, ayaṃ rogasamasīsī nāma. Yassa pana aññataraṃ vedanaṃ vedayato vedanāvūpasamo ca āsavakkhayo ca ekappahāreneva hoti, ayaṃ vedanāsamasīsī nāma. Yassa pana ṭhānādīsu iriyāpathesu aññatarasamaṅgino vipassantassa iriyāpathassa pariyosānañca āsavakkhayo ca ekappahāreneva hoti, ayaṃ iriyāpathasamasīsī nāma. Yassa pana upakkamato vā sarasato vā jīvitapariyādānañca āsavakkhayo ca ekappahāreneva hoti, ayaṃ jīvitasamasīsī nāma. Ayamidha adhippeto. Tattha [P 4.0007] kiñcāpi āsavapariyādānaṃ maggacittena, jīvitapariyādānaṃ cuticittena hotīti ubhinnaṃ ekakkhaṇe sambhavo nāma natthi. Yasmā panassa āsavesu khīṇamattesu paccavekkhaṇavārānantarameva jīvitapariyādānaṃ gacchati, antaraṃ na paññāyati, tasmā evaṃ vuttaṃ.

6. 'Not before and not after' means neither earlier nor later, but in a single moment. Here, the 'samasīsī' person is spoken of. He is of four kinds: the disease-samasīsī, the feeling-samasīsī, the posture-samasīsī, and the life-samasīsī. Herein, for a person who is afflicted by some disease, when the pacification of the disease and the destruction of the taints occur in a single stroke, this person is called the disease-samasīsī. Furthermore, for a person experiencing some feeling, when the pacification of the feeling and the destruction of the taints occur in a single stroke, this person is called the feeling-samasīsī. Furthermore, for a person endowed with one of the postures such as standing and practicing insight, when the end of the posture and the destruction of the taints occur in a single stroke, this person is called the posture-samasīsī. Furthermore, for a person whose life is exhausted either through exertion or by its natural ending, when the exhaustion of life and the destruction of the taints occur in a single stroke, this person is called the life-samasīsī. This last one is what is intended here. Therein, although the exhaustion of the taints occurs with the path-consciousness and the exhaustion of life occurs with the death-consciousness, so there is indeed no possibility of both occurring in a single moment; nevertheless, because for this person, as soon as the taints are destroyed, the exhaustion of life occurs immediately after the turn of reviewing, and no interval is discerned, it is stated thus.

Antarāparinibbāyīti [V 3.0152] yo pañcasu suddhāvāsesu yattha katthaci uppanno nibbattakkhaṇe vā thokaṃ atikkamitvā vā vemajjhe ṭhatvā vā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Upahaccaparinibbāyīti yo tattheva āyuvemajjhaṃ atikkamitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti. Asaṅkhāraparinibbāyīti yo tesaṃyeva puggalānaṃ asaṅkhāreneva appayogena kilese khepeti. Sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyīti yo sasaṅkhārena sappayogena kilese khepeti. Uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti yo heṭṭhā catūsu suddhāvāsesu yattha katthaci nibbattitvā tato cuto anupubbena akaniṭṭhe uppajjitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti.

'One who attains parinibbāna in the interval' is the name for one who, having been reborn in any of the five Pure Abodes, attains Arahantship either at the moment of rebirth, or after a short time has passed, or while in the middle of the life-span. 'One who attains parinibbāna upon approach' is the name for one who, right there in that Pure Abode, having passed beyond the middle of the life-span, attains Arahantship. 'One who attains parinibbāna without exertion' is the name for one among those very persons who destroys the defilements without prompting and without effort. 'One who attains parinibbāna with exertion' is the name for one who destroys the defilements with prompting and with effort. 'One who goes upstream to Akaniṭṭha' is the name for one who, having been reborn in any of the four lower Pure Abodes, passes away from there and, being reborn successively, arises in the Akaniṭṭha realm and attains Arahantship.

7-9. Dukkhānupassīsuttādivaṇṇanā

7-9. Commentary on the Discourses on Contemplation of Suffering, etc.

17-19. Sattame [M 3.0150] dukkhānupassīti pīḷanākāraṃ dukkhato anupassanto. Aṭṭhame anattānupassīti avasavattanākāraṃ anattāti anupassanto. Navame sukhānupassīti sukhanti evaṃ ñāṇena anupassanto.

17-19. In the seventh discourse, 'one who contemplates suffering' means one who repeatedly contemplates the characteristic of oppression as suffering. In the eighth, 'one who contemplates non-self' means one who repeatedly contemplates the characteristic of not being subject to one's will as non-self. In the ninth, 'one who contemplates happiness' means one who repeatedly contemplates with knowledge thus: 'It is happiness'.

10. Niddasavatthusuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Discourse on the Grounds for Designation

20. Dasame niddasavatthūnīti niddasādivatthūni, “niddaso bhikkhu, nibbīso, nittiṃso, niccattālīso, nippaññāso”ti evaṃ vacanakāraṇāni. Ayaṃ kira pañho titthiyasamaye uppanno. Titthiyā hi dasavassakāle mataṃ nigaṇṭhaṃ niddasoti vadanti. So kira [P 4.0008] puna dasavasso na hoti. Na kevalañca dasavasso, navavassopi ekavassopi na hoti. Eteneva nayena vīsativassādikālepi mataṃ nigaṇṭhaṃ “nibbīso nittiṃso niccattālīso nippaññāso”ti vadanti. Āyasmā ānando gāme vicaranto taṃ kathaṃ sutvā vihāraṃ gantvā bhagavato ārocesi. Bhagavā āha – “na idaṃ, ānanda, titthiyānaṃ adhivacanaṃ, mama sāsane khīṇāsavassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Khīṇāsavo hi dasavassakāle parinibbuto puna dasavasso na hoti. Na kevalañca dasavassova, navavassopi…pe… ekavassopi. Na kevalañca ekavassova, ekādasamāsikopi…pe… ekamāsikopi ekamuhuttikopi na hotiyeva”. Kasmā? Puna paṭisandhiyā abhāvā. Nibbīsādīsupi eseva nayo. Iti bhagavā “mama sāsane [V 3.0153] khīṇāsavassetaṃ adhivacana”nti vatvā yehi kāraṇehi niddaso hoti, tāni dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

20. In the tenth discourse, 'grounds for designation' means the grounds for 'niddasa' (without ten), etc., such as, 'a monk is without ten, without twenty, without thirty, without forty, without fifty'—these are the reasons for such statements. This question, it is said, arose in the doctrine of the sectarians. For the sectarians declare a Nigaṇṭha who has died at the age of ten years as 'niddasa' (without ten). He, it is said, does not become ten years old again. Not only does he not become ten years old, he does not become nine years old or even one year old. In the same way, they declare a Nigaṇṭha who has died at the age of twenty years or more as 'nibbīsa' (without twenty), 'nittiṃsa' (without thirty), 'niccattālīsa' (without forty), 'nippaññāsa' (without fifty). The Venerable Ānanda, while wandering in the village, heard this talk and, upon returning to the monastery, reported it to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'This, Ānanda, is not a designation of the sectarians; in my dispensation, this is a designation of one whose taints are destroyed. For one whose taints are destroyed, having attained final Nibbāna at the age of ten years, does not become ten years old again. Not only does he not become ten years old, but not nine years old... not even one year old. Not only does he not become one year old, but not eleven months... not even one month, or even for one moment.' Why? Because there is no further relinking. The same method applies to 'nibbīsa', etc. Thus, the Blessed One, having said, 'In my dispensation, this is the designation of one whose taints are destroyed,' began this discourse to show the reasons why one is 'niddasa'.

Tattha idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane. Sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hotīti sikkhāttayapūraṇe balavacchando hoti. Āyatiñca sikkhāsamādāne avigatapemoti anāgate punadivasādīsupi sikkhāpūraṇe avigatapemeneva samannāgato hoti. Dhammanisantiyāti dhammanisāmanāya. Vipassanāyetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Icchāvinayeti taṇhāvinaye. Paṭisallāneti ekībhāve. Vīriyārambheti kāyikacetasikassa vīriyassa [M 3.0151] pūraṇe. Satinepakketi [P 4.0009] satiyañceva nipakabhāve. Diṭṭhipaṭivedheti maggadassane. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Therein, 'here' means in this dispensation. 'He has intense desire in undertaking the training' means he has a strong desire to fulfill the threefold training. 'And in the future, he has unfading affection in undertaking the training' means he is endowed with unfading affection for fulfilling the training also in the future, on subsequent days, etc. 'In reflection on the Dhamma' means in the investigation of the Dhamma. This is a designation for insight. 'In the removal of desire' means in the removal of craving. 'In seclusion' means in the state of being alone. 'In the undertaking of energy' means in the fulfilling of bodily and mental energy. 'In mindfulness and prudence' means in mindfulness and in wisdom. 'In the penetration of view' means in the seeing of the path. The rest is clear everywhere.

Anusayavaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on Latent Tendencies, the Second.

3. Vajjisattakavaggo

3. The Chapter of the Seven on the Vajjis

1. Sārandadasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sārandada Discourse

21. Tatiyassa paṭhame sārandade cetiyeti evaṃnāmake vihāre. Anuppanne kira tathāgate tattha sārandadassa yakkhassa nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ cetiyaṃ ahosi, athettha bhagavato vihāraṃ kāresuṃ. So sārandadacetiyaṃtveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Yāvakīvañcāti yattakaṃ kālaṃ. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipātāti divasassa tikkhattuṃ sannipatantāpi antarantarā sannipatantāpi abhiṇhaṃ sannipātāva. Sannipātabahulāti “hiyyopi purimadivasampi sannipatamha, puna ajja kimatthaṃ sannipatāmā”ti vosānamanāpajjanena sannipātabahulā. Vuddhiyeva licchavī vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā no parihānīti abhiṇhaṃ asannipatantā hi disāsu āgataṃ sāsanaṃ na suṇanti, tato “asukagāmasīmā vā nigamasīmā vā ākulā, asukaṭṭhāne corā pariyuṭṭhitā”ti na jānanti. Corāpi “pamattā rājāno”ti ñatvā gāmanigamādīni paharantā janapadaṃ nāsenti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ parihāni hoti[V 3.0154]. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipatantā pana taṃ pavattiṃ suṇanti, tato balaṃ pesetvā amittamaddanaṃ karonti. Corāpi “appamattā [P 4.0010] rājāno, na sakkā amhehi vaggabandhanena vicaritu”nti bhijjitvā palāyanti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ vuddhi hoti. Tena vuttaṃ – “vuddhiyeva licchavī vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā no parihānī”ti.

21. In the first discourse of the third chapter: 'at the Sārandada Cetiya' means in the monastery of that name. It is said that before the Tathāgata arose, there was a shrine at that place, the dwelling place of the yakkha Sārandada. Later, they built a monastery there for the Blessed One, and it became known as the Sārandada Cetiya. 'As long as' means for whatever length of time. 'Frequent assemblies' means that whether they assemble three times a day or from time to time, they are indeed frequent assemblers. 'Assembling often' means they assemble often without giving way to cessation, thinking, 'We assembled yesterday and the day before; for what purpose should we assemble again today?' 'For the Licchavis and Vajjis, only growth is to be expected, not decline.' Indeed, if they do not assemble frequently, they do not hear the news coming from the various regions. Consequently, they do not know: 'The border of such-and-such village or town is disturbed,' or 'Thieves have arisen in such-and-such a place.' The thieves, too, knowing, 'The kings are heedless,' attack villages, towns, and so on, destroying the country. In this way, the kings decline. But when they assemble frequently, they hear such news. Then, they send forces and crush their enemies. The thieves, too, realizing, 'The kings are vigilant; we cannot roam in gangs,' break up and flee. In this way, the kings prosper. Therefore, it was said: 'For the Licchavis and Vajjis, only growth is to be expected, not decline.'

Samaggātiādīsu sannipātabheriyā niggatāya “ajja me kiccaṃ atthi maṅgalaṃ atthī”ti vikkhepaṃ karontā na samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Bherisaddaṃ pana sutvāva bhuñjamānāpi alaṅkurumānāpi vatthāni nivāsayamānāpi addhabhuttā addhālaṅkatā vatthaṃ nivāsentāva sannipatantā samaggā sannipatanti nāma. Sannipatitā pana cintetvā mantetvā kattabbaṃ katvā ekatova avuṭṭhahantā na samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Evaṃ vuṭṭhitesu hi ye paṭhamaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ evaṃ hoti [M 3.0152] – “amhehi bāhirakathāva sutā, idāni vinicchayakathā bhavissatī”ti. Ekato vuṭṭhahantā pana samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Apica “asukaṭṭhāne gāmasīmā vā nigamasīmā vā ākulā, corā vā pariyuṭṭhitā”ti sutvā “ko gantvā amittamaddanaṃ karissatī”ti vutte “ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ ahaṃ paṭhama”nti vatvā gacchantāpi samaggā vuṭṭhahanti nāma. Ekassa pana kammante osīdamāne sesā puttabhātaro pesetvā tassa kammantaṃ upatthambhayamānāpi āgantukarājānaṃ “asukassa gehaṃ gacchatu, asukassa gehaṃ gacchatū”ti avatvā sabbe ekato saṅgaṇhantāpi ekassa maṅgale vā roge vā aññasmiṃ vā pana tādise sukhadukkhe uppanne sabbe tattha sahāyabhāvaṃ gacchantāpi samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karonti nāma.

Regarding 'in concord,' and so on: When the assembly drum is sounded, those who make excuses, saying, 'Today I have business; I have an auspicious ceremony,' are not said to assemble in concord. But those who, upon the very hearing of the drum's sound, assemble even while eating, while adorning themselves, or while dressing—coming half-eaten, half-adorned, and still in the act of dressing—are said to assemble in concord. Furthermore, having assembled, having deliberated, discussed, and done what should be done, if they do not rise up together, they are not said to depart in concord. For when they rise up in this way, those who leave first think: 'We have heard only the external talk; the discussion of the decision will happen now.' But those who rise up together are said to depart in concord. Moreover, having heard, 'In such-and-such a place, the village border or town border is disturbed, or thieves have arisen,' when it is asked, 'Who will go and subdue the enemy?' those who go, saying, 'I first! I first!' are also said to depart in concord. Furthermore, when one person's work is failing, the others send their sons and brothers to support his work; when a visiting king arrives, without saying, 'Let him go to so-and-so's house, let him go to so-and-so's house,' they all receive him together; and when for one person an auspicious event, sickness, or other such happiness or sorrow arises, they all go there to act as companions—in these ways, they are said to perform the duties of the Vajjis in concord.

Appaññattantiādīsu pubbe akataṃ suṅkaṃ vā baliṃ vā daṇḍaṃ vā āharāpentā appaññattaṃ paññāpenti nāma. Porāṇapaveṇiyā āgatameva pana anāharāpentā paññattaṃ samucchindanti [P 4.0011] nāma. Coroti gahetvā dassite avicinitvā chejjabhejjaṃ anusāsantā porāṇaṃ vajjidhammaṃ samādāya na vattanti nāma. Tesaṃ apaññattaṃ paññāpentānaṃ abhinavasuṅkādipīḷitā manussā “atiupaddutamha, ke imesaṃ vijite vasissantī”ti paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ hananti. Paññattaṃ samucchindantānaṃ paveṇiāgatāni suṅkādīni agaṇhantānaṃ koso parihāyati, tato hatthiassabalakāyaorodhādayo yathānibaddhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ alabhamānā thāmabalena parihāyanti. Te neva yuddhakkhamā honti na pāricariyakkhamā. Porāṇaṃ vajjidhammaṃ samādāya avattantānaṃ vijite manussā “amhākaṃ puttaṃ pitaraṃ bhātaraṃ acoraṃyeva coroti [V 3.0155] katvā chindiṃsu bhindiṃsū”ti kujjhitvā paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ hananti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ parihāni hoti. Apaññattaṃ na paññāpentānaṃ pana “paveṇiāgataṃyeva rājāno karontī”ti manussā haṭṭhatuṭṭhā kasivāṇijjādike kammante sampādenti. Paññattaṃ asamucchindantānaṃ paveṇiāgatāni suṅkādīni gaṇhantānaṃ koso vaḍḍhati, tato hatthiassabalakāyaorodhādayo yathānibaddhaṃ vaṭṭaṃ labhamānā thāmabalasampannā yuddhakkhamā ceva pāricariyakkhamā ca honti. Porāṇe vajjidhamme [M 3.0153] samādāya vattantānaṃ manussā na ujjhāyanti. “Rājāno porāṇapaveṇiyā karonti, aṭṭakulikasenāpatiuparājūhi parikkhitaṃ sayampi parikkhipitvā paveṇipotthakaṃ vācāpetvā anucchavikameva [P 4.0012] daṇḍaṃ pavattayanti, etesaṃ doso natthi, amhākaṃyeva doso”ti appamattā kammante karonti. Evaṃ rājūnaṃ vuddhi hoti.

Regarding 'what has not been enacted,' and so on: Those who introduce a toll, tax, or fine that was not previously made are said to enact what was not enacted. But those who fail to collect what has come down through ancient tradition are said to abolish what has been enacted. Those who, having arrested and presented someone as a thief, pronounce punishments of cutting and breaking without investigation, are said not to abide by and practice the ancient Vajjian law. For those who enact what was not enacted, the people, oppressed by new tolls and so on, think, 'We are greatly harassed! Who can live in their domain?' They enter the border regions, become thieves or their companions, and destroy the country. For those who abolish what has been enacted, by not collecting traditional tolls and so on, the treasury declines. Consequently, the elephant corps, cavalry, army, and harem, not receiving their established allowance, decline in strength and power. They become unfit for war and unfit for service. In the domain of those who do not abide by the ancient Vajjian law, the people grow angry, thinking, 'They took our son, father, or brother, who was not a thief, declared him a thief, and had him cut and broken!' They enter the border regions, become thieves or their companions, and destroy the country. In this way, the kings decline. But for those who do not enact what was not enacted, the people, joyful and delighted, think, 'The kings act only according to tradition!' and they successfully carry out their work in agriculture, trade, and so on. For those who do not abolish what has been enacted and collect the traditional tolls and so on, their treasury grows. Consequently, the elephant corps, cavalry, army, and harem, receiving their established allowance, become endowed with strength and power, fit for war and for service. For those who abide by the ancient Vajjian laws, the people do not find fault. They think, 'The kings act according to ancient tradition. They themselves uphold what was established by the eight clansmen, the general, and the viceroy; they have the book of tradition read and apply only a suitable punishment. There is no fault in them; the fault is ours alone.' Being vigilant, they carry out their work. In this way, the kings prosper.

Sakkarissantīti yaṃkiñci tesaṃ sakkāraṃ karontā sundarameva karissanti. Garuṃ karissantīti garubhāvaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā karissanti. Mānessantīti manena piyāyissanti. Pūjessantīti paccayapūjāya pūjessanti. Sotabbaṃ maññissantīti divasassa dve tayo vāre upaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā tesaṃ kathaṃ sotabbaṃ saddhātabbaṃ maññissanti. Tattha ye evaṃ mahallakānaṃ rājūnaṃ sakkārādīni na karonti, ovādatthāya vā nesaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ na gacchanti, te tehi vissaṭṭhā anovadiyamānā kīḷāpasutā rajjato parihāyanti. Ye pana tathā paṭipajjanti, tesaṃ mahallakarājāno “idaṃ kātabbaṃ idaṃ na kātabba”nti porāṇapaveṇiṃ ācikkhanti. Saṅgāmaṃ patvāpi “evaṃ pavisitabbaṃ, evaṃ nikkhamitabba”nti upāyaṃ dassenti. Te tehi ovadiyamānā yathāovādaṃ paṭipajjamānā sakkonti rajjapaveṇiṃ sandhāretuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – “vuddhiyeva licchavī vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.

They will honor them—whatever honor they show, they will do it well. They will respect them—they will establish a state of reverence and then act. They will esteem them—they will hold them dear in their hearts. They will venerate them—they will venerate them with offerings of requisites. They will consider them worth listening to—going to attend on them two or three times a day, they will consider their words worthy to be heard and believed. Here, those who do not show such honors to the elder kings, or who do not go to attend on them for advice, are abandoned by them. Unadvised, given to play, they decline from their rule. But for those who conduct themselves thus, the elder kings instruct them in the ancient tradition, saying, 'This should be done, this should not be done.' Even when they have reached the battlefield, they show them the strategy, saying, 'Enter like this, withdraw like this.' Being thus advised by them and practicing according to the advice, they are able to maintain the royal lineage. Therefore, it is said: 'Growth is indeed to be expected for the Licchavis of the Vajjis.'

Kulitthiyoti kulagharaṇiyo. Kulakumāriyoti anividdhā tāsaṃ dhītaro. Okassāti vā pasayhāti vā pasayhākārassevetaṃ nāmaṃ. Okāsātipi paṭhanti. Tattha [P 4.0013] okassāti avakasitvā ākaḍḍhitvā. Pasayhāti abhibhavitvā ajjhottharitvāti ayaṃ vacanattho. Evañhi karontānaṃ vijite manussā “amhākaṃ gehe puttabhātaropi, kheḷasiṅghānikādīni mukhena apanetvā saṃvaḍḍhitā dhītaropi ime balakkārena gahetvā attano ghare vāsentī”ti kupitā paccantaṃ pavisitvā corā vā corasahāyā vā hutvā janapadaṃ hananti. Evaṃ akarontānaṃ pana vijite [V 3.0156] manussā appossukkā sakāni kammāni karontā rājakosaṃ vaḍḍhenti. Evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.

'Women of good family' refers to matrons of the clan. 'Young girls of good family' refers to their virgin daughters. 'By dragging away' or 'by force'—these are names for an act of coercion. Some also read it as 'okāsā.' Therein, 'by dragging away' means having forcibly dragged them away. 'By force' means having overpowered and overwhelmed them—this is the meaning of the words. For when they act thus, people in their dominion become enraged, thinking, 'The mothers of our sons, and our daughters whom we raised by wiping away their spit and mucus with our mouths—these men take them by force and keep them in their own homes!' Entering the borderlands, they become thieves or allies of thieves and ravage the countryside. But when they do not act thus, people in their dominion, being untroubled, attend to their own work and enrich the royal treasury. Thus, in this matter, growth and decline should be understood.

Vajjīnaṃ [M 3.0154] vajjicetiyānīti vajjirājūnaṃ vajjiraṭṭhe cittīkataṭṭhena cetiyānīti laddhanāmāni yakkhaṭṭhānāni. Abbhantarānīti antonagare ṭhitāni. Bāhirānīti bahinagare ṭhitāni. Dinnapubbaṃ katapubbanti pubbe dinnañca katañca. No parihāpessantīti ahāpetvā yathāpavattameva karissanti. Dhammikaṃ baliṃ parihāpentānañhi devatā ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ na karonti, anuppannaṃ dukkhaṃ uppādetuṃ asakkontiyopi uppannaṃ kāsasīsarogādiṃ vaḍḍhenti, saṅgāme patte sahāyā na honti. Aparihāpentānaṃ pana ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ karonti, anuppannaṃ sukhaṃ uppādetuṃ asakkontiyopi uppannaṃ kāsasīsarogādiṃ haranti, saṅgāmasīse sahāyā hontīti. Evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.

'The Vajjian shrines of the Vajjis' refers to the places of yakkhas in the Vajjian country of the Vajjian kings, which have received the name 'cetiyas' because they are objects of veneration. 'Internal' means those situated inside the city. 'External' means those situated outside the city. 'What was formerly given and formerly done' means what was given and done in the past. 'They will not let it decline' means they will continue it just as it has been established, without diminishing it. For when people diminish the righteous offerings, the deities do not provide well-arranged protection. Even if unable to cause unarisen suffering to arise, they aggravate existing ailments such as coughs and head diseases, and they are not allies when battle is joined. But for those who do not diminish them, the deities provide well-arranged protection. Even if unable to cause unarisen happiness to arise, they remove existing ailments such as coughs and head diseases, and they are allies at the forefront of battle. Thus, in this matter, growth and decline should be understood.

Dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇaguttīti ettha rakkhā eva yathā anicchitaṃ nāgacchati, evaṃ āvaraṇato āvaraṇaṃ. Yathā icchitaṃ na nassati, evaṃ gopāyanato gutti. Tattha balakāyena parivāretvā rakkhanaṃ pabbajitānaṃ dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti nāma na hoti. Yathā pana vihārassa upavane rukkhe na chindanti, vājikā vājaṃ na [P 4.0014] karonti, pokkharaṇīsu macche na gaṇhanti, evaṃ karaṇaṃ dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti nāma. Kintīti kena nu kho kāraṇena.

Regarding 'righteous protection, shielding, and guarding': herein, protection (rakkhā) is called shielding (āvaraṇa) because it bars in such a way that the undesirable does not approach. It is called guarding (gutti) because it preserves in such a way that the desirable is not lost. In this context, providing protection for renunciates by surrounding them with an army is not called 'righteous protection, shielding, and guarding.' Rather, when people do not cut down trees in the monastery's nearby grove, when hunters do not engage in killing, and when they do not catch fish in the ponds—such action is called 'righteous protection, shielding, and guarding.' Why is that? For what reason?

Tattha ye anāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ āgamanaṃ na icchanti, te assaddhā honti appasannā. Pabbajite sampatte paccuggamanaṃ na karonti, gantvā na passanti, paṭisanthāraṃ na karonti, pañhaṃ na pucchanti, dhammaṃ na suṇanti, dānaṃ na denti, anumodanaṃ na suṇanti, nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ na saṃvidahanti. Atha nesaṃ avaṇṇo uggacchati “asuko nāma rājā assaddho appasanno, pabbajite sampatte paccuggamanaṃ na karoti…pe… nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ na saṃvidahatī”ti. Taṃ sutvā pabbajitā tassa nagaradvārena gacchantāpi nagaraṃ na pavisanti. Evaṃ anāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ anāgamanameva hoti. Āgatānaṃ pana phāsuvihāre asati yepi ajānitvā āgatā, te “vasissāmāti tāva cintetvā āgatamhā, imesaṃ pana rājūnaṃ iminā nīhārena ke vasissantī”ti nikkhamitvā gacchanti. Evaṃ anāgatesu anāgacchantesu āgatesu dukkhaṃ viharantesu so doso pabbajitānaṃ anāvāso hoti. Tato devatārakkhā na hoti, devatārakkhāya [V 3.0157] asati amanussā okāsaṃ [M 3.0155] labhanti, amanussā ussannā anuppannaṃ byādhiṃ uppādenti. Sīlavantānaṃ dassanapañhapucchanādivatthukassa puññassa anāgamo hoti. Vipariyāyena yathāvuttakaṇhapakkhaviparītassa sukkapakkhassa sambhavo hotīti evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.

Therein, those who do not desire the coming of arahants who have not yet come are faithless and without confidence. When renunciates arrive, they do not go out to meet them, do not go to visit them, do not exchange friendly greetings, do not ask questions, do not listen to the Dhamma, do not give alms, do not listen to the blessing, and do not arrange a dwelling place. Then, ill repute spreads about them: 'King so-and-so is faithless and without confidence; when renunciates arrive, he does not go out to meet them… he does not arrange a dwelling place.' Hearing this, renunciates, even when passing by the gate of that city, do not enter the city. Thus, it is simply the non-arrival of arahants who have not yet come. Furthermore, when there is no comfortable dwelling for those who have already arrived, even those who came without knowing this, think, 'We came intending to stay, but with these kings behaving in this manner, who would stay?' and so they depart and go elsewhere. Thus, with those who have not yet come not arriving, and with those who have arrived dwelling in discomfort, that place becomes uninhabitable for renunciates. Consequently, there is no protection from the deities; when there is no protection from the deities, non-human beings find an opportunity; when non-human beings are rampant, they cause unarisen diseases to arise. There is no arising of merit that is based on seeing virtuous ones, asking questions, and so forth. Conversely, the opposite occurs: the bright side, which is the reverse of the dark side just described, comes to be. Thus, in this matter, growth and decline should be understood.

2. Vassakārasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Vassakāra Sutta

22. Dutiye abhiyātukāmoti abhibhavanatthāya yātukāmo. Vajjīti vajjirājāno. Evaṃmahiddhiketi evaṃ mahatiyā rājiddhiyā samannāgate. Etena nesaṃ samaggabhāvaṃ katheti. Evaṃmahānubhāveti evaṃ mahantena rājānubhāvena samannāgate[P 4.0015]. Etena nesaṃ hatthisippādīsu katasikkhataṃ katheti, yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “sikkhitā vatime licchavikumārakā, susikkhitā vatime licchavikumārakā, yatra hi nāma sukhumena tāḷacchiggaḷena asanaṃ atipātayissanti poṅkhānupoṅkhaṃ avirādhita”nti (saṃ. ni. 5.1115). Ucchecchāmīti ucchindissāmi. Vināsessāmīti adassanaṃ nayissāmi. Anayabyasananti avaḍḍhiñceva, ñātibyasanañca. Āpādessāmīti pāpayissāmi.

22. In the second sutta, 'wishing to attack' (abhiyātukāmo) means desiring to go in order to subdue. 'The Vajjis' (Vajjī) means the Vajjian kings. 'Of such great power' (evaṃmahiddhike) means endowed with such great royal power. By this, he speaks of their state of unity. 'Of such great influence' (evaṃmahānubhāve) means endowed with such great royal influence. By this, he speaks of their state of having completed training in the elephant art and so on, in reference to which it was said: 'These Licchavi princes are so trained, so well-trained, that they can shoot an arrow through a subtle keyhole, shaft after shaft, without missing.' 'I will uproot' (ucchejjāmi) means I will cut them off. 'I will annihilate' (vināsessāmi) means I will bring them to disappearance. 'Ruin and downfall' (anayabyasanaṃ) means both non-prosperity and the destruction of relatives. 'I will bring upon them' (āpādessāmi) means I will cause them to arrive at this.

Iti kira so ṭhānanisajjādīsu imaṃ yuddhakathameva katheti, “gamanasajjā hothā”ti ca balakāyaṃ āṇāpeti. Kasmā? Gaṅgāya kira ekaṃ paṭṭanagāmaṃ nissāya addhayojanaṃ ajātasattuno vijitaṃ, addhayojanaṃ licchavīnaṃ. Tatra pabbatapādato mahagghabhaṇḍaṃ otarati. Taṃ sutvā “ajja yāmi, sve yāmī”ti ajātasattuno saṃvidahantasseva licchavino samaggā sammodamānā puretaraṃ āgantvā sabbaṃ gaṇhanti. Ajātasattu pacchā āgantvā taṃ pavattiṃ ñatvā kujjhitvā gacchati. Te punasaṃvaccharepi tatheva karonti. Atha so balavāghātajāto, tadā evamakāsi.

Thus, it is said, in standing, sitting, and so forth, he spoke only of this talk of war, and he commanded his army, 'Be ready for departure!' Why? It is said that, based at a port village on the Ganges, half a yojana was Ajātasattu’s dominion, and half a yojana was the Licchavis’. There, valuable goods would descend from the foot of the mountain. Having heard of this, while Ajātasattu was still making arrangements, thinking, 'I will go today, I will go tomorrow,' the Licchavis, united and rejoicing in harmony, would arrive first and seize everything. Ajātasattu, arriving later and learning of that event, would go away in anger. They would do the same thing again in the following years. Then, with strong enmity having arisen in him, he acted thus at that time.

Tato cintesi – “gaṇena saddhiṃ yuddhaṃ nāma bhāriyaṃ, ekopi moghappahāro nāma natthi. Ekena kho pana paṇḍitena saddhiṃ mantetvā karonto niraparādho hoti, paṇḍito ca satthārā sadiso natthi, satthā ca avidūre dhuravihāre vasati, handāhaṃ pesetvā pucchāmi. Sace me gatena [M 3.0156] koci attho bhavissati, satthā tuṇhī bhavissati. Anatthe pana sati [P 4.0016] ‘kiṃ rañño tattha [V 3.0158] gatenā’ti vakkhatī”ti. So vassakāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pesesi. Brāhmaṇo gantvā bhagavato tamatthaṃ ārocesi. Tena vuttaṃ – atha kho rājā…pe… āpādessāmi vajjīti.

Then he thought: 'War with a group is indeed burdensome, and not a single blow is futile. However, one who acts after consulting with a wise person is blameless, and there is no wise person equal to the Teacher. The Teacher dwells not far away in the chief monastery. Well now, I shall send someone and ask. If there is some benefit for me in going, the Teacher will remain silent. But if there is disadvantage, he will say, "What is to be gained by the king going there?"' So he sent the brahmin Vassakāra. The brahmin went and reported that matter to the Blessed One. Therefore, it was said: 'Then the king… I will bring the Vajjis to ruin.'

Bhagavantaṃ bījayamānoti thero vattasīse ṭhatvā bhagavantaṃ bījati, bhagavato pana sītaṃ vā uṇhaṃ vā natthi. Bhagavā brāhmaṇassa vacanaṃ sutvā tena saddhiṃ amantetvā therena saddhiṃ mantetukāmo kinti te, ānanda, sutantiādimāha. Taṃ vuttatthameva.

Regarding 'fanning the Blessed One' (Bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno), the Elder, standing in the performance of his duties, fanned the Blessed One; but for the Blessed One, there is neither cold nor heat. The Blessed One, having heard the brahmin’s words, did not consult with him, but wishing to consult with the Elder, said the words beginning with, 'What have you heard, Ānanda?' That has the meaning already stated.

Ekamidāhanti idaṃ bhagavā pubbe vajjīnaṃ imassa vajjisattakassa desitabhāvappakāsanatthaṃ āha. Akaraṇīyāti akattabbā, aggahetabbāti attho. Yadidanti nipātamattaṃ. Yuddhassāti karaṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ, abhimukhaṃ yuddhena gahetuṃ na sakkāti attho. Aññatra upalāpanāyāti ṭhapetvā upalāpanaṃ. Upalāpanā nāma “alaṃ vivādena, idāni samaggā homā”ti hatthiassarathahiraññasuvaṇṇādīni pesetvā saṅgahakaraṇaṃ, evañhi saṅgahaṃ katvā kevalaṃ vissāsena sakkā gaṇhitunti attho. Aññatra mithubhedāti ṭhapetvā mithubhedaṃ. Iminā “aññamaññabhedaṃ katvāpi sakkā ete gahetu”nti dasseti. Idaṃ brāhmaṇo bhagavato kathāya nayaṃ labhitvā āha. Kiṃ pana bhagavā brāhmaṇassa imāya kathāya nayalābhaṃ jānātīti? Āma jānāti. Jānanto kasmā kathesi? Anukampāya. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – “mayā akathitepi katipāhena gantvā sabbe gaṇhissati, kathite pana samagge bhindanto tīhi saṃvaccharehi gaṇhissati. Ettakampi jīvitameva varaṃ. Ettakañhi jīvantā attano patiṭṭhābhūtaṃ puññaṃ karissantī”ti. Abhinanditvāti [P 4.0017] cittena nanditvā. Anumoditvāti “yāva subhāsitamidaṃ bhotā gotamenā”ti vācāya anumoditvā. Pakkāmīti rañño santikaṃ gato. Rājāpi tameva pesetvā sabbe bhinditvā gantvā anayabyasanaṃ pāpesi.

Regarding 'this one thing' (ekamidāhaṃ), the Blessed One said this to make it known that he had previously taught this heptad of principles to the Vajjis. 'Not to be overcome' (akaraṇīyā) means not to be acted against, not to be seized; this is the meaning. 'That is' (yadidaṃ) is merely a particle. 'By war' (yuddhassa) is the genitive case in the instrumental sense; the meaning is that they cannot be seized by direct warfare. 'Except by cajolery' (aññatra upalāpanāya) means setting aside cajolery. Cajolery means the act of support by sending elephants, horses, chariots, gold, silver, and so on, saying, 'Enough with strife, let us now be united.' The meaning is that, having supported them in this way, they can be seized through mere trust. 'Except by creating dissension' (aññatra mithubhedā) means setting aside mutual division. By this, it shows: 'Even by creating mutual division, it is possible to seize them.' The brahmin said this, having grasped the method from the Blessed One’s talk. But did the Blessed One know that the brahmin would grasp the method from this talk? Yes, he knew. Knowing, why did he speak? Out of compassion. It is said that he thought thus: 'If I do not speak, he will go and seize them all in a few days. But if I speak, by causing division among the united, he will seize them in three years. Even that much life is excellent. For, living that long, they will perform merit that will be a foundation for themselves.' 'Having delighted' (abhinanditvā) means being pleased in mind. 'Having approved' (anumoditvā) means rejoicing with speech, saying, 'How well-spoken this is by the good Gotama.' 'He departed' (pakkāmi) means he went to the king’s presence. The king, too, sent that very person, and after causing division among them all, he went and brought them to ruin and disaster.

3. Paṭhamasattakasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the First Sutta of the Heptad

23. Tatiye abhiṇhaṃ sannipātāti idaṃ vajjisattake vuttasadisameva. Idhāpi ca abhiṇhaṃ asannipatantā disāsu āgatasāsanaṃ na suṇanti, tato [M 3.0157] “asukavihārasīmā ākulā, uposathappavāraṇā ṭhitā, asukasmiṃ ṭhāne bhikkhū vejjakammadūtakammādīni karonti, viññattibahulā phalapupphadānādīhi jīvikaṃ kappentī”tiādīni na jānanti. Pāpabhikkhūpi “pamatto [V 3.0159] saṅgho”ti ñatvā rāsibhūtā sāsanaṃ osakkāpenti. Abhiṇhaṃ sannipatantā pana taṃ pavattiṃ suṇanti, tato bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pesetvā sīmaṃ ujuṃ kārenti, uposathappavāraṇāyo pavattāpenti, micchājīvānaṃ ussannaṭṭhāne ariyavaṃsike pesetvā ariyavaṃsaṃ kathāpenti, pāpabhikkhūnaṃ vinayadharehi niggahaṃ kārāpenti. Pāpabhikkhūpi “appamatto saṅgho, na sakkā amhehi vaggabandhanena vicaritu”nti bhijjitvā palāyanti. Evamettha vuddhihāniyo veditabbā.

3. In the third sutta, the phrase 'frequent assemblies' is just as was stated in the Vajjisattaka. Here too, not assembling frequently, they do not hear the news that has come from the various regions. Consequently, they do not know of such matters as: 'The boundary of such-and-such monastery is disturbed; the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā ceremonies are suspended; in such-and-such a place, monks perform medical practice, messenger duties, and so on; being full of solicitations, they make a living by giving fruits, flowers, and the like.' The evil monks, too, knowing, 'The Saṅgha is heedless,' form a faction and cause the Dispensation to decline. However, by assembling frequently, they hear of such occurrences.
